# Changelog (/docs/changelog)

Notable changes to the Visuno component library and these docs, newest first.
Component source lives in the [components repository](https://github.com/Visuno/components).

## Unreleased [#unreleased]

- **Status pill** — now stays on one line and keeps its action button visible in narrow containers. Before, a tight space clipped the button off the end; now the label truncates first, then the meta/file chip, while the glyph and button never shrink. Fixed across React, Angular and Flutter.

- **Loaders render as true circles again** — the Angular test-bench base stylesheet was missing the "keep round" overrides, so round elements (the **radar** and **ring** step-loaders, dots, avatars, pulses) rendered as squircles under the global squircle corner shape. Restored, so they're proper circles.

- **React ≡ Angular parity** — the cross-framework parity suite now covers **every** shipped component (previously five), with a coverage gate that fails CI if a component ships without a spec. Bringing the whole library under test surfaced and fixed a batch of real Angular drift: `account-table` and `task-table` rendered unprefixed classes so none of the shared styles applied; many components dropped the `vo-sw`/`vo-enter` motion classes or the right icon glyph; and the reduced-motion service reported the wrong value on first read (so animations that should have been instant for people who prefer reduced motion weren't). The components now render the same structure, styles and API surface across both frameworks.

- **Angular build fix** — `@visuno/angular` and the Angular test bench no longer fail to compile: the agent run timeline dropped its `@angular/platform-browser` dependency (it rendered brand logos through `DomSanitizer`, which also broke strict builds) and now renders them directly.

- **Date picker, Event calendar & Agenda** — three new **Dates** components with live docs pages. The **date picker** opens a calendar with quick picks and a box that understands "next friday", and in `range` mode becomes a two-month range picker with ready-made ranges and Apply. The **event calendar** shows a work week you can add to and open for details, with an agent that finds a free slot and suggests it. The **agenda** lists today's schedule with a live now line and the notes an agent prepared for each event. (React and docs land now; Angular and Flutter to follow.)

- **Segmented control** — the docs example and the Angular/Flutter test benches now show a real "Pricing launch" planner: picking Day, Week or Month switches the panel below between a day agenda, a week list and a month grid, with Today and prev/next steppers. The previous demo had a dead radio group that drove nothing, so clicking appeared to do nothing — now every pick visibly changes the panel.

- **Angular demos** — restored the React demos’ interactive state updates, streamed stories, retries, approvals, replay controls, and reduced-motion behavior. Added missing controlled inputs and copy/disabled button support in the Angular library.

- **Angular** — component selectors now use PascalCase that mirrors the React component names (`<vo-status-pill>` → `<StatusPill>`, `<vo-icon>` → `<Icon>`, `<vo-agent-tree>` → `<AgentTree>`, …). The three selectors that shadowed native HTML elements are prefixed to stay unambiguous: `<VoButton>`, `<VoButtonCopy>`, `<VoProgress>`. The `voGridItem` / `vo-field-zone` directives become `gridItem` / `fieldZone`. The shared `--vo-*` design tokens and `vo-*` CSS classes are unchanged. **Breaking:** update Angular templates to the new tag names.

- **Docs** — a global site footer now appears on every page (MIT licence, Star on GitHub, a link to the machine-readable **llms.txt**, Imprint, and "Powered by SDK Industries"), plus a floating **back-to-top** button that fades in once you scroll.

- **Angular Stat cards** — adapt columns and spacing to the component width so cards fit narrow panels as well as mobile screens.

- **Angular Code viewer** — removed oversized gaps between code lines while preserving code indentation and blank lines.

- **Angular test bench** — added the missing Number field, OTP field, Search input, and Slider examples with interactive states.

- **Docs** — new getting-started guides: **Installation** (per-framework setup), **Theming** (the two switches and the `--vo-*` token system, with per-framework code tabs), **Accessibility** (semantics, keyboard, focus, reduced motion), and **Using with AI** (point a coding assistant at the `llms.txt` docs). Grouped under a collapsible **Docs** section in the sidebar, and every nav entry now carries a Visuno icon.

- **Angular** — use the same shared web styles as React for consistent typography, controls, icons, and Soft/Blueprint themes.

- **Slider** — new shared component in all four frameworks: a track with a
  single value or a range, optional discrete steps and named stops, and an
  agent-recommended value marked on the track. Keyboard and drag, tokens only.
- **Search input** — new shared component in all four frameworks: a search
  field with scoped filters, recent queries and an inline agent answer.
- **Number field** — new shared component in all four frameworks: type a number
  or step it with minus and plus, with units, limits, and a note when a value is
  clamped to fit.
- **OTP field** — new shared component in all four frameworks: a one-time code,
  one box per digit, that auto-advances, navigates by keyboard and fills from a
  paste.
- **Docs preview** — live example stages now always use the docs page's own theme
  (light or dark), never the browser's colour-scheme preference. The per-preview
  Light/Dark toggle has been removed; the component tokens follow the site theme.
- **Icon** — new shared component in all four frameworks: one line icon from a shared
  MIT set of ~5,200, or your own SVG. Colour follows `currentColor` so icons theme for
  free; sizes run `xs`–`xl` on a 24×24 grid. Any name resolves on the web; Angular and
  Flutter draw names outside the compiled core set, and custom glyphs, from a `path`.
  The whole set now uses canonical, descriptive names (`chevron-right`, `circle-check`,
  `terminal-2`…) across every framework.
- **Packages** — the library now publishes as installable packages: `@visuno/react` and
  `@visuno/angular` on npm, and `visuno` on pub.dev for Flutter. Each is released from its
  framework directory in the components repo.
- **Vanilla JS dropped** — Visuno is now **three frameworks**: React, Angular and Flutter.
  The Vanilla JS tabs have been removed from every component page, and the docs, FAQ and
  roadmap updated to match. React is now the reference implementation.
- **Landing page** — the home page now showcases the **whole library** live: every
  shipped component appears as a running preview card, grouped by category, with the
  component count derived from the list. New marketing hero leading with the Visuno
  name, a secondary "Star on GitHub" action, and feature pills.
- **Frameworks slider** — the frameworks strip is now an auto-scrolling black & white
  logo slider covering React, Angular, Flutter and the React
  meta-frameworks it works with (Next.js, Remix, Gatsby, Astro).
- **Modal** — new shared component in all three frameworks: a centred dialog over a
  dimmed backdrop, closed by the backdrop, a button or Escape, with focus and page
  scroll kept in check. It carries the active style and theme to its portal, so it
  matches the surrounding components (rounded in Soft, correct light/dark).
- **Run summary** — the "Run details" and "Open changes" buttons now work: Run
  details opens a Modal with the run's stats, Open changes opens a full diff view.
- **Thinking states** — four new indicators: Pulse, Wave, Bounce and Spiral.
- **Run cost** — the spend bar now glides with the number instead of stalling.
- **Toast** — a dismissed toast can be shown again straight after.
- **Imprint page** added with the legal information of SDK Industries, linked from
  the docs navigation and the homepage footer.
- **Stat cards** homepage preview reworked into a responsive single-column layout.

## 2026-11-07 [#2026-11-07]

- **16 Conversation components** documented: live answer, thread panel, composer,
  model picker, voice capture, voice orb, tool call, artifact card, image generation,
  rich text editor, prompt starters, prompt library, attachment tray, response versions,
  answer action bar, and feedback sheet.

## 2026-11-06 [#2026-11-06]

- **7 Agent status components** documented, including status pill, thinking, reasoning
  trail, agent phases, step loader, action log, and context meter.
- Docs landing page **redesigned** — a quieter hero with live, self-animating component
  previews and the full library advertised as preview cards.
- Component documentation updated and **sections reorganised** for clarity (Agent status,
  Conversation, Charts and tables, Dates, Forms and inputs).
- Light wordmark asset added so the logo reads correctly in dark mode.
- **GitHub Pages** deployment enabled, with the private components repository read through
  a GitHub App token in CI.
- Initial commit — docs site scaffolded on Next.js and Fumadocs.


# Account table (/docs/components/account-table)

Customer accounts you can search and filter by plan. Each row shows the logo, plan tag, seats, a
health bar and the MRR; click a row and it opens to the note the agent left — with an optional
action button (like **Draft email**) that spins until its promise settles, then shows its done
label. The rows stagger in again whenever the search or the filter changes.

<Preview>
  <AccountTableExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { AccountTable, type AccountTableAccount } from './account-table/AccountTable';

const accounts: AccountTableAccount[] = [
  { name: 'Northwind', color: 'var(--vo-av-b)', plan: 'Enterprise', seats: 120, health: 92, mrr: '$14,400', note: 'Expanding. Design team added 18 seats this month.' },
  { name: 'Lumen Labs', color: 'var(--vo-av-l)', plan: 'Pro', seats: 14, health: 48, mrr: '$672', note: 'Usage fell 40% after their lead designer left.' },
];

<AccountTable
  accounts={accounts}
  action={{ label: 'Draft email', doneLabel: 'Draft ready', onClick: () => draft() }}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [AccountTableComponent] -->
accounts: AccountTableAccount[] = [
  { name: 'Northwind', color: 'var(--vo-av-b)', plan: 'Enterprise', seats: 120, health: 92, mrr: '$14,400', note: 'Expanding. Design team added 18 seats this month.' },
  { name: 'Lumen Labs', color: 'var(--vo-av-l)', plan: 'Pro', seats: 14, health: 48, mrr: '$672', note: 'Usage fell 40% after their lead designer left.' },
];
action: AccountTableAction = { label: 'Draft email', doneLabel: 'Draft ready', onClick: () => this.draft() };

<AccountTable [accounts]="accounts" [action]="action" (openChange)="onOpen($event)" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/account_table.dart';

AccountTable(
  accounts: const [
    AccountTableAccount(name: 'Northwind', color: Color(0xFF4890FA), plan: 'Enterprise', seats: 120, health: 92, mrr: r'$14,400', note: 'Expanding. Design team added 18 seats this month.'),
    AccountTableAccount(name: 'Lumen Labs', color: Color(0xFF9776FA), plan: 'Pro', seats: 14, health: 48, mrr: r'$672', note: 'Usage fell 40% after their lead designer left.'),
  ],
  action: AccountTableAction(
    label: 'Draft email',
    doneLabel: 'Draft ready',
    onClick: (a) => Future.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 800)),
  ),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accounts` | `AccountTableAccount[]` | The account rows. Each has `name`, `color`, `plan`, `seats`, `health` (0–100), `mrr` and an optional `note`. |
| `plans` | `string[]` | The plan filters after All. Defaults to the plans in `accounts`, in first-seen order. |
| `planTones` | `Record<string, Tone>` | The tag colour per plan. Defaults to Enterprise purple, Pro blue, Team teal. |
| `plan` / `defaultPlan` | `string` | The active plan filter, or `''` for All. |
| `onPlanChange` | `(plan) => void` | Called when a filter chip is picked. |
| `query` / `defaultQuery` | `string` | The search text. Matches account names. |
| `onQueryChange` | `(query) => void` | Called as the search text changes. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `string \| null` | The account whose row is open, or `null`. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(name) => void` | Called when a row opens or closes. |
| `action` | `{ label; doneLabel?; onClick }` | A button in the open row's note. Return a promise and it spins until it settles, then shows `doneLabel`. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | The search field's placeholder. Defaults to `Search accounts`. |
| `emptyLabel` | `string` | Shown when nothing matches the search and filter. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The plan
tags run a little brighter than the shared tones — each plan takes its own saturated tint (blue,
purple, teal and so on), and the health bar fills green from 80, amber from 60 and red below, all
from the theme tokens. In Soft the panel, chips and tags are rounder.


# Action log (/docs/components/action-log)

An action log is a streaming list of what the agent does: each read, search, edit or command
lands as a row, running with a spinner, then done with a check and the time it took. A row with
output opens to show it, like a diff or test run. The header shows a spinner while the run is live
and a green dot once it finishes.

<Preview>
  <ActionLogExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ActionLog } from './action-log/ActionLog';

<ActionLog
  title="Agent activity"
  running
  actions={[
    { icon: 'file-text', title: <>Read <code>Pricing.tsx</code></>, detail: 'src/pages, 212 lines', state: 'done', time: '0.4s' },
    { icon: 'term', title: <>Ran <code>npm test</code></>, detail: '24 tests passed', state: 'running' },
  ]}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ActionLogComponent] -->
<ActionLog
  title="Agent activity"
  [running]="true"
  [actions]="actions"
></ActionLog>

// actions: Action[] = [
//   { icon: 'file-text', title: 'Read <code>Pricing.tsx</code>', detail: 'src/pages, 212 lines', state: 'done', time: '0.4s' },
//   { icon: 'term', title: 'Ran <code>npm test</code>', detail: '24 tests passed', state: 'running' },
// ];
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/action_log.dart';

ActionLog(
  running: true,
  actions: const [
    Action(icon: Icons.description_outlined, title: 'Read Pricing.tsx', detail: 'src/pages, 212 lines', state: ActionState.done, time: '0.4s'),
    Action(icon: Icons.terminal, title: 'Ran npm test', detail: '24 tests passed', state: ActionState.running),
  ],
)
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `Action[]` | The tool calls, newest at the end. Each has an `icon`, a `title`, an optional `detail`, a `state` of running or done, an optional `time`, and optional `output`. |
| `title` | `string` | The header text. Defaults to "Agent activity". |
| `running` | `boolean` | Shows a spinner in the header while true, and a green dot once false. |
| `status` | `string` | The words beside the header mark. Defaults to "Running step N", then "N steps, Xs". |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set false to give it a card of its own. |
| `onToggle` / `toggleRow` | `callback` | Fires when a row opens or closes. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the rows and the output panes are squared off with hairline edges; in Soft they are
rounded chips with soft fills. Added and removed lines in a row's output take the add and remove
colors from the tokens.


# Activity heatmap (/docs/components/activity-heatmap)

An activity heatmap shows when something is busy, as a 7×24 grid of cells — one a day down, one
an hour across — each tinted from the accent by its value. Pass one or more `series`; each is 168
values from 0 to 1 (Monday 12am first), with a `max` and `unit` for the tips and an optional
`note`. With two or more series a switch appears, and picking one sweeps it in as a wave from the
top left. In a narrow card the grid shows half the day at a time in bigger cells and scrolls
sideways, starting at the latest hours.

<Preview>
  <ActivityHeatmapExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ActivityHeatmap, type ActivityHeatmapSeries } from './activity-heatmap/ActivityHeatmap';

const series: ActivityHeatmapSeries[] = [
  { key: 'agent', label: 'Agent', values: agentValues, max: 40, unit: 'runs', note: 'Busiest overnight, when the queue runs' },
  { key: 'team', label: 'Team', values: teamValues, max: 25, unit: 'edits', note: 'Busiest 10am to 4pm on weekdays' },
];

<ActivityHeatmap series={series} defaultValue="agent" period="Last 4 weeks" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ActivityHeatmapComponent] -->
series: ActivityHeatmapSeries[] = [
  { key: 'agent', label: 'Agent', values: agentValues, max: 40, unit: 'runs', note: 'Busiest overnight, when the queue runs' },
  { key: 'team', label: 'Team', values: teamValues, max: 25, unit: 'edits', note: 'Busiest 10am to 4pm on weekdays' },
];

<ActivityHeatmap [series]="series" defaultValue="agent" period="Last 4 weeks" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/activity_heatmap.dart';

final series = [
  ActivityHeatmapSeries(key: 'agent', label: 'Agent', values: agentValues, max: 40, unit: 'runs', note: 'Busiest overnight, when the queue runs'),
  ActivityHeatmapSeries(key: 'team', label: 'Team', values: teamValues, max: 25, unit: 'edits', note: 'Busiest 10am to 4pm on weekdays'),
];

ActivityHeatmap(series: series, defaultValue: 'agent', period: 'Last 4 weeks'),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `series` | `ActivityHeatmapSeries[]` | One or more series; the switch shows when there are two or more. |
| `value` | `string` | The series on show, by key. Leave it out to let the switch pick it. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | The series shown first when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first series. |
| `onValueChange` | `(key) => void` | Called when the switch picks a series. |
| `title` | `string` | Header text. Defaults to `Activity`. |
| `period` | `string` | The line under the title before the cells fill in, and when a series has no note. Defaults to `Last 4 weeks`. |
| `series[].key` | `string` | Identifies the series, used by `value` / `defaultValue`. |
| `series[].label` | `string` | The switch label, like `Agent`. |
| `series[].values` | `number[]` | 168 values from 0 to 1, one an hour, Monday 12am first. |
| `series[].max` | `number` | What a full cell counts, for the tips, like `40`. |
| `series[].unit` | `string` | What it counts, for the tips, like `runs`. |
| `series[].note` | `string` | The line under the title while this series shows. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface, and each cell is a mix of the accent into the chip by its value — so the whole
grid shifts with the theme's accent and the empty cells read against the surface. In Soft the card
and cells are a touch rounder.


# Agenda (/docs/components/agenda)

An agenda lists today's events in order. A live **now line** sits after the last event that is over,
so you can see at a glance what is next. Past events fade back. Open an event to reveal the notes the
agent prepared for it and an optional action like **Join**. Events without notes don't open.

<Preview>
  <AgendaExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Agenda } from './agenda/Agenda';

const items = [
  { time: '09:30', title: 'Pricing review with Maya', detail: '30 min · Zoom', past: true },
  { time: '11:00', title: 'Agent demo', detail: '45 min · Room 2',
    notes: ['Latest build is green.', 'Talking points ready.'],
    action: { label: 'Join in 18 min' } },
  { time: '16:00', title: 'Ship pricing v4', detail: 'visuno.dev/pricing' },
];

<Agenda title="Today" subtitle="Friday, Oct 23" now="10:42" items={items} defaultOpen="Agent demo" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [AgendaComponent] -->
<Agenda title="Today" subtitle="Friday, Oct 23" now="10:42"
  [items]="items" defaultOpen="Agent demo" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/agenda.dart';

Agenda(
  title: 'Today',
  subtitle: 'Friday, Oct 23',
  now: '10:42',
  items: const [
    AgendaItem(time: '09:30', title: 'Pricing review with Maya', detail: '30 min · Zoom', past: true),
    AgendaItem(time: '11:00', title: 'Agent demo', detail: '45 min · Room 2',
      notes: ['Latest build is green.', 'Talking points ready.'],
      action: AgendaAction(label: 'Join in 18 min')),
  ],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `AgendaItem[]` | The events, in order. Each has a `time`, `title`, optional `detail`, `people`, `notes` and `action`. |
| `title` | `string` | The heading, like `Today`. |
| `subtitle` | `string` | The quiet line under the title, like `Monday, Oct 19`. |
| `count` | `string` | The tag in the corner. Defaults to `N events`. |
| `now` | `string` | The time on the now line, like `10:42`. Leave it out for no line. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `string \| null` | The item whose notes are open, by key. Leave it out to let each item toggle. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(key: string \| null) => void` | Fires when the open item changes. |

An `AgendaItem` carries `time`, `title`, `detail?`, `people?`, `past?` (already over — fades back),
`notes?` (shown when opened) and `action?` (`{ label, onClick }`, a button at the end of the notes).

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The now
line, event bars and prep-note sparkles take the active theme's accent; avatars use the shared
`--vo-av-*` palette. All spacing and radii come from the `--vo-*` tokens.


# Agent inbox (/docs/components/agent-inbox)

The agent inbox puts every run in one list, grouped by what it needs: **Needs you**, **Running** and
**Done**. A running run shows a live clock; one that waits for you offers **Approve**, and one that
failed turns red and offers **Retry**. When a run changes group it glides to its new place, an empty
group goes away, and the line beside the title says what is left.

<Preview>
  <AgentInboxExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { AgentInbox, type InboxRun } from './agent-inbox/AgentInbox';

const runs: InboxRun[] = [
  { id: 'pub', title: 'Publish the pricing page', agent: 'Design agent', group: 'needs', detail: 'Waiting for your approval' },
  { id: 'tok', title: 'Export tokens to CSS', agent: 'Build agent', group: 'needs', failed: true, detail: 'Failed: rate limited', why: 'Figma answered 429. Safe to retry' },
  { id: 'cards', title: 'Rework the plan cards', agent: 'Design agent', group: 'running', detail: 'Editing frame 3 of 6', seconds: 102 },
  { id: 'copy', title: 'Rewrite plan descriptions', agent: 'Copy agent', group: 'done', ended: '12m ago' },
];

<AgentInbox runs={runs} onApprove={(id) => start(id)} onRetry={(id) => retry(id)} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [AgentInboxComponent] -->
runs: InboxRun[] = [
  { id: 'pub', title: 'Publish the pricing page', agent: 'Design agent', group: 'needs', detail: 'Waiting for your approval' },
  { id: 'cards', title: 'Rework the plan cards', agent: 'Design agent', group: 'running', detail: 'Editing frame 3 of 6', seconds: 102 },
];

<AgentInbox [runs]="runs" (approve)="start($event)" (retry)="retry($event)" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/agent_inbox.dart';

final runs = <InboxRun>[
  const InboxRun(id: 'pub', title: 'Publish the pricing page', agent: 'Design agent', group: InboxGroup.needs, detail: 'Waiting for your approval'),
  const InboxRun(id: 'cards', title: 'Rework the plan cards', agent: 'Design agent', group: InboxGroup.running, detail: 'Editing frame 3 of 6', seconds: 102),
];

AgentInbox(
  runs: runs,
  onApprove: (id) => start(id),
  onRetry: (id) => retry(id),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runs` | `InboxRun[]` | Every run to show, each in its group. |
| `onApprove` | `(id) => void` | Adds Approve to the runs that need you and haven't failed. |
| `onRetry` | `(id) => void` | Adds Retry to the runs that failed. |
| `title` | `string` | The inbox's name. Defaults to `"Inbox"`. |
| `status` | `string` | The line beside the title. Defaults to `"2 need you"`, then `"2 running"`, then `"All clear · 4 done today"`. |
| `run.id` | `string` | Keeps a run's row when it moves group. |
| `run.title` | `string` | What the run is for, like "Publish the pricing page". |
| `run.agent` | `string` | Which agent runs it. Its first letter marks the row. |
| `run.color` | `string` | The mark's fill, like `var(--vo-av-l)`. Defaults to the accent. |
| `run.group` | `needs \| running \| done` | Which part of the inbox the run sits in. |
| `run.detail` | `string` | The line under the title: why it needs you, or what it is doing now. |
| `run.failed` | `boolean` | Turns the row red and offers Retry instead of Approve. |
| `run.why` | `string` | More on the failure, in a tooltip on its detail line. |
| `run.seconds` | `number` | How long a running run has gone. Its clock counts on from here. |
| `run.ended` | `string` | When a finished run ended, like "12m ago". |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The panel
sits on a surface with the card shadow; a failed run tints with the bad tokens, the running clock and
the Approve pill use the accent, and the avatar marks take the shared `--vo-av-*` colours with their
own ink. In Soft the panel and its rows are rounder.


# Agent lanes (/docs/components/agent-lanes)

Agent lanes show several agents working side by side, each in its own lane and hue — its badge, its
step track, its `Working` tag and its stretch of the relay line that joins the badges. A working lane
breathes, shimmers and fills its next step; a `handoff` opens a line between two lanes and runs a
light down the relay line from the sender's badge to the taker's, and the stretch it crossed stays
lit. Each `lane` takes a `name`, an `icon`, a `tone`, a `status`, the `activity` it is on, how many
`steps` the track is cut into and how many are `done`, and an optional `log` the row opens to.

<Preview>
  <AgentLanesExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { AgentLanes, type AgentLane, type AgentHandoff } from './agent-lanes/AgentLanes';

const lanes: AgentLane[] = [
  { key: 'researcher', name: 'Researcher', icon: 'search', tone: 'blue', status: 'done', activity: 'Noted 3 patterns', done: 3 },
  { key: 'designer', name: 'Designer', icon: 'edit', tone: 'purple', status: 'working', activity: 'Exporting frames', done: 2 },
  { key: 'reviewer', name: 'Reviewer', icon: 'eye', tone: 'green', status: 'waiting', activity: 'Waiting for the designer' },
];

const handoff: AgentHandoff = { from: 'researcher', to: 'designer', what: 'the brief' };

<AgentLanes lanes={lanes} handoff={handoff} onPausedChange={setPaused} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [AgentLanesComponent] -->
lanes: AgentLane[] = [
  { key: 'researcher', name: 'Researcher', icon: 'search', tone: 'blue', status: 'done', activity: 'Noted 3 patterns', done: 3 },
  { key: 'designer', name: 'Designer', icon: 'edit', tone: 'purple', status: 'working', activity: 'Exporting frames', done: 2 },
  { key: 'reviewer', name: 'Reviewer', icon: 'eye', tone: 'green', status: 'waiting', activity: 'Waiting for the designer' },
];
handoff: AgentHandoff = { from: 'researcher', to: 'designer', what: 'the brief' };

<AgentLanes [lanes]="lanes" [handoff]="handoff" [pauseWired]="true" (pausedChange)="paused = $event" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/agent_lanes.dart';

AgentLanes(
  lanes: const [
    AgentLane(key: 'researcher', name: 'Researcher', icon: Icons.search, tone: LaneTone.blue, status: LaneStatus.done, activity: 'Noted 3 patterns', done: 3),
    AgentLane(key: 'designer', name: 'Designer', icon: Icons.edit_outlined, tone: LaneTone.purple, status: LaneStatus.working, activity: 'Exporting frames', done: 2),
    AgentLane(key: 'reviewer', name: 'Reviewer', icon: Icons.visibility_outlined, tone: LaneTone.green, status: LaneStatus.waiting, activity: 'Waiting for the designer'),
  ],
  handoff: const AgentHandoff(from: 'researcher', to: 'designer', what: 'the brief'),
  onPausedChange: (v) => setState(() => paused = v),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lanes` | `AgentLane[]` | The agents, each in its own lane and hue. |
| `title` | `string` | Header text. Defaults to "N agents working", "All agents paused" or "All N agents finished". |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds to show as `m:ss`. Leave it out to let the header count while agents work. |
| `paused` | `boolean` | Whether every agent is paused. Working lanes then show `Paused` and the clock stops. |
| `onPausedChange` | `(paused) => void` | Adds the Pause all / Resume button, until every lane is done. |
| `handoff` | `AgentHandoff` | The hand-off to show. Clear it and its line slides away; the stretch it crossed stays lit. |
| `expanded` | `string[]` | Keys of the lanes that are open. Leave it out to let each row toggle itself. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |
| `lane.name` | `string` | The agent's name, like "Researcher". |
| `lane.icon` | `IconName` | The glyph on the agent's badge. |
| `lane.tone` | `blue \| purple \| green \| orange \| red \| yellow \| pink \| teal` | The lane's hue. Defaults to `blue`. |
| `lane.status` | `queued \| waiting \| working \| paused \| done` | `working` breathes and fills its next step; `done` fills the badge with its hue. |
| `lane.activity` | `string` | What the agent is on, or what it waits for. Crossfades on change and shimmers while working. |
| `lane.steps` | `number` | How many steps the track is cut into. Defaults to `3`. |
| `lane.done` | `number` | How many steps are finished. The next one fills while the agent works. |
| `lane.progress` | `number` | How far through the step in hand, 0 to 1. Leave it out and that step fills part way. |
| `lane.log` | `{ text; time? }[]` | What the agent did, shown when the lane is opened. New entries slide in. |
| `handoff` | `{ from; to; what }` | One agent passing work to another down the relay line. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). Each lane's
hue comes from the theme's agent palette tokens (`--vo-pb`, `--vo-pl`, `--vo-pm` …) with a livelier
"mark" variant for its track, line and finished badge, so the lanes stay 3:1 against the surface; in
dark mode the agent colours are light already and are used as they are. In the Soft style the lanes
are rounder and the tracks are hatched rather than washed.


# Agent phases (/docs/components/agent-phases)

Agent phases show which phase the agent is in, in one line: its glyph, its name shimmering while the
phase lasts, and the seconds so far, with a track of six short segments under it that fills phase by
phase. When the agent needs you, is slow or fails, a line under the track says so with what to do;
once it is done the line reads how long it took and opens to the phases it ran through.

<Preview>
  <AgentPhasesExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { AgentPhases } from './agent-phases/AgentPhases';

<AgentPhases phase="reading" label="Reading 3 articles" />
<AgentPhases phase="searching" error={{ text: 'The search timed out', onRetry: retry }} />
<AgentPhases phase="reading" slow={{ text: 'Still working…', onStop: stop }} />
<AgentPhases phase="waiting" ask={{ text: 'Offer Maya a refund of $48?', onApprove: approve }} />
<AgentPhases phase="done" took={{ thinking: 2, searching: 3, reading: 4 }} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [AgentPhasesComponent] -->
<AgentPhases phase="reading" label="Reading 3 articles"></AgentPhases>
<AgentPhases phase="searching" [error]="searchError"></AgentPhases>
<AgentPhases phase="reading" [slow]="slowNote"></AgentPhases>
<AgentPhases phase="waiting" [ask]="refundAsk"></AgentPhases>
<AgentPhases phase="done" [took]="took"></AgentPhases>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/agent_phases.dart';

const AgentPhases(phase: AgentPhase.reading, label: 'Reading 3 articles'),
AgentPhases(phase: AgentPhase.searching, error: AgentPhasesError(text: 'The search timed out', onRetry: retry)),
AgentPhases(phase: AgentPhase.reading, slow: AgentPhasesSlow(text: 'Still working…', onStop: stop)),
AgentPhases(phase: AgentPhase.waiting, ask: AgentPhasesAsk(text: 'Offer Maya a refund of \$48?', onApprove: approve)),
const AgentPhases(phase: AgentPhase.done, took: {AgentPhase.thinking: 2, AgentPhase.searching: 3, AgentPhase.reading: 4}),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `phase` | `thinking \| searching \| reading \| waiting \| writing \| done` | Which phase the agent is in. |
| `label` | `string` | What the line says. Defaults to the phase's name; once done, "Thought for 12s". |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds so far. Counts by itself while left out, and stops while waiting for you. |
| `error` | `object` | A step that failed: the line turns red and says so, with Retry. Has `text`, optional `detail`, and `onRetry`. |
| `slow` | `object` | Shown while the phase takes long, with Stop. Has `text` and an optional `onStop`. |
| `ask` | `object` | What the agent waits for in the waiting phase. Has `text`, optional `approveLabel`, `onApprove` and optional `onDecline`. |
| `took` | `Record<phase, number>` | Seconds each phase took, for the list a finished line opens to. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Whether the finished line is open. Leave `open` out to let the header toggle it. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The glyph
and the current segment take the phase's colour — the accent while it works, amber while it waits,
red on an error and green when done. In Blueprint the segments are squared off and the shimmer rests
on a solid colour.


# Agent run timeline (/docs/components/agent-run-timeline)

An agent run timeline draws one run as a Gantt chart. Every step is a bar on a shared time axis:
the model thinking or writing (purple), a tool like a file read or a test run (teal), or an app the
agent works in, such as Figma or GitHub (orange), each with its own mark. A playhead marks now while
the run streams and the lanes it has passed take a faint wash; the step at work breathes a ring round
its icon and its bar carries a bright leading edge. A failed step hatches red and tags its label, and
a retry hangs a dashed line off the end of the step it retries. The key under the title counts how
long each kind has run, and the footer adds up the total time, cost, steps and retries. Once the run
is done the playhead stops at the finish and turns green.

<Preview>
  <AgentRunTimelineExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { AgentRunTimeline, type TimelineStep } from './agent-run-timeline/AgentRunTimeline';

const steps: TimelineStep[] = [
  { label: 'Plan the change', icon: 'spark', kind: 'model', start: 0, duration: 1.6, cost: 0.03 },
  { label: 'Read 6 files', icon: 'file-text', kind: 'tool', start: 1.6, duration: 2.2, cost: 0.02 },
  { label: 'Search Figma', brand: 'figma', kind: 'app', start: 1.9, duration: 1.4, cost: 0.01 },
  { label: 'Run tests', icon: 'term', kind: 'tool', start: 6.5, duration: 1.5, failed: true, tag: '2 failed' },
  { label: 'Run tests again', icon: 'refresh', kind: 'tool', start: 8.1, duration: 1.9, retry: true },
];

<AgentRunTimeline title="Run 4821, update the pricing page" steps={steps} time={6.3} span={12} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```ts
// imports: [AgentRunTimelineComponent]
steps: TimelineStep[] = [
  { label: 'Plan the change', icon: 'spark', kind: 'model', start: 0, duration: 1.6, cost: 0.03 },
  { label: 'Read 6 files', icon: 'file-text', kind: 'tool', start: 1.6, duration: 2.2, cost: 0.02 },
  { label: 'Search Figma', brand: 'figma', kind: 'app', start: 1.9, duration: 1.4, cost: 0.01 },
  { label: 'Run tests', icon: 'term', kind: 'tool', start: 6.5, duration: 1.5, failed: true, tag: '2 failed' },
  { label: 'Run tests again', icon: 'refresh', kind: 'tool', start: 8.1, duration: 1.9, retry: true },
];
```

```html
<AgentRunTimeline
  title="Run 4821, update the pricing page"
  [steps]="steps"
  [time]="6.3"
  [span]="12"
></AgentRunTimeline>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/agent_run_timeline.dart';

AgentRunTimeline(
  title: 'Run 4821, update the pricing page',
  time: 6.3,
  span: 12,
  steps: const [
    TimelineStep(label: 'Plan the change', icon: Icons.auto_awesome, kind: StepKind.model, start: 0, duration: 1.6, cost: 0.03),
    TimelineStep(label: 'Read 6 files', icon: Icons.description_outlined, kind: StepKind.tool, start: 1.6, duration: 2.2, cost: 0.02),
    TimelineStep(label: 'Search Figma', brand: StepBrand.figma, kind: StepKind.app, start: 1.9, duration: 1.4, cost: 0.01),
    TimelineStep(label: 'Run tests', icon: Icons.terminal, kind: StepKind.tool, start: 6.5, duration: 1.5, failed: true, tag: '2 failed'),
    TimelineStep(label: 'Run tests again', icon: Icons.refresh, kind: StepKind.tool, start: 8.1, duration: 1.9, retry: true),
  ],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The run's name, shown over the status line. |
| `steps` | `TimelineStep[]` | The steps of the run, each a bar on the shared axis. |
| `time` | `number` | Seconds into the run. Bars grow up to it and the playhead sits on it. Leave it out once the run has finished. |
| `span` | `number` | Seconds the axis covers. Defaults to the end of the last step, rounded up to a multiple of 4. |
| `ticks` | `number[]` | Labels on the axis, in seconds. Defaults to quarters of the span. |
| `status` | `string` | The line under the title. Defaults to the steps running now, then "Finished in 11.7s". |
| `stats` | `TimelineStat[]` | The figures in the footer once the run is done. Defaults to the total time, cost, steps and retries, which count up while it plays. |
| `kindLabels` | `{ model?; tool?; app? }` | The names of the kinds in the key. Defaults to Model, Tools and Apps. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set false to give it a card of its own. |

A `TimelineStep` has a `label`, an optional `icon` or `brand` (an app's own mark, like `figma`,
`github` or `slack`), a `kind` (`model`, `tool` or `app`, which picks its colour), a `start` and
`duration` in seconds, an optional `color`, `cost`, and — for a step that failed — `failed`, a `tag`
and a `note`, and `retry` to hang a dashed line off the step it retries. A `TimelineStat` has a
`value`, a `label` and an optional `icon`.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). Each kind
keeps its colour from the chart palette — purple for the model, teal for tools, orange for apps — and
the playhead runs in the accent, turning green at the finish. In Blueprint the bars square off and a
running bar switches from a sweeping sheen to a marching stripe; a failed bar is red and hatched in
every theme.


# Agent tree (/docs/components/agent-tree)

An agent tree shows an orchestrator and its sub-agents as a tree. Each row has its `name`, its
`task`, a status glyph and a `cost`; a branch's cost is its own plus everything under it, and the
header rolls up the whole run. A chevron folds a branch, and the arrow keys move through it as in
any tree view. A failed step can carry a `fix` — a button under its task that offers the way out.

<Preview>
  <AgentTreeExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { AgentTree, type AgentNode } from './agent-tree/AgentTree';

const root: AgentNode = {
  id: 'root', name: 'Orchestrator', task: 'Plans the work and hands it out', status: 'running', cost: 0.04,
  children: [
    { id: 'res', name: 'Research agent', task: 'Compare 3 pricing pages', status: 'done', cost: 0.02, children: [
      { id: 'res1', name: 'Read the pages', task: '3 pages, 9.4k words', status: 'done', cost: 0.06 },
    ] },
    { id: 'des', name: 'Design agent', task: 'Rework the plan cards', status: 'failed', cost: 0.02, children: [
      { id: 'des1', name: 'Apply library tokens', task: "color.accent.600 isn't in the library", status: 'failed', cost: 0.02,
        fix: { label: 'Use color.accent.500', onClick: applyFix } },
    ] },
  ],
};

<AgentTree root={root} title="Redesign the pricing page" defaultCollapsed={['res']} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [AgentTreeComponent] -->
root: AgentNode = {
  id: 'root', name: 'Orchestrator', task: 'Plans the work and hands it out', status: 'running', cost: 0.04,
  children: [ /* agents and their steps */ ],
};

<AgentTree
  [root]="root"
  title="Redesign the pricing page"
  [defaultCollapsed]="['res']"
  (collapsedChange)="onCollapsed($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/agent_tree.dart';

const root = AgentNode(
  id: 'root', name: 'Orchestrator', task: 'Plans the work and hands it out',
  status: AgentNodeStatus.running, cost: 0.04,
  children: [
    AgentNode(id: 'res', name: 'Research agent', task: 'Compare 3 pricing pages',
      status: AgentNodeStatus.done, cost: 0.02, children: [
        AgentNode(id: 'res1', name: 'Read the pages', task: '3 pages, 9.4k words',
          status: AgentNodeStatus.done, cost: 0.06),
      ]),
  ],
);

AgentTree(
  root: root,
  title: 'Redesign the pricing page',
  defaultCollapsed: const ['res'],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | `AgentNode` | The orchestrator, with its agents and their steps as children. |
| `title` | `string` | The run's goal, like "Redesign the pricing page". |
| `status` | `string` | The line under the title. Defaults to "Running", "N steps failed" or "Done". |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds to show as `m:ss`. Leave it out to count up until the root is done. |
| `summary` | `string \| false` | Shown under the tree once the root is done. `false` hides it; default rolls one up. |
| `collapsed` | `string[]` | Ids of the folded branches (controlled). |
| `defaultCollapsed` | `string[]` | Ids folded to begin with when uncontrolled. |
| `onCollapsedChange` | `(ids) => void` | Emitted when a branch folds or unfolds, with the ids now folded. |
| `formatCost` | `(dollars) => string` | Writes a cost. Defaults to dollars and cents, like `$0.12`. |
| `AgentNode.id` | `string` | Identifies the node; used as the fold key. |
| `AgentNode.name` | `string` | Like "Design agent", or a step's name. |
| `AgentNode.task` | `string` | Its task, or what it is doing now. Crossfades when it changes. |
| `AgentNode.status` | `queued \| running \| done \| failed` | Picks the status glyph and row tint. |
| `AgentNode.cost` | `number` | What this node spent on its own. A branch shows this plus everything under it. |
| `AgentNode.fix` | `{ label; onClick }` | On a failed step, a button under its task that offers the way out. |
| `AgentNode.children` | `AgentNode[]` | The agents or steps under this node. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The tree
sits on a surface; the running glyph spins in the accent colour, a done branch turns green and a
failed step tints its row with the bad-tone background, so it reads in either theme. In Soft the
card, rows and the fix button are rounder.


# Answer action bar (/docs/components/answer-action-bar)

Every action on an answer in one raised rail under it: **copy** it, **regenerate** it — which
keeps each version and pages between them — give it a **thumbs** up or down (a down asks what was
off, and the reason can write a new version that answers it), and **read it aloud**, which widens
the button into a progress bar and a clock and lights each word as it is read. Pass `versions`
oldest first; each version carries its own `meta`, its own `rating`, and an optional `changed`
phrase that is highlighted as what moved from the version before.

<Preview>
  <AnswerActionBarExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { AnswerActionBar, type AnswerVersion } from './answer-action-bar/AnswerActionBar';

const versions: AnswerVersion[] = [
  { text: 'Pro is $24 a month, or $19 billed yearly. That saves 15%.', meta: 'Sonnet 5.5 · 6.2s' },
  {
    text: 'Pro is $24 a month, or $19 billed yearly, which saves 21%, or $60 a year.',
    changed: '21%, or $60 a year',
    meta: 'Sonnet 5.5 · 4.8s',
  },
];

<AnswerActionBar
  question="How much do people save on the yearly Pro plan?"
  versions={versions}
  onRegenerate={addVersion}
  onCopy={(text) => {}}
  onRate={(index, rating) => {}}
  onReason={(index, reason) => {}}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [AnswerActionBarComponent] -->
versions: AnswerVersion[] = [
  { text: 'Pro is $24 a month, or $19 billed yearly. That saves 15%.', meta: 'Sonnet 5.5 · 6.2s' },
];

<AnswerActionBar
  [question]="'How much do people save on the yearly Pro plan?'"
  [versions]="versions"
  (regenerateClick)="addVersion()"
  (copyText)="onCopy($event)"
  (rateChange)="onRate($event)"
  (reason)="onReason($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/answer_action_bar.dart';

AnswerActionBar(
  question: 'How much do people save on the yearly Pro plan?',
  versions: const [
    AnswerVersion(
      text: 'Pro is \$24 a month, or \$19 billed yearly. That saves 15%.',
      meta: 'Sonnet 5.5 · 6.2s',
    ),
  ],
  onRegenerate: addVersion,
  onCopy: (text) {},
  onRate: (index, rating) {},
  onReason: (index, reason) {},
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `question` | `string` | The person's message the answer replies to, shown as a bubble above it. |
| `versions` | `AnswerVersion[]` | Every version of the answer so far, oldest first. |
| `version` / `defaultVersion` | `number` | Which version is showing. Leave `version` out to let the arrows page through them. |
| `onVersionChange` | `(index) => void` | Called when the version shown changes. |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | The newest version is still being written: paging and reading wait. |
| `onRegenerate` | `() => void` | Called by the regenerate button. Add a version and show it to answer it. |
| `onCopy` | `(text) => void` | Called with the plain text after it is copied. |
| `onRate` | `(index, rating) => void` | Called when a thumb is pressed or pressed again to clear it. |
| `reasons` | `string[]` | The reasons a thumbs down offers. Defaults to Wrong numbers, Too long, Not our tone, Missed the brief. |
| `onReason` | `(index, reason) => void` | Called with the reason picked after a thumbs down. |
| `status` | `string` | The quiet line under the bar, like "Writing a new version". It shimmers while streaming. |
| `statusTone` | `warn \| ok` | `warn` turns the status amber; `ok` gives it a green check. |
| `reading` / `defaultReading` | `idle \| playing \| paused` | Read aloud: `playing` lights each word in turn, `paused` keeps the place. |
| `onReadingChange` | `(state) => void` | Called when read-aloud starts, pauses, resumes or ends. |
| `secondsPerWord` | `number` | How long the built-in reading clock gives each word. Defaults to `0.28`. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |
| `AnswerVersion` | `{ text; changed?; meta?; rating? }` | One version: its `text`, the `changed` phrase that is highlighted, its quiet `meta`, and its own `rating`. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The rail
is a surface pill with the shared shadow; the thumbs tint with the ok and bad tokens when pressed,
the read-aloud button and the lit word pick up the accent tint, and the changed phrase is marked
with the ok highlight — all from the theme tokens, so the bar reads against a light or a dark
thread.


# Artifact card (/docs/components/artifact-card)

A file the agent made, shown four ways with the same behaviour: a `compact` row, a `preview` card
with its first page, an `inline` chip inside a message, or a `stack` of its versions. Each plays a
writing state while `state` is `writing` — the meta line shows `status` and the actions hold back —
then settles when it turns `ready`. From there you can open the file in a reader, switch between its
`versions`, Copy its content and Download it.

<Preview>
  <ArtifactCardExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ArtifactCard, type ArtifactVersion } from './artifact-card/ArtifactCard';

const versions: ArtifactVersion[] = [
  { title: 'Pricing page review', meta: 'edited 2 hours ago', note: 'First pass', content: '# Pricing page review\n\n## Summary\n\n…' },
  { title: 'Pricing page review', meta: 'edited just now', note: 'Fixes, ordered by impact', content: '# Pricing page review\n\n## Summary\n\n…' },
];

<ArtifactCard
  variant="compact"
  versions={versions}
  kind="Report"
  icon="file-text"
  state="ready"
  onOpen={(v) => openBesideChat(v)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ArtifactCardComponent] -->
versions: ArtifactVersion[] = [
  { title: 'Pricing page review', meta: 'edited 2 hours ago', note: 'First pass', content: '# Pricing page review\n\n## Summary\n\n…' },
  { title: 'Pricing page review', meta: 'edited just now', note: 'Fixes, ordered by impact', content: '# Pricing page review\n\n## Summary\n\n…' },
];

<ArtifactCard
  variant="compact"
  [versions]="versions"
  kind="Report"
  icon="file-text"
  state="ready"
  (opened)="openBesideChat($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/artifact_card.dart';

const versions = [
  ArtifactVersion(title: 'Pricing page review', meta: 'edited 2 hours ago', note: 'First pass', content: '# Pricing page review\n\n## Summary\n\n…'),
  ArtifactVersion(title: 'Pricing page review', meta: 'edited just now', note: 'Fixes, ordered by impact', content: '# Pricing page review\n\n## Summary\n\n…'),
];

ArtifactCard(
  variant: ArtifactVariant.compact,
  versions: versions,
  kind: 'Report',
  icon: Icons.description_outlined,
  state: ArtifactState.ready,
  onOpen: (v) => openBesideChat(v),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `compact \| preview \| inline \| stack` | How the card shows the file. Defaults to `compact`. |
| `versions` | `ArtifactVersion[]` | The versions, oldest first. |
| `version` | `number` | Index of the version shown. Leave it out to let the versions menu change it. |
| `defaultVersion` | `number` | The version shown at first. Defaults to the latest. |
| `onVersionChange` | `(version) => void` | Called when the shown version changes. |
| `state` | `writing \| ready` | `writing` holds the actions back and shows `status`; `ready` settles the card. |
| `status` | `string` | The line shown while writing, like "Reading the page…". |
| `progress` | `number` | How far the writing has got, from 0 to 1. The compact card draws it along its bottom edge. |
| `kind` | `string` | The kind of file on the meta line, like "Report" or "Table". |
| `icon` | `IconName` | The file's icon. |
| `fileName` | `string` | The name Download saves under, before "-v3.md". Defaults to the slugged title. |
| `ext` | `string` | The extension Download saves with. `csv` also shows the content as a table in the reader. |
| `onOpen` | `(version) => void` | Called when the file is opened. With a handler, Open does not show the card's own reader. |
| `openLabel` | `string` | The Open button's tip, like "Open beside the chat". Its label stays "Open". |
| `onCopy` | `(version) => void` | Called after Copy has put the version's content on the clipboard. |
| `onDownload` | `(version) => void` | Called after Download has saved the version's content as a file. |
| `ArtifactVersion.title` | `string` | The file's name in this version. |
| `ArtifactVersion.meta` | `string` | When this version was made, like "edited 2 hours ago". |
| `ArtifactVersion.note` | `string` | What changed in this version. Shown in the menu and the stack. |
| `ArtifactVersion.content` | `string` | The file itself, as Markdown (or CSV when `ext` is `csv`). |
| `ArtifactVersion.summary` | `string` | The text on the preview's first page. Defaults to the first paragraph of `content`. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface with the shared shadow, the icon tile and version marks take the accent, and the
reader opens over the card's nearest positioned ancestor — the stage here, your chat column in an
app. In Soft the card and its buttons are rounder; the stack also casts a soft shadow on the desk
that fades as the sheets are laid out.


# Attachment tray (/docs/components/attachment-tray)

A drop zone, then the files as plain rows. Each file wears its type's hue — its badge, its
progress ring and the wash that fills its row from the left as it uploads. Once a file is up the
agent reads it: the line shimmers, then says what it found, like `12 pages`. Pass `files` with each
one's `progress`, `reading` and `detail`; `onFiles` hands back what the person dropped or picked.

<Preview>
  <AttachmentTrayExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { AttachmentTray, type Attachment } from './attachment-tray/AttachmentTray';

const [files, setFiles] = useState<Attachment[]>([]);

<AttachmentTray
  files={files}
  title="Drop files here"
  action={{ label: 'add sample files', onClick: addSamples }}
  onFiles={(picked) => upload(picked)}
  onRemove={(id) => setFiles((f) => f.filter((x) => x.id !== id))}
/>;

// each file: { id, name, size, progress /* 0–100 */, reading?, detail? }
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [AttachmentTrayComponent] -->
files: Attachment[] = [
  { id: 'brief.pdf', name: 'brief.pdf', size: 2_400_000, progress: 100, detail: '12 pages' },
];

<AttachmentTray
  [files]="files"
  title="Drop files here"
  [action]="{ label: 'add sample files', onClick: addSamples }"
  (filesPicked)="upload($event)"
  (remove$)="files = files.filter(f => f.id !== $event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/attachment_tray.dart';

AttachmentTray(
  files: const [
    Attachment(id: 'brief.pdf', name: 'brief.pdf', size: 2400000, progress: 100, detail: '12 pages'),
  ],
  title: 'Drop files here',
  action: AttachmentAction(label: 'add sample files', onClick: addSamples),
  onRemove: (id) => setState(() => files.removeWhere((f) => f.id == id)),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | `Attachment[]` | The files in the tray, each uploading then read in place. |
| `onFiles` | `(files: File[]) => void` | Files the person dropped on the tray or picked with the file dialog. |
| `onRemove` | `(id) => void` | Adds a remove button to each file. Called once the file has animated out. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | The drop zone's heading. Defaults to "Drop files here". |
| `action` | `{ label; onClick }` | A link after "or" in the drop zone, like "add sample files". |
| `accept` | `string` | Passed to the file input, like `image/*,.pdf`. |
| `summary` | `string` | The line under the list. Defaults to how many files the agent can read. |
| `dragging` | `boolean` | Shows the drop zone as if a file were being dragged over it, for a scripted demo. |
| `file.progress` | `number` | 0 to 100. The ring closes and the row fills with the file type's colour. |
| `file.reading` | `boolean` | While the agent reads the file: a spinner, and "Reading" shimmering after the size. |
| `file.detail` | `string` | What the agent found once it has read the file, like "12 pages". |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). Each file
takes its hue from its type — PDF, image, CSV and the rest — drawn from the palette tokens, so the
badge, the ring and the row wash stay in step across the themes; in Soft the drop zone and badges are
rounder. The dashed drop-zone edge, the uploading rings and the reading shimmer all respect
`prefers-reduced-motion`.


# Badge (/docs/components/badge)

A badge is a compact label. Its `tone` picks the color (neutral, the accent tint, the three
states, or one of eight tag colors). Two sizes, an optional dot or icon before the label, and an
optional remove button after it.

<Preview>
  <BadgeExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Badge } from './badge/Badge';

<Badge tone="success">Live</Badge>
<Badge tone="success" dot>Running</Badge>
<Badge tone="accent" size="sm">Pro</Badge>
<Badge tone="warning" onRemove={() => drop()}>Production</Badge>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [BadgeComponent] -->
<Badge tone="success">Live</Badge>
<Badge tone="success" [dot]="true" [live]="true">Running</Badge>
<Badge tone="accent" size="sm">Pro</Badge>
<Badge tone="warning" [removable]="true" (remove)="drop()">Production</Badge>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/badge.dart';

const Badge('Live', tone: BadgeTone.success),
const Badge('Running', tone: BadgeTone.success, dot: true),
const Badge('Pro', tone: BadgeTone.accent, size: BadgeSize.sm),
Badge('Production', tone: BadgeTone.warning, onRemove: drop),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `neutral \| accent \| success \| warning \| danger \| blue \| violet \| green \| orange \| red \| yellow \| pink \| teal` | Color as text on its own tint. Neutral by default. |
| `size` | `sm \| md` | `sm` is 20px tall, `md` is 24px (the default). |
| `dot` | `boolean` | A dot in the badge's color before the label. |
| `icon` | `IconName` | An icon before the label. |
| `onRemove` / `remove` | `callback` | Shows a remove button after the label. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the badge is squared off and set in small caps with a hairline in its own color; in Soft
it is a pill.


# Bar chart (/docs/components/bar-chart)

A bar chart plots a value per bar, with a readout on hover that breaks each one down by `series` and
a switch between `ranges`. The bars grow in one after another a moment after the chart appears, then
redraw left to right on every switch while the total rolls to its new figure. Off by default each
bar is one block in the accent; set `stacked` to split every bar into its parts in the chart palette,
with a legend.

<Preview>
  <BarChartExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { BarChart } from './bar-chart/BarChart';

const series = [
  { label: 'Shipped', tipLabel: 'shipped' },
  { label: 'Needed review', tipLabel: 'reviewed' },
  { label: 'Failed', tipLabel: 'failed' },
];

const ranges = [
  { key: 'w', label: 'Week', bars: [{ label: 'Mon', values: [42, 9, 2] }, /* ... */] },
  { key: 'm', label: 'Month', bars: [{ label: 'W1', values: [180, 40, 9] }, /* ... */] },
];

<BarChart label="Agent runs" series={series} ranges={ranges} defaultRange="w" unit="runs" stacked />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [BarChartComponent] -->
<BarChart
  label="Agent runs"
  [series]="series"
  [ranges]="ranges"
  defaultRange="w"
  unit="runs"
  [stacked]="true"
  (rangeChange)="onRange($event)"
></BarChart>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/bar_chart.dart';

BarChart(
  label: 'Agent runs',
  unit: 'runs',
  stacked: true,
  series: const [
    BarChartSeries(label: 'Shipped', tipLabel: 'shipped'),
    BarChartSeries(label: 'Needed review', tipLabel: 'reviewed'),
    BarChartSeries(label: 'Failed', tipLabel: 'failed'),
  ],
  ranges: const [
    BarChartRange(key: 'w', label: 'Week', bars: [
      BarChartBar(label: 'Mon', values: [42, 9, 2]),
      // one BarChartBar per bar
    ]),
    BarChartRange(key: 'm', label: 'Month', bars: [
      BarChartBar(label: 'W1', values: [180, 40, 9]),
    ]),
  ],
  defaultRange: 'w',
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | The name over the big number, like "Agent runs". |
| `series` | `BarChartSeries[]` | What each part of a bar means, in order. The readout breaks each bar down by these. Each has a `label`, an optional `tipLabel` and, when stacked, an optional `color`. |
| `stacked` | `boolean` | Draws each bar as a stack of its parts in the palette's colours, with a legend. Off by default: one bar in the accent, with the breakdown in the readout. |
| `ranges` | `BarChartRange[]` | One set of bars per range. Each has a `key`, a `label` and `bars: { label, values }[]`. With more than one, a switch picks between them. |
| `range` | `string` | Key of the range shown. Leave it out to let the switch change it. |
| `defaultRange` | `string` | The range shown first when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first range. |
| `onRangeChange` | `(key: string) => void` | Called with the new key when the switch changes. |
| `unit` | `string` | What the values count, like "runs" in "66 runs". |
| `format` | `(n: number) => string` | Writes a value. Defaults to whole numbers like `1,240`. |

Each `BarChartBar` carries `values: number[]` — one per series, stacked from the bottom — so the
series order sets the order of the parts, the legend and the breakdown in the readout.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The bars
use the chart palette (`--vo-c1..c6`: the accent, then violet, orange, green…) unless a series sets
its own `color`; the readout tooltip sits on the ink tone and the big number and labels read from the
foreground and muted tokens. In Soft the bars and tooltip are rounder.


# Browser session (/docs/components/browser-session)

A browser session shows the agent browsing the web for you: a small browser frame with the page it
is on, the steps it takes under it, and Pause and Take over. When a step waits for you — a cookie
banner in the way, say — it shows why and a button to let the agent go on. Take over hands the page
to you: its frame turns the accent colour, its controls become usable, and the button reads Hand
back.

<Preview>
  <BrowserSessionExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { BrowserSession } from './browser-session/BrowserSession';

<BrowserSession
  title="Pricing research"
  url="northwind.app/pricing"
  steps={[
    { label: 'Click "Pricing"', state: 'done' },
    { label: 'Read the plans table', state: 'waiting', detail: 'A cookie banner covers the table' },
  ]}
  ask={{ label: 'Allow closing it', onAllow: allow }}
>
  <div className="vo-bws-pg">{/* the page, drawn as a wireframe */}</div>
</BrowserSession>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [BrowserSessionComponent] -->
<BrowserSession
  title="Pricing research"
  url="northwind.app/pricing"
  [steps]="steps"
  [ask]="cookieAsk"
>
  <ng-template #page>
    <div class="vo-bws-pg"><!-- the page, drawn as a wireframe --></div>
  </ng-template>
</BrowserSession>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/browser_session.dart';

BrowserSession(
  title: 'Pricing research',
  url: 'northwind.app/pricing',
  steps: const [
    BrowserStep(label: 'Click "Pricing"', state: BrowserStepState.done),
    BrowserStep(label: 'Read the plans table', state: BrowserStepState.waiting, detail: 'A cookie banner covers the table'),
  ],
  ask: BrowserAsk(label: 'Allow closing it', onAllow: allow),
  page: const PricingWireframe(),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | What the agent is browsing for, like "Pricing research". |
| `url` | `string` | The address bar: the page's address, or the search being typed. |
| `search` | `boolean` | Marks `url` as a search, with a magnifier instead of the padlock. |
| `steps` | `BrowserStep[]` | The steps the agent takes. Each has a `label`, a `state` of `queued`, `running`, `waiting` or `done`, and an optional `detail`. |
| `cursor` | `object` | The agent's own pointer, in pixels from the page's top left. Hidden while you have control. |
| `ask` | `object` | While a step waits: the button that lets the agent go on. Has a `label` and `onAllow`. |
| `paused` / `defaultPaused` | `boolean` | Pause holds the agent where it is. Leave `paused` out to let the button toggle it. |
| `inControl` / `defaultInControl` | `boolean` | Take over hands the page to you. Leave `inControl` out to let the button toggle it. |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds to show as m:ss. Leave it out to let the clock count while browsing. |
| `status` | `string` | The line under the title. Defaults to a status word, then the clock. |
| `summary` | `string` | Shown under the steps once every step is done. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The page
is drawn small, with real words where they matter and grey lines for the rest; a price the agent has
taken is marked in the accent fill. While you have control the frame turns the accent colour. In
Blueprint the frame and chips are squared off.


# Buttons (/docs/components/buttons)

A button is a pill in one of the variants — `primary` for the main action, `soft` and `line` for the
rest, `ghost` for the quietest — in three sizes. Return a promise from `onClick` and the button runs
itself: it shows the busy face until the promise settles, then the done face. `ButtonCopy` copies
text and flashes a check.

<Preview>
  <ButtonsExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonCopy } from './buttons/Buttons';

<Button variant="primary">Primary</Button>
<Button variant="soft" size="sm">Small</Button>

// return a promise and the button runs busy -> done by itself
<Button variant="primary" busyLabel="Publishing" doneLabel="Published" onClick={publish}>
  Publish
</Button>
<Button variant="accent" success onClick={save}>Save</Button>

<ButtonCopy text="https://example.com" label="Copy link" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ButtonComponent, ButtonCopyComponent] -->
<VoButton variant="primary">Primary</VoButton>
<VoButton variant="soft" size="sm">Small</VoButton>

<VoButton variant="primary" busyLabel="Publishing" doneLabel="Published" (click)="publish()">
  Publish
</VoButton>
<VoButton variant="accent" [success]="true" (click)="save()">Save</VoButton>

<VoButtonCopy text="https://example.com" label="Copy link" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/buttons.dart';

const Button('Primary', variant: ButtonVariant.primary),
const Button('Small', variant: ButtonVariant.soft, size: ButtonSize.sm),

Button('Publish', variant: ButtonVariant.primary, busyLabel: 'Publishing', doneLabel: 'Published', onClick: publish),
Button('Save', variant: ButtonVariant.accent, success: true, onClick: save),

ButtonCopy(text: 'https://example.com', label: 'Copy link'),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `primary \| accent \| soft \| line \| ghost \| ink` | The style. Left out, a plain pill. `ink` is the old name for `primary`. |
| `size` | `sm \| md \| lg` | The three sizes; `md` is the default. |
| `icon` | `IconName` | An icon before the label. |
| `onClick` | `(e) => void \| Promise<unknown>` | Return a promise and the button runs busy then done by itself. |
| `busy` / `done` | `boolean` | Drive the busy or done face yourself. Clicks are ignored while shown. |
| `busyLabel` / `doneLabel` | `ReactNode` | The labels on the busy and done faces. |
| `busyGlyph` | `spin \| think` | The busy glyph: a spinner, or the agent's turning dots. |
| `success` | `boolean` | The done face turns green. |
| `pressed` | `boolean` | For a toggle: whether it is on, as `aria-pressed`. |
| `tip` / `kbd` | `string` | A tooltip, with an optional shortcut after it. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
variants read against the theme's accent and surface tokens; in Soft the pills are rounder and
softer, and the busy and done faces blur across in either theme.


# Card (/docs/components/card)

A card is a surface you build other components onto. It has an optional header (a `title`, a
`subtitle` and an end `action` slot), a body of whatever you put inside, and an optional `footer`
of actions. `pad` sets the inset; set `interactive` (or pass `onClick`) and the whole card becomes a
hit target that lifts on hover, takes focus, and fires on Enter or Space.

<Preview>
  <CardExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Card } from './card/Card';
import { Badge } from './badge/Badge';

<Card
  title="Nightly run"
  subtitle="Finished 4 minutes ago"
  action={<Badge tone="success">Live</Badge>}
  footer={<>
    <button className="vo-pill vo-ghost vo-sm">Dismiss</button>
    <button className="vo-pill vo-sm" data-variant="accent">Open run</button>
  </>}
>
  <p>Drop anything in the body.</p>
</Card>

<Card interactive onClick={() => open()}>
  <span className="vo-crd-t">Interactive card</span>
</Card>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [CardComponent, BadgeComponent] -->
<Card title="Nightly run" subtitle="Finished 4 minutes ago">
  <Badge card-action tone="success">Live</Badge>
  <p>Drop anything in the body.</p>
  <button card-footer class="vo-pill vo-ghost vo-sm">Dismiss</button>
  <button card-footer class="vo-pill vo-sm" data-variant="accent">Open run</button>
</Card>

<Card [interactive]="true" (clicked)="open()">
  <span class="vo-crd-t">Interactive card</span>
</Card>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/card.dart';
import 'components/badge.dart';

VoCard(
  title: 'Nightly run',
  subtitle: 'Finished 4 minutes ago',
  action: const Badge('Live', tone: BadgeTone.success),
  footer: [
    TextButton(onPressed: dismiss, child: const Text('Dismiss')),
    FilledButton(onPressed: open, child: const Text('Open run')),
  ],
  child: const Text('Drop anything in the body.'),
),

VoCard(
  interactive: true,
  onTap: open,
  child: const Text('Interactive card'),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | A title shown in the header. |
| `subtitle` | `ReactNode` | A subtitle under the title. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | An end slot in the header, aligned right (a badge, a menu button). |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | A footer of actions below the body. |
| `footerAlign` | `start \| end \| between` | How the footer's actions align. `end` by default. |
| `pad` | `none \| sm \| md` | Inset for header, body and footer. `md` by default. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | Makes the whole card a hit target that lifts, takes focus and fires on Enter/Space. |
| `onClick` / `clicked` / `onTap` | `callback` | Fired when an interactive card is activated. Setting it implies `interactive`. |

In Angular the header end slot and the footer are projected with the `card-action` and `card-footer`
attributes; in Flutter `action` is a widget and `footer` a list of widgets.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In Soft
the card has rounded corners and floats on a soft shadow; in Blueprint it is squared off with a
hairline instead of the float. An interactive card lifts on hover and keeps a visible focus ring;
with reduced motion it still restyles but does not travel.


# Change review (/docs/components/change-review)

Change review walks a set of changed `files` as a diff. Pick a file in the list, then **keep** or
**undo** each hunk on its own — Keep turns to a green done chip, an undone hunk's Undo sits on the
surface, and pressing either again takes the choice back. **Keep all** settles the current file and
steps to the next; **Undo all** settles it in place. Hover a line to reveal its comment button and
ask the agent about that change. The file list rolls each file up to kept, undone or part-decided.

<Preview>
  <ChangeReviewExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ChangeReview, type ChangedFile } from './change-review/ChangeReview';

const files: ChangedFile[] = [
  {
    name: 'PricingCard.tsx',
    path: 'src/PricingCard.tsx',
    hunks: [
      {
        title: 'Use the shared button',
        lines: [
          { kind: 'ctx', line: 14, text: '  return (' },
          { kind: 'del', line: 15, text: '    <button className="cta-old">' },
          { kind: 'add', line: 15, text: '    <Button variant="primary">' },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
];

<ChangeReview
  files={files}
  onDecisionsChange={(d) => console.log(d)}
  onComment={(c) => ask(c.text)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ChangeReviewComponent] -->
files: ChangedFile[] = [
  {
    name: 'PricingCard.tsx', path: 'src/PricingCard.tsx',
    hunks: [{ title: 'Use the shared button', lines: [
      { kind: 'ctx', line: 14, text: '  return (' },
      { kind: 'del', line: 15, text: '    <button className="cta-old">' },
      { kind: 'add', line: 15, text: '    <Button variant="primary">' },
    ] }],
  },
];

<ChangeReview
  [files]="files"
  (decisionsChange)="onDecisions($event)"
  (comment)="ask($event.text)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/change_review.dart';

ChangeReview(
  files: const [
    ChangedFile(
      name: 'PricingCard.tsx',
      path: 'src/PricingCard.tsx',
      hunks: [
        Hunk(title: 'Use the shared button', lines: [
          DiffLine(kind: DiffKind.ctx, line: 14, text: '  return ('),
          DiffLine(kind: DiffKind.del, line: 15, text: '    <button className="cta-old">'),
          DiffLine(kind: DiffKind.add, line: 15, text: '    <Button variant="primary">'),
        ]),
      ],
    ),
  ],
  onDecisionsChange: (d) => debugPrint('$d'),
  onComment: (c) => ask(c.text),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | `ChangedFile[]` | The files to review. Each has a `name`, an optional `path` and its `hunks`. |
| `file` | `number` | The file shown on the right, by index (controlled). |
| `defaultFile` | `number` | The file shown first when uncontrolled. Defaults to `0`. |
| `onFileChange` | `(index) => void` | Called when the shown file changes. |
| `decisions` | `Record<string, 'kept' \| 'undone'>` | Kept or undone, by hunk key (controlled). |
| `defaultDecisions` | `Record<string, 'kept' \| 'undone'>` | Starting decisions when uncontrolled. |
| `onDecisionsChange` | `(decisions) => void` | Called when any hunk's decision changes. |
| `onComment` | `(comment) => void` | Called when the person asks the agent about a line. Without a question it sends "Why this change?". |
| `title` | `string` | Header over the file list. Defaults to `"N files changed"`. |

### `ChangedFile` / `Hunk` / `DiffLine` [#changedfile--hunk--diffline]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file.name` | `string` | Like `"PricingCard.tsx"`. Its extension becomes the type label. |
| `file.path` | `string` | Shown above the diff. Defaults to the name. |
| `hunk.title` | `string` | What the change does, like `"Use the shared button"`. |
| `hunk.key` | `string` | Identifies the hunk in `decisions`. Defaults to `"<file name>#<index>"`. |
| `line.kind` | `add \| del \| ctx` | `add` and `del` lines are coloured; `ctx` lines are unchanged context. |
| `line.line` | `number` | The line number shown in the gutter. |
| `line.text` | `string` | The line's text. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). Added and
removed lines take the ok and bad tints; a hunk's Keep reads as the accent on a tint of itself, and
turns to the green done chip once kept — all from the theme tokens. The comment box uses the field
tokens, becoming a squircle in Blueprint where the browser supports it.


# Citation hover card (/docs/components/citation-hover-card)

An answer with numbered citations. Hovering, focusing or tapping one shows its source in a small card
underneath — the coloured mark and site, the title, the passage the answer relies on (with the part
that matters highlighted) and a link. The card rises in place; moving to another citation replays the
entrance. It takes the answer `text` (where `[n]` cites source n and a blank line starts a new
paragraph) and the list of `sources`.

<Preview>
  <CitationHoverCardExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { CitationHoverCard, type CitationHoverCardSource } from './citation-hover-card/CitationHoverCard';

const sources: CitationHoverCardSource[] = [
  {
    mark: 'B',
    color: '#4a5a8a',
    site: 'baymard.com',
    title: 'Pricing page UX benchmark',
    quote: <>Those leading with the annual plan saw <mark>a 12 to 20% higher rate</mark>.</>,
    meta: 'Read 4 days ago',
  },
];

<CitationHoverCard
  text="Teams that show the annual price first convert better[1]."
```
