```tsx
  sources={sources}
  onOpenSource={(s, i) => console.log(s.site, i)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [CitationHoverCardComponent] -->
sources: CitationHoverCardSource[] = [
  {
    mark: 'B', color: '#4a5a8a', site: 'baymard.com',
    title: 'Pricing page UX benchmark',
    quote: 'Those leading with the annual plan saw <mark>a 12 to 20% higher rate</mark>.',
    meta: 'Read 4 days ago',
  },
];

<CitationHoverCard
  [text]="'Teams that show the annual price first convert better[1].'"
  [sources]="sources"
  (openSource)="onOpen($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/citation_hover_card.dart';

CitationHoverCard(
  text: 'Teams that show the annual price first convert better[1].',
  sources: const [
    CitationHoverCardSource(
      mark: 'B',
      color: Color(0xFF4A5A8A),
      site: 'baymard.com',
      title: 'Pricing page UX benchmark',
      quote: 'Those leading with the annual plan saw a 12 to 20% higher rate.',
      highlight: 'a 12 to 20% higher rate',
      meta: 'Read 4 days ago',
    ),
  ],
  onOpenSource: (source, index) => debugPrint(source.site),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | The answer. `[n]` cites source n; a blank line starts a new paragraph. |
| `sources` | `CitationHoverCardSource[]` | The sources behind the citations (source n is `sources[n − 1]`). |
| `openLabel` | `string` | The link in the card's corner. Defaults to `Open source`. |
| `open` | `number \| null` | Opens a source's card from outside (`0` is the first), or closes it with `null`. Hover, focus and taps still work. |
| `onOpenSource` | `(source, index) => void` | Called when the card's link is clicked, with the source and its index. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(index \| null) => void` | Called when a card opens or closes, with the source's index, or `null`. |
| `source.mark` | `string` | One or two letters on the source's coloured mark, like `B`. |
| `source.color` | `string` | The mark's colour, like `#4a5a8a` or `var(--vo-pm)`. |
| `source.site` | `string` | Where it comes from, like `baymard.com` or `Drive`. |
| `source.title` | `string` | The source's title. |
| `source.quote` | `ReactNode` | The passage the answer relies on. Wrap the part that matters in `<mark>`. |
| `source.meta` | `string` | The quiet line in the corner, like `Read 4 days ago`. |
| `source.href` | `string` | Opens in a new tab from the card's link. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card sits
on a surface with the pop shadow; the citation chips use the hover and accent tokens, the quote's accent
rule uses `--vo-accent-mark` and its highlight uses the selection tint, so it all reads against the
stage. In Soft the chips and card are rounder.


# Code viewer (/docs/components/code-viewer)

The code the agent wrote, across one or more files. The lines it changed are marked — their
number turns green and the line gets a wash — and the `+N changed` count in the header follows the
open file. Click a line and the agent explains it: a note folds open under the line, reads for a
moment, then crossfades to what it says. The copy button copies the open file's text.

<Preview>
  <CodeViewerExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { CodeViewer, type CodeFile } from './code-viewer/CodeViewer';

const files: CodeFile[] = [
  {
    name: 'PlanCard.tsx',
    lines: [
      { code: [['k', 'export function'], ' ', ['f', 'PlanCard'], '() {'] },
      {
        code: [['tg', '  <Button '], ['at', 'variant'], '=', ['s', '"primary"'], ['tg', '/>']],
        changed: true,
        note: 'Swapped the custom button for the shared one.',
      },
      { code: '}' },
    ],
  },
];

<CodeViewer files={files} onCopy={(text) => navigator.clipboard.writeText(text)} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [CodeViewerComponent] -->
files: CodeFile[] = [
  {
    name: 'PlanCard.tsx',
    lines: [
      { code: [['k', 'export function'], ' ', ['f', 'PlanCard'], '() {'] },
      { code: [['tg', '  <Button />']], changed: true, note: 'Shared button now.' },
      { code: '}' },
    ],
  },
];

<CodeViewer [files]="files" (copy)="onCopy($event)" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/code_viewer.dart';

CodeViewer(
  files: [
    CodeFile(
      name: 'PlanCard.tsx',
      lines: [
        CodeLine(pieces: [
          CodePiece('export function ', CodeToken.k),
          CodePiece('PlanCard', CodeToken.f),
          CodePiece('() {'),
        ]),
        CodeLine(
          pieces: [CodePiece('  <Button />', CodeToken.tg)],
          changed: true,
          note: 'Shared button now.',
        ),
        CodeLine.text('}'),
      ],
    ),
  ],
  onCopy: (text) {},
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | `CodeFile[]` | The files the agent changed. Each has a `name` and `lines`. |
| `file` | `string` | The open file, by name. Leave it out to let the tabs switch it. |
| `defaultFile` | `string` | The file open at first when `file` is not controlled. |
| `onFileChange` | `(name) => void` | Called with the name of the file the tabs switch to. |
| `line` | `number \| null` | The line whose note is open (0 is the first), or `null`. Leave it out to let a click open it. |
| `defaultLine` | `number \| null` | The line open at first when `line` is not controlled. |
| `onLineChange` | `(line) => void` | Called with the line whose note opened, or `null` when it closed. |
| `delay` | `number` | How long a note says "Reading the line" before it answers, in ms. Defaults to `600`. |
| `unchangedNote` | `string` | The note for a line the agent didn't change and has nothing to say about. |
| `onCopy` | `(text) => void` | Called with the file's text when it is copied. |
| `CodeLine.code` | `string \| CodePiece[]` | The line as plain text, or as `[token, text]` pieces to highlight. |
| `CodeLine.changed` | `boolean` | The agent changed this line: its number turns green and the line gets a wash. |
| `CodeLine.note` | `string` | What the agent says about the line when you click it. |

The highlight tokens are `k` keyword, `s` string, `f` function, `cm` comment, `tg` tag and `at`
attribute.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The panel
sits on a surface; the changed-line wash comes from the `ok` token, the open line and its note from
the selection tint, and the syntax colours from the shared highlight tokens, so the code reads the
same against either theme.


# Composer (/docs/components/composer)

The composer is the box you write to the agent in — not a plain field but a small component on a
surface. Text grows as you type; attachments load as chips above it and hold Send until they are
ready (a failed one shows in red with a Try again button). Two menus set what the agent works on
(`contexts`) and what it may do (`modes`), a microphone swaps the toolbar for a dictation bar, and
Send fires `onSubmit` and clears the box. `value`, `attachments`, `context` and `mode` are
controllable — leave the matching input out to let the composer keep that piece itself.

<Preview>
  <ComposerExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Composer } from './composer/Composer';

<Composer
  contexts={[
    { value: 'pricing', label: 'Pricing v4', detail: 'Figma, 6 frames', icon: 'figma' },
    { value: 'marketing', label: 'Marketing site', detail: 'Code, main branch', icon: 'code' },
  ]}
  defaultContext="pricing"
  onSubmit={({ text, attachments }) => send(text, attachments)}
  onDictate={startListening}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ComposerComponent] -->
<Composer
  [contexts]="contexts"
  defaultContext="pricing"
  (send)="onSend($event)"
  (dictate)="startListening()"
/>
```

```ts
contexts: ComposerOption[] = [
  { value: 'pricing', label: 'Pricing v4', detail: 'Figma, 6 frames', icon: 'figma' },
  { value: 'marketing', label: 'Marketing site', detail: 'Code, main branch', icon: 'term' },
];
onSend(m: ComposerMessage) { /* m.text, m.attachments */ }
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/composer.dart';

Composer(
  contexts: const [
    ComposerOption(value: 'pricing', label: 'Pricing v4', detail: 'Figma, 6 frames', icon: Icons.dashboard_outlined),
    ComposerOption(value: 'marketing', label: 'Marketing site', detail: 'Code, main branch', icon: Icons.terminal),
  ],
  defaultContext: 'pricing',
  onSubmit: (m) => send(m.text, m.attachments),
  onDictate: startListening,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string` | The text in the box. Leave `value` out to let the composer keep it. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | Called as the text changes. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | The placeholder text. Becomes `Listening…` while dictating. |
| `onSubmit` | `({ text, attachments }) => void` | Called when the person sends. The box clears itself afterwards. |
| `busy` / `onStop` | `boolean` / `() => void` | The agent is answering: Send turns into Stop, which calls `onStop`. |
| `thread` | `ReactNode` | The conversation shown above the box. |
| `attachments` / `defaultAttachments` | `ComposerAttachment[]` | Chips above the text. `loading` holds Send; `error` shows red with Try again. |
| `onAttachmentsChange` | `(attachments) => void` | Called when a chip is removed. |
| `addOptions` / `onAdd` | `ComposerOption[]` / `(value) => void` | What the attach menu offers, and the pick. |
| `onRetry` | `(key) => void` | Called by Try again on a failed attachment. |
| `contexts` / `context` / `onContextChange` | `ComposerOption[]` / `string` | What the agent works on. The chip only shows when there are some. |
| `modes` / `mode` / `onModeChange` | `ComposerOption[]` / `string` | What the agent may do. Defaults to Ask, Edit and Plan. |
| `onDictate` | `() => void` | Called by the microphone. The mic button only shows when this is set. |
| `dictating` / `dictationSeconds` | `boolean` / `number` | Swaps the toolbar for the dictation bar and the clock it shows. |
| `onDictationEnd` | `(keep) => void` | Called by Cancel (`false`, text goes back) or Done (`true`, text stays). |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The box
sits on a surface with a soft shadow and the shared tokens drive its chips, menus and the accent
Send button, so it reads against the stage; in Soft the box and its pills are rounder.


# Context meter (/docs/components/context-meter)

A context meter is a pill with a ring that shows how full the context window is. It opens a panel
with one bar split by kind, a legend whose rows list what is in each part, and a Compact button
that summarises older turns to free room. The ring turns orange past a warning share, and a message
line fades in with a warning or a result.

<Preview>
  <ContextMeterExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ContextMeter } from './context-meter/ContextMeter';

<ContextMeter
  limit={200000}
  parts={[
    { key: 'files', label: 'Files', tokens: 56200, items: 'PricingCard.tsx 18.2k, tokens.css 6.1k' },
    { key: 'tools', label: 'Tool output', tokens: 41800 },
    { key: 'chat', label: 'Chat', tokens: 32100 },
  ]}
  onCompact={async () => summarise()}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ContextMeterComponent] -->
<ContextMeter
  [limit]="200000"
  [parts]="parts"
  (compact)="summarise()"
></ContextMeter>

// parts: ContextPart[] = [
//   { key: 'files', label: 'Files', tokens: 56200, items: 'PricingCard.tsx 18.2k, tokens.css 6.1k' },
//   { key: 'tools', label: 'Tool output', tokens: 41800 },
//   { key: 'chat', label: 'Chat', tokens: 32100 },
// ];
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/context_meter.dart';

ContextMeter(
  limit: 200000,
  parts: const [
    ContextPart(key: 'files', label: 'Files', tokens: 56200, items: 'PricingCard.tsx 18.2k, tokens.css 6.1k'),
    ContextPart(key: 'tools', label: 'Tool output', tokens: 41800),
    ContextPart(key: 'chat', label: 'Chat', tokens: 32100),
  ],
  onCompact: () async => summarise(),
)
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parts` | `ContextPart[]` | What fills the context. Each has a `key`, a `label`, its `tokens`, an optional `color`, and optional `items` shown on hover. |
| `limit` | `number` | The size of the context window, in tokens, like 200000. |
| `warnAt` | `number` | From this share of the limit (0 to 1) the ring turns orange. Defaults to 0.85. |
| `message` | `string` | A line under the legend. Crossfades when it changes. |
| `messageTone` | `warn \| ok` | warn shows it in orange with a warning sign, ok in green with a check. |
| `compacted` | `boolean` | Set once compacted: the button turns into Undo. |
| `hint` | `string` | The quiet line beside the button. Defaults to "Summarises older turns". |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the panel is open. Leave it out to let the pill toggle it. |
| `onCompact` / `compact` | `callback` | Called by Compact. Return a promise and the button spins until it settles. |
| `onUndo` / `undo` | `callback` | Called by Undo once compacted. |
| `onOpenChange` / `openChange` | `callback` | Fires when the panel opens or shuts. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the pill, the bar and the panel are squared off; in Soft they are rounded. The ring takes
the accent mark and the warning mark past the warning share, and the bar segments take the part
palette (blue, teal, violet, grey) from the tokens unless a part sets its own color.


# Date Picker (/docs/components/date-picker)

A date picker is a field that opens a calendar. Quick picks (**Today**, **Tomorrow**, **In a week**)
sit under a box that understands plain English — type "next friday" or "in 2 weeks" and it picks the
day straight away. The arrow keys move the focus a day or a week, across months too.

Pass **`range`** and the same component becomes a range picker: two months side by side with
ready-made ranges (last 7 days, last 30 days, this quarter), a live preview of the span as you hover,
and **Apply**.

<Preview>
  <DatePickerExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from './date-picker/DatePicker';

const [day, setDay] = useState<Date | null>(null);

// single day
<DatePicker value={day} onValueChange={setDay} />

// range mode: two months, presets, Apply
const [range, setRange] = useState({ start: null, end: null });
<DatePicker range rangeValue={range} onRangeChange={setRange} onApply={r => save(r)} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [DatePickerComponent] -->
<DatePicker [value]="day" (valueChange)="day = $event" />

<DatePicker range [rangeValue]="range"
  (rangeChange)="range = $event" (apply)="save($event)" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/date_picker.dart';

DatePicker(
  value: day,
  onValueChange: (d) => setState(() => day = d),
),

DatePicker(
  range: true,
  rangeValue: range,
  onRangeChange: (r) => setState(() => range = r),
  onApply: (r) => save(r),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `range` | `boolean` | Pick a start and end across two months instead of a single day. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `Date \| null` | The picked day (single mode). Pass `value` with `onValueChange` for a controlled field. |
| `onValueChange` | `(date: Date \| null) => void` | Fires with the picked day (single mode). |
| `rangeValue` / `defaultRangeValue` | `{ start: Date \| null; end: Date \| null }` | The picked range (range mode). |
| `onRangeChange` | `(range) => void` | Fires with the range as it is built (range mode). |
| `onApply` | `(range: { start: Date; end: Date }) => void` | Fires when **Apply** is pressed (range mode). |
| `month` / `defaultMonth` | `Date` | The month on show, as its first day. In range mode this is the left calendar. |
| `presets` | `{ label: string; days: number }[]` | Quick picks under the text box (single mode). |
| `rangePresets` | `{ key, label, range }[]` | The side list of ready-made ranges (range mode). |
| `parse` | `(text, today) => Date \| null` | Turns typed text into a day. Defaults to plain English (single mode). |
| `today` | `Date` | The day marked with a dot. Pass one when rendering on a server. |
| `weekStartsOn` | `0 \| 1` | `1` starts weeks on Monday (the default), `0` on Sunday. |
| `locale` | `string` | Used for the month name, weekday letters and the default format. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The field,
popover and calendar take the active theme's surface and field-line colors; the picked day and the
range span use the accent. Field radius follows `--vo-r-field` (squared off in Blueprint, rounder in
Soft). All driven by the shared `--vo-*` tokens.


# Decision prompt (/docs/components/decision-prompt)

The agent asks a few quick questions before it starts — one at a time, with a row of
options for each. Number keys pick, **Enter** continues and **Skip** lets the agent decide.
Once every question is answered the body settles into a summary and a line that says the
agent is getting going; pass `started` to settle that line with a check.

<Preview>
  <DecisionPromptExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { DecisionPrompt, type DecisionQuestion } from './decision-prompt/DecisionPrompt';

const questions: DecisionQuestion[] = [
  {
    question: 'Which frames should the agent redesign?',
    label: 'Frames',
    options: [
      { label: 'Pricing only', detail: '1 frame' },
      { label: 'Pricing and checkout', detail: '3 frames' },
      { label: 'The whole flow', detail: '9 frames' },
    ],
  },
  // …more questions
];

<DecisionPrompt
  questions={questions}
  startLabel="Starting the redesign"
  onComplete={(answers) => run(answers)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [DecisionPromptComponent] -->
questions: DecisionQuestion[] = [
  {
    question: 'Which frames should the agent redesign?',
    label: 'Frames',
    options: [
      { label: 'Pricing only', detail: '1 frame' },
      { label: 'Pricing and checkout', detail: '3 frames' },
      { label: 'The whole flow', detail: '9 frames' },
    ],
  },
];

<DecisionPrompt
  [questions]="questions"
  startLabel="Starting the redesign"
  (complete)="run($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/decision_prompt.dart';

DecisionPrompt(
  questions: const [
    DecisionQuestion(
      question: 'Which frames should the agent redesign?',
      label: 'Frames',
      options: [
        DecisionOption(label: 'Pricing only', detail: '1 frame'),
        DecisionOption(label: 'Pricing and checkout', detail: '3 frames'),
        DecisionOption(label: 'The whole flow', detail: '9 frames'),
      ],
    ),
  ],
  startLabel: 'Starting the redesign',
  onComplete: (answers) => run(answers),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `questions` | `DecisionQuestion[]` | The questions the agent asks, in order. |
| `answers` | `(number \| null)[]` | The answers so far — an option's index, or `null` for a skipped question. Leave it out to let Continue and Skip fill it. |
| `defaultAnswers` | `(number \| null)[]` | The answers the prompt starts with when uncontrolled. |
| `onAnswersChange` | `(answers) => void` | Called whenever the answers change (a pick, or a skip). Angular: `(answersChange)`. |
| `onComplete` | `(answers) => void` | Called once every question is answered. Angular: `(complete)`. |
| `skippedLabel` | `string` | What the summary says for a skipped question. Defaults to `Agent decides`. |
| `startLabel` | `string` | The line under the summary while the agent gets going. Defaults to `Starting`. |
| `started` | `boolean` | The agent has got going: the summary line settles with a check. |
| `startedLabel` | `string` | What that line says once started. Defaults to `startLabel`. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |
| `question.label` | `string` | A short name for the question in the summary, like "Scope". |
| `option.detail` | `string` | Quiet text at the end of the row, like "3 frames" or "Recommended". |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). It sits
flat in the chat thread by default; set `bare` to `false` to give it its own surface card. The active
step dot and the picked option's key badge take the accent tint, so the prompt reads against the stage
in either theme; in Soft the card, options and pills are rounder.


# Design review (/docs/components/design-review)

Something the agent made, laid out for sign-off. One column runs the `checks`; the other holds the
`messages` — a teammate's verdict, the agent's reply — oldest first. The `phase` carries it from
`review` to `approved` (the Ship button turns on), then `shipping`, and finally `live` or
`scheduled`. Beside the Ship button a menu picks how it ships from your `options`.

<Preview>
  <DesignReviewExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { DesignReview } from './design-review/DesignReview';

<DesignReview
  title="Pricing page v4"
  subtitle="6 screens · sent for review by the design agent"
  checks={[
    { label: 'Visual diff', state: 'ok', note: '2 of 6 screens changed' },
    { label: 'Library tokens', state: 'ok', note: 'All from the library' },
    { label: 'Contrast', state: 'run' },
  ]}
  messages={[
    { author: { name: 'Maya Kim', initials: 'MK' }, verdict: { label: 'Changes requested', tone: 'warn' },
      text: 'Start the plan toggle on yearly.' },
  ]}
  phase="approved"
  note="Waiting on Maya"
  onShip={(o) => ship(o.key)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [DesignReviewComponent] -->
<DesignReview
  title="Pricing page v4"
  subtitle="6 screens · sent for review by the design agent"
  [checks]="checks"
  [messages]="messages"
  phase="approved"
  note="Waiting on Maya"
  (shipClick)="ship($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/design_review.dart';

DesignReview(
  title: 'Pricing page v4',
  subtitle: '6 screens · sent for review by the design agent',
  checks: const [
    ReviewCheck(label: 'Visual diff', state: ReviewCheckState.ok, note: '2 of 6 screens changed'),
    ReviewCheck(label: 'Contrast', state: ReviewCheckState.run),
  ],
  messages: const [
    ReviewMessage(
      author: ReviewAuthor(name: 'Maya Kim', initials: 'MK'),
      verdict: ReviewVerdict(label: 'Changes requested', tone: VerdictTone.warn),
      text: 'Start the plan toggle on yearly.',
    ),
  ],
  phase: ReviewPhase.approved,
  note: 'Waiting on Maya',
  onShip: (o) => ship(o.key),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | What is up for review, like "Pricing page v4". |
| `subtitle` | `string` | The line under the title. |
| `icon` | `IconName` | The header mark. Defaults to `palette`. |
| `checks` | `ReviewCheck[]` | The Checks column: `{ label; state: wait \| run \| ok \| bad; note? }`. |
| `messages` | `ReviewMessage[]` | The review so far, oldest first: who, an optional verdict tag, and the text. |
| `phase` | `review \| approved \| shipping \| live \| scheduled` | Where it is. `approved` turns the Ship button on; `live`/`scheduled` replace the buttons with a done line. |
| `note` | `string` | The line beside the Ship button, like "Waiting on Maya". |
| `waitingLabel` | `string` | Shown in the review column before anyone has written. |
| `options` | `ShipOption[]` | The ways it can ship, picked from the menu beside the button. |
| `option` / `defaultOption` | `string` | The picked option key, controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `onOptionChange` | `(key) => void` | The picked ship option changed. |
| `onShip` | `(option) => void` | The Ship button was pressed, with the chosen option. |
| `doneLabel` | `string` | Replaces the chosen label on the done line once it is live or scheduled. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a `--vo-panel` surface; the header mark, the verdict tags and the checks' ok/bad glyphs all
take their colours from the theme tokens (`--vo-ok`, `--vo-warn`, `--vo-bad`, `--vo-pb`), and the
Ship button follows the accent, so the whole review reads against either theme. Once it is live the
header mark shifts to the ok tint.


# Design tuner (/docs/components/design-tuner)

A live preview beside a few sliders, with a button that hands the tuning to the agent. Drag a
slider — or arrow-key it — to tweak the sample card by hand, or press **Tune with agent** and it
walks each value to a target, turns the row it is moving accent, and drops a note on what it
changed. Each slider sets a `--vo-<key>` variable on the preview, so the card reshapes live.

<Preview>
  <DesignTunerExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { DesignTuner, type TunerParam } from './design-tuner/DesignTuner';

<DesignTuner
  title="Pricing card"
  status="Edited by you"
  actionLabel="Tune with agent"
  onValuesChange={(values) => console.log(values)}
  onTune={() => startAgentTune()}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [DesignTunerComponent] -->
<DesignTuner
  title="Pricing card"
  actionLabel="Tune with agent"
  (valuesChange)="onValues($event)"
  (tune_)="startAgentTune()"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/design_tuner.dart';

DesignTuner(
  title: 'Pricing card',
  onValuesChange: (values) => debugPrint('$values'),
  onTune: startAgentTune,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `params` | `TunerParam[]` | The sliders. Defaults to radius, padding, spacing and shadow for the sample card. |
| `values` | `Record<string, number>` | The value of each slider by key. Leave it out to let the sliders keep their own. |
| `onValuesChange` | `(values) => void` | Fires with the values by key whenever a slider or the agent moves one. |
| `title` | `string` | What is being tuned, like `"Pricing card"`. |
| `status` | `string` | Quiet line beside the title, like `"Edited by you"` or `"Agent is tuning"`. |
| `active` | `string` | Key of the slider the agent is moving now; its value turns the accent colour. |
| `tuning` | `boolean` | The agent is tuning: the button thinks and stops taking clicks. |
| `note` | `ReactNode` | What the agent changed and why, shown above the button. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | The button's label, like `"Tune with agent"` or `"Tune again"`. |
| `onTune` | `() => void` | Fires when the agent-tune button is pressed. |

A `TunerParam` is `{ key, label, min, max, value, unit?, decimals? }`: `key` names the `--vo-<key>`
variable the preview reads, `unit` is appended to whole numbers (like `px`), and `decimals` shows
and sets the value with that many decimals instead of rounding.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
preview sits on a chip-tinted stage; the slider fill and knob, the accent CTA and the agent's note
all draw from the theme tokens, and the sample card's own radius, padding, spacing and shadow are
exactly what the sliders drive. The agent respects `prefers-reduced-motion`, snapping to the tuned
values instead of walking them.


# Details panel (/docs/components/details-panel)

A details panel shows a record's properties in folding sections and lets you edit them in
place. Each `section` holds `rows`: a `select` row picks its value from a small menu (with a
coloured dot, an avatar or a plain chevron), a `number` row rolls to its new value, a `tags`
row carries labels and an optional add button, and a plain row just shows its `value`. The
accent flashes behind a value when it changes. A `copyValue` adds a copy button beside the
title.

<Preview>
  <DetailsPanelExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { DetailsPanel, type DetailsPanelSection } from './details-panel/DetailsPanel';

const sections: DetailsPanelSection[] = [
  {
    key: 'props',
    title: 'Properties',
    rows: [
      {
        key: 'status',
        label: 'Status',
        type: 'select',
        defaultValue: 'review',
        options: [
          { value: 'progress', label: 'In progress', color: 'var(--vo-py)' },
          { value: 'review', label: 'In review', color: 'var(--vo-accent)' },
          { value: 'shipped', label: 'Shipped', color: 'var(--vo-ok)' },
        ],
      },
      { key: 'tokens', label: 'Tokens', type: 'number', value: 184200 },
      { key: 'due', label: 'Due', value: 'Oct 24' },
    ],
  },
];

<DetailsPanel title="Pricing page redesign" kind="RUN" copyValue="run_8f2a" sections={sections} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [DetailsPanelComponent] -->
sections: DetailsPanelSection[] = [
  {
    key: 'props', title: 'Properties',
    rows: [
      { key: 'status', label: 'Status', type: 'select', defaultValue: 'review',
        options: [
          { value: 'progress', label: 'In progress', color: 'var(--vo-py)' },
          { value: 'review', label: 'In review', color: 'var(--vo-accent)' },
        ] },
      { key: 'tokens', label: 'Tokens', type: 'number', value: 184200 },
    ],
  },
];

<DetailsPanel
  title="Pricing page redesign"
  kind="RUN"
  copyValue="run_8f2a"
  [sections]="sections"
  (valueChange)="onChange($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/details_panel.dart';

DetailsPanel(
  title: 'Pricing page redesign',
  kind: 'RUN',
  copyValue: 'run_8f2a',
  sections: [
    DetailsPanelSection(
      key: 'props',
      title: 'Properties',
      rows: [
        DetailsPanelRow.select(
          key: 'status',
          label: 'Status',
          defaultValue: 'review',
          options: const [
            DetailsPanelOption(value: 'progress', label: 'In progress', color: Color(0xFF856404)),
            DetailsPanelOption(value: 'review', label: 'In review', color: Color(0xFF116FF8)),
          ],
        ),
        const DetailsPanelRow.number(key: 'tokens', label: 'Tokens', number: 184200),
        const DetailsPanelRow.text(key: 'due', label: 'Due', value: 'Oct 24'),
      ],
    ),
  ],
);
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The title at the top, like "Pricing page redesign". |
| `kind` | `string` | A short type tag before the title, like "RUN". |
| `copyValue` | `string` | Adds a copy button that copies this, like a run ID. |
| `copyLabel` | `string` | The copy button's tooltip. Defaults to "Copy run ID". |
| `sections` | `DetailsPanelSection[]` | The folding sections, each a `key`, a `title` and its `rows`. |
| `open` | `string[]` | Keys of the open sections. Leave it out to let the headers toggle them; every section starts open. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open) => void` | Called when the open sections change. |
| `row.type` | `text \| select \| number \| tags` | What the row shows. A plain `text` row is the default. |
| `select.options` | `{ value; label; detail?; color?; avatar? }[]` | The menu choices, with a dot (`color`), an `avatar` or a plain chevron. |
| `select.onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | Called when the row's value changes. |
| `number.value` | `number` | The value, which rolls into view and whenever it changes. |
| `number.format` | `(n) => string` | Turns the number into text. Defaults to a rounded number with thousands separators. |
| `tags.tags` | `{ label; tone? }[]` | The labels; `tone` tints a chip. Later tags enter with the panel. |
| `tags.onAdd` | `() => void` | Shows an add button after the labels and fires when it is pressed. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
panel sits on a surface; values hover and flash with the accent tint, dots and avatars take
the hue tokens, and the folding sections draw from the shared `fold` and popover tokens, so
everything reads against either theme. In Soft the panel, menus and chips are rounder.


# Donut chart (/docs/components/donut-chart)

A donut chart shows a whole split into parts: a ring of `segments` that draw in one by one, with a
legend beside it. Each segment takes a `label` and a `value`, and gets a colour from the chart
palette unless you pass one. The middle shows the total with its `label` and `unit`; hovering a
segment or its legend row highlights both and shows that one in the middle instead.

<Preview>
  <DonutChartExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { DonutChart } from './donut-chart/DonutChart';

const segments = [
  { label: 'Design reviews', value: 14.2 },
  { label: 'Code changes', value: 9.6 },
  { label: 'Research', value: 6.1 },
  { label: 'Other', value: 1.7, color: 'var(--vo-faint)' },
];

<DonutChart segments={segments} label="Agent time" unit="h" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [DonutChartComponent] -->
segments: DonutChartSegment[] = [
  { label: 'Design reviews', value: 14.2 },
  { label: 'Code changes', value: 9.6 },
  { label: 'Research', value: 6.1 },
  { label: 'Other', value: 1.7, color: 'var(--vo-faint)' },
];

<DonutChart [segments]="segments" label="Agent time" unit="h" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/donut_chart.dart';

DonutChart(
  segments: const [
    DonutChartSegment(label: 'Design reviews', value: 14.2),
    DonutChartSegment(label: 'Code changes', value: 9.6),
    DonutChartSegment(label: 'Research', value: 6.1),
    DonutChartSegment(label: 'Other', value: 1.7),
  ],
  label: 'Agent time',
  unit: 'h',
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `segments` | `DonutChartSegment[]` | The ring's parts. Each is `{ label, value, color? }`. |
| `label` | `string` | Under the total in the middle, like "Agent time". Defaults to `Total`. |
| `unit` | `string` | After every value, like `h` in "14.2h". |
| `format` | `(n: number) => string` | Writes a value. Defaults to one decimal, like `14.2`. |
| `active` | `number \| null` | Index of the highlighted segment, or `null`. Leave it out to let hovering highlight it. |
| `defaultActive` | `number \| null` | The highlight to start with when uncontrolled. |
| `onActiveChange` | `(index: number \| null) => void` | Fires when the highlighted segment changes (Angular: `activeChange`; Flutter: `onActiveChange`). |

A `DonutChartSegment` is `{ label: string; value: number; color?: string }`; `color` defaults to the
chart palette (`--vo-c1..c6`) in order.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). Segment
colours come from the chart palette tokens (`--vo-c1..c6`), the card sits on a surface, and the
legend hover tint and the centre text read from the theme tokens. The arcs sweep in and the total
counts up on load; with `prefers-reduced-motion` the ring appears already drawn.


# Draft review (/docs/components/draft-review)

An email the agent drafted, laid out like the email it is: who it goes to, the `subject`, the `body`
and any `attachments`. Check and edit it, then send now or later — the menu beside the button picks
`when` — or `discard` it. A `warning` can stop it before it sends, like an attachment the message
mentions but nothing attached, and after sending there is a short window to `undo`. The `phase` drives
what the footer shows.

<Preview>
  <DraftReviewExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { DraftReview } from './draft-review/DraftReview';

<DraftReview
  subtitle="After the pricing review with Maya"
  to={[{ name: 'Maya Kim', initials: 'MK', color: 'var(--vo-av-l)' }]}
  subject="Pricing v4: what changed"
  body={"Hi Maya,\n\nHere's what changed on the pricing page…"}
  phase="draft"
  onSend={(option) => send(option.key)}
  onDiscard={() => discard()}
  onUndo={() => bringBack()}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [DraftReviewComponent] -->
<DraftReview
  subtitle="After the pricing review with Maya"
  [to]="[{ name: 'Maya Kim', initials: 'MK', color: 'var(--vo-av-l)' }]"
  subject="Pricing v4: what changed"
  [body]="draftBody"
  phase="draft"
  (send)="onSend($event)"
  (discard)="onDiscard()"
  (undo)="onUndo()"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/draft_review.dart';

DraftReview(
  subtitle: 'After the pricing review with Maya',
  to: const [DraftRecipient(name: 'Maya Kim', initials: 'MK')],
  subject: 'Pricing v4: what changed',
  body: "Hi Maya,\n\nHere's what changed on the pricing page…",
  phase: DraftPhase.draft,
  onSend: (option) => send(option.key),
  onDiscard: () => discard(),
  onUndo: () => bringBack(),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The bold first line. Defaults to "Draft from the agent". |
| `subtitle` | `string` | The quieter line under the title. |
| `to` | `DraftRecipient[]` | Who it goes to: `{ name; initials?; color? }`. |
| `subject` | `string` | The subject line. Editable when `onSubjectChange` is set. |
| `body` | `string` | The message as the agent wrote it. Stays editable; read edits from `onBodyChange`. |
| `attachments` | `DraftAttachment[]` | Files on the draft: `{ name; size?; loading? }`. |
| `warning` | `{ text; actions }` | A problem to settle before it sends, with its own buttons. |
| `phase` | `draft \| sending \| undo \| sent \| scheduled \| discarded` | Drives what the footer shows. |
| `sendOptions` | `SendOption[]` | The "when to send" menu: `{ key; label; detail? }`. `now` sends straight away. |
| `sendOption` / `defaultSendOption` | `string` | The picked option's key, controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `undoLeft` | `number` | Seconds left to undo, shown while the phase is `undo`. |
| `onSend` | `(option) => void` | Called when Send (or Schedule) is pressed, with the chosen option. |
| `onDiscard` | `() => void` | Called by the Discard button. |
| `onUndo` | `() => void` | Takes it back: undoes a send, cancels a scheduled one, or brings back a discarded draft. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface with the card shadow; the warning uses the warn tint, a sent draft the ok tint, and
a scheduled one the blue "preview" tint — all from the theme tokens. In Soft the card, chips and pills
are rounder.


# Error recovery (/docs/components/error-recovery)

A run that hit an error, with the steps around it and a choice of how the agent should carry on.
Each `step` carries a `state` — `done`, `fail`, `run`, `wait`, `skip` or `hand` — that picks its
glyph, and an optional `note` under it that crossfades when it changes. The `options` are the ways
the agent can continue; pick one and press Continue, and the choices fold away.

<Preview>
  <ErrorRecoveryExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ErrorRecovery, type RecoveryStep } from './error-recovery/ErrorRecovery';

const steps: RecoveryStep[] = [
  { label: 'Pull 1,240 deals from the CRM', state: 'done', note: 'Done in 8s' },
  { label: 'Write to the Pipeline 2026 sheet', state: 'fail', note: 'Error 403: lost edit access' },
  { label: 'Post the summary in #sales', state: 'wait' },
];

<ErrorRecovery
  title="Sync the pipeline to Sheets"
  status="Stopped at step 2"
  steps={steps}
  options={[
    { value: 'retry', label: 'Ask for edit access, then retry' },
    { value: 'skip', label: 'Skip it and post the summary' },
    { value: 'hand', label: 'Hand it over to Maya' },
  ]}
  onContinue={(value) => carryOn(value)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ErrorRecoveryComponent] -->
steps: RecoveryStep[] = [
  { label: 'Pull 1,240 deals from the CRM', state: 'done', note: 'Done in 8s' },
  { label: 'Write to the Pipeline 2026 sheet', state: 'fail', note: 'Error 403: lost edit access' },
  { label: 'Post the summary in #sales', state: 'wait' },
];
options = [
  { value: 'retry', label: 'Ask for edit access, then retry' },
  { value: 'skip', label: 'Skip it and post the summary' },
  { value: 'hand', label: 'Hand it over to Maya' },
];

<ErrorRecovery
  title="Sync the pipeline to Sheets"
  status="Stopped at step 2"
  [steps]="steps"
  [options]="options"
  (continue)="carryOn($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/error_recovery.dart';

ErrorRecovery(
  title: 'Sync the pipeline to Sheets',
  status: 'Stopped at step 2',
  steps: const [
    RecoveryStep(label: 'Pull 1,240 deals from the CRM', state: RecoveryStepState.done, note: 'Done in 8s'),
    RecoveryStep(label: 'Write to the Pipeline 2026 sheet', state: RecoveryStepState.fail, note: 'Error 403: lost edit access'),
    RecoveryStep(label: 'Post the summary in #sales', state: RecoveryStepState.wait),
  ],
  options: const [
    RecoveryOption(value: 'retry', label: 'Ask for edit access, then retry'),
    RecoveryOption(value: 'skip', label: 'Skip it and post the summary'),
    RecoveryOption(value: 'hand', label: 'Hand it over to Maya'),
  ],
  onContinue: (value) => carryOn(value),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | What the agent was doing, like "Sync the pipeline to Sheets". |
| `status` | `string` | Where the run stands, like "Stopped at step 2". Crossfades when it changes. |
| `steps` | `RecoveryStep[]` | The steps around the failure. Each has a `label`, a `state` and an optional `note`. |
| `step.state` | `done \| fail \| run \| wait \| skip \| hand` | Picks the glyph: a check, a red alert, a spinner, a quiet dot, a struck-through skip or a hand-off. |
| `step.note` | `string` | The quiet line under the step, like "Done in 8s" or the error. Crossfades when it changes. |
| `question` | `string` | The question above the choices. Defaults to "How should the agent continue?". |
| `options` | `RecoveryOption[]` | The ways the agent can carry on, each a `{ value, label }`. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string` | The chosen option, controlled or uncontrolled. Defaults to the first option. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | Called when a different choice is picked. |
| `onContinue` | `(value) => void` | Called with the chosen option when Continue is pressed. |
| `continueLabel` | `string` | The label on the confirm button. Defaults to "Continue". |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Whether the choices show. Leave it out and they fold away once Continue is pressed. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open) => void` | Called when the choices fold open or closed. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The step
glyphs take their colour from the theme tokens — a green check, a red alert, a plum hand-off — and
the rail between steps, the selected choice and the Continue pill all draw from the same tokens, so
the whole block reads against either background; in Soft the choices and the pill are rounder.


# Eval results (/docs/components/eval-results)

An eval suite's latest run: one bar segment per case, the pass count against the run before, and
the cases — all of them, or only the failed ones. The `Run evals` button spins while the suite runs
and the count reads `Running 3 of 8`. A failed case opens to show what was `expected` and what it
`got`, with a `fix` button that reruns just that case.

<Preview>
  <EvalResultsExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { EvalResults, type EvalCase } from './eval-results/EvalResults';

const cases: EvalCase[] = [
  { id: 'seat', name: 'Names the Pro seat limit', status: 'pass', time: '0.6s' },
  {
    id: 'price',
    name: 'Prices match the billing table',
    status: 'fail',
    time: '0.9s',
    expected: '$24 a seat, billed yearly',
    got: '$29 a seat, billed yearly',
    source: 'Billing table, Pro row',
    fix: { label: 'Use $24 and rerun', onClick: rerun },
  },
];

<EvalResults
  title="Pricing copy evals"
  subtitle="Copy agent · 8 cases · run 2h ago"
  cases={cases}
  previousPassed={8}
  onRun={run}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [EvalResultsComponent] -->
cases: EvalCase[] = [
  { id: 'seat', name: 'Names the Pro seat limit', status: 'pass', time: '0.6s' },
  { id: 'price', name: 'Prices match the billing table', status: 'fail', time: '0.9s',
    expected: '$24 a seat, billed yearly', got: '$29 a seat, billed yearly',
    source: 'Billing table, Pro row', fix: { label: 'Use $24 and rerun', onClick: rerun } },
];

<EvalResults
  title="Pricing copy evals"
  subtitle="Copy agent · 8 cases · run 2h ago"
  [cases]="cases"
  [previousPassed]="8"
  (run)="run()"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/eval_results.dart';

final cases = <EvalCase>[
  const EvalCase(id: 'seat', name: 'Names the Pro seat limit', status: EvalStatus.pass, time: '0.6s'),
  EvalCase(
    id: 'price',
    name: 'Prices match the billing table',
    status: EvalStatus.fail,
    time: '0.9s',
    expected: '\$24 a seat, billed yearly',
    got: '\$29 a seat, billed yearly',
    source: 'Billing table, Pro row',
    fix: EvalFix(label: 'Use \$24 and rerun', onClick: rerun),
  ),
];

EvalResults(
  title: 'Pricing copy evals',
  subtitle: 'Copy agent · 8 cases · run 2h ago',
  cases: cases,
  previousPassed: 8,
  onRun: run,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The suite's name, like "Pricing copy evals". |
| `subtitle` | `string` | The line under the title, like "Copy agent · 8 cases · run 2h ago". Crossfades when it changes. |
| `cases` | `EvalCase[]` | One per case: `id`, `name`, `status`, and (for a failure) `time`, `expected`, `got`, `source`, `fix`. |
| `onRun` | `() => void` | Adds the run button. |
| `running` | `boolean` | Whether the whole suite is running: the button spins and the count reads "Running 3 of 8". |
| `runLabel` | `string` | The run button's label. Defaults to "Run evals". |
| `previousPassed` | `number` | How many passed the run before. Once the run settles, a tag compares with it. |
| `filter` / `defaultFilter` | `all \| fail` | Which cases show: all of them, or only the failed ones. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `string[]` | Ids of the failed cases that are open. Leave it out to let each one open itself. |

| `EvalCase` | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `queued \| running \| pass \| fail` | How the case did; picks its glyph and bar colour. |
| `time` | `string` | How long it took, like "0.9s", shown once it has a result. |
| `expected` / `got` / `source` | `string` | For a failed case: what should have come back, what did, and where the answer comes from. |
| `fix` | `{ label; onClick }` | A white button under a failed case's details, like "Use $24 and rerun". |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The panel
sits on a surface with the card shadow; pass and fail take the `--vo-ok` and `--vo-bad` tokens for
their glyphs and bar segments, and a failed case tints with `--vo-bad-bg`, so it all reads against
the stage. In Soft the panel, pills and segmented control are rounder.


# Event Calendar (/docs/components/event-calendar)

An event calendar shows a work week as a time grid. Drag an event to another time or day, click free
time to add one, and open an event for its details card — who is coming, the agent's **prep notes**,
and **Join**. Ask the agent to **find a time** and it sweeps the week, then suggests open slots; the
first is the pick and the rest wait behind it. **Book** adds the picked slot as an event.

<Preview>
  <EventCalendarExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { EventCalendar } from './event-calendar/EventCalendar';

const [events, setEvents] = useState([
  { id: 'kickoff', title: 'Kickoff with Maya', start: new Date(2026, 9, 19, 10), end: new Date(2026, 9, 19, 11), tone: 'purple' },
]);

<EventCalendar
  week={new Date(2026, 9, 19)}
  now={new Date(2026, 9, 23, 10, 42)}
  events={events}
  onEventsChange={setEvents}
  askLabel="Find 45 min for a design review"
  onAsk={findSlot}
  suggestions={suggestions}
  onBook={book}
  onPrepNotes={ev => `Context for ${ev.title} is ready.`}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [EventCalendarComponent] -->
<EventCalendar [week]="week" [now]="now"
  [events]="events" (eventsChange)="events = $event"
  askLabel="Find 45 min for a design review" (ask)="findSlot()"
  [suggestions]="suggestions" (book)="book($event)" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/event_calendar.dart';

EventCalendar(
  week: DateTime(2026, 10, 19),
  now: DateTime(2026, 10, 23, 10, 42),
  events: events,
  onEventsChange: (e) => setState(() => events = e),
  askLabel: 'Find 45 min for a design review',
  onAsk: findSlot,
  suggestions: suggestions,
  onBook: book,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `week` | `Date` | The first day shown, like Monday Oct 19. Its time of day is ignored. |
| `events` / `defaultEvents` | `EventCalendarEvent[]` | The events. Each has `id`, `title`, `start`, `end`, optional `tone` and `people`. |
| `onEventsChange` | `(events) => void` | Fires when an event is moved, added or removed. |
| `days` | `number` | How many days to show, from `week`. Defaults to 5. |
| `startHour` / `hours` | `number` | The first hour and how many hours the grid shows. Defaults to 9am for 8 hours. |
| `now` | `Date` | Marks today and draws the now line. Leave it out for neither. |
| `selected` / `defaultSelected` | `string \| null` | The event whose details card is open, by id. |
| `askLabel` / `onAsk` | `string` / `() => void` | Adds the agent's button to the header. |
| `finding` | `boolean` | The agent is looking: its button thinks and a scan line sweeps the week. |
| `suggestions` | `EventCalendarSuggestion[]` | Slots the agent suggests. The first is the pick, the rest wait behind it. |
| `onBook` / `onSkip` | `(suggestion) => void` | Book the picked slot, or skip to the next. |
| `onPrepNotes` | `(event) => ReactNode \| Promise` | Adds the agent's prep notes to the details card. |
| `onJoin` | `(event) => void` | Adds **Join** to the details card. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). Event
blocks take the eight tone tints (`--vo-pb`, `--vo-pl`, …); the now line and the agent's scan use the
accent. The grid, times and details card follow the shared `--vo-*` surface, line and spacing tokens.


# Feedback sheet (/docs/components/feedback-sheet)

A feedback sheet sits under an answer in a chat thread. The thumbs rate it; a thumbs down
opens a sheet with quick `reasons` and a free-text box so the person can say what missed.
Send shows a spinner, then the sheet folds away and a thank-you line lands. A thumbs up just
notes it. It is `bare` by default so it reads flat under a message; set it to `false` for a
card of its own.

<Preview>
  <FeedbackSheetExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { FeedbackSheet, type Feedback } from './feedback-sheet/FeedbackSheet';

<FeedbackSheet
  onSubmit={(f: Feedback) => save(f)}
  onRatingChange={(r) => track(r)}
>
  I tightened the hero spacing to 24px and swapped the CTA to the accent blue.
</FeedbackSheet>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [FeedbackSheetComponent] -->
<FeedbackSheet
  message="I tightened the hero spacing to 24px…"
  (submit)="save($event)"
  (ratingChange)="track($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/feedback_sheet.dart';

FeedbackSheet(
  message: 'I tightened the hero spacing to 24px…',
  onSubmit: (f) => save(f),
  onRatingChange: (r) => track(r),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` / `message` | `ReactNode` / `string` | The answer being rated, shown above the thumbs. |
| `rating` | `'up' \| 'down' \| null` | Whether the answer was rated good or bad. Leave it out to let the thumbs set it. |
| `onRatingChange` | `(rating) => void` | Called when the thumbs change. |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the reasons sheet is open. Leave it out and thumbs down opens it. |
| `selected` | `string[]` | The reasons picked. Leave it out to let the chips keep it. |
| `comment` | `string` | What is written in the box. Leave it out to let the box keep it. |
| `question` | `string` | The heading of the sheet that opens on thumbs down. |
| `reasons` | `string[]` | Quick reasons to pick from. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | The box placeholder. |
| `note` | `string` | A quiet note beside the buttons, like who sees the feedback. |
| `sending` | `boolean` | Shows the spinner on Send, for a scripted demo. |
| `sent` | `Feedback \| null` | What was sent, which shows the thank-you line. Leave it out and Send sets it. |
| `onSubmit` | `(feedback) => void \| Promise<void>` | Called with what the person picked and wrote. Return a promise to show a spinner until it settles. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat under a message in a chat thread (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
active bad thumb and the thank-you line take their tints from the `--vo-bad` and `--vo-ok` tokens,
the selected chips from the accent, and the box line from the field tokens, so the sheet reads
against the stage; in Soft the chips, box and buttons are rounder.


# Field extraction (/docs/components/field-extraction)

The agent reads a document on the left and lists the fields it found on the right, each with
how sure it is. A new field slides in and its source region on the page lights up for a moment,
so you can see where each value came from. A field the agent is unsure of (`confidence` under
`0.6`) asks the person to check it — they type the value into the field itself and confirm with
Enter or by clicking away. The Send button waits until every field is sure or checked.

<Preview>
  <FieldExtractionExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

Wrap the parts of the page a field comes from in a zone, and tie each field to its zone with a
matching `key`/`field`. The zone lights up while its field is read, hovered or checked.

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { FieldExtraction, FieldZone, type ExtractedField } from './field-extraction/FieldExtraction';

const fields: ExtractedField[] = [
  { key: 'no', label: 'Invoice no.', value: 'NW-2041', confidence: 0.99 },
  { key: 'due', label: 'Due by', value: '1? Nov 2026', confidence: 0.41 },
];

<FieldExtraction
  page={
    <>
      <FieldZone field="no"><span className="vo-muted">Invoice no.</span> NW-2041</FieldZone>
      <FieldZone field="due" className="vo-fex-smudge">Due by 1? Nov 2026</FieldZone>
    </>
  }
  fields={fields}
  status="Reading page 1"
  sendLabel="Send to Sheets"
  onFix={(key, value) => confirm(key, value)}
  onSend={send}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [FieldExtractionComponent, VoFieldZoneComponent] -->
<FieldExtraction
  [fields]="fields"
  [status]="status"
  sendLabel="Send to Sheets"
  (fix)="onFix($event.key, $event.value)"
  (onSend)="send()"
>
  <div fieldZone field="no"><span class="vo-muted">Invoice no.</span> NW-2041</div>
  <div fieldZone field="due" class="vo-fex-smudge">Due by 1? Nov 2026</div>
</FieldExtraction>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/field_extraction.dart';

FieldExtraction(
  page: const [
    FexPageRow(zone: 'no', left: 'Invoice no.', right: 'NW-2041'),
    FexPageRow(zone: 'due', left: 'Due by', right: '1? Nov 2026', smudge: true),
  ],
  fields: const [
    ExtractedField(key: 'no', label: 'Invoice no.', value: 'NW-2041', confidence: 0.99),
    ExtractedField(key: 'due', label: 'Due by', value: '1? Nov 2026', confidence: 0.41),
  ],
  status: 'Reading page 1',
  sendLabel: 'Send to Sheets',
  onFix: (key, value) => confirm(key, value),
  onSend: send,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | `ReactNode` | The page being read, on the left. Wrap the parts the fields come from in `FieldZone`. |
| `fields` | `ExtractedField[]` | The fields found so far, in order. Each new one slides in and its zone lights up for a moment. |
| `reading` | `boolean` | A scan line passes down the page each time this turns true, and Send waits while it is true. |
| `status` | `string` | The quiet line by the title, like "Reading page 1". Crossfades when it changes. |
| `checkHint` | `string` | Replaces the status while a field is being checked. |
| `onFix` | `(key, value) => void` | Called when a checked field is confirmed with Enter or by clicking away. |
| `title` | `string` | The heading over the field list. Defaults to "Extracted fields". |
| `sendLabel` | `string` | The button under the fields. It waits until every field is sure or checked. |
| `sendState` | `idle \| sending \| sent` | `idle` shows `sendLabel`, `sending` a spinner, `sent` a check and `sentLabel`. |
| `sentLabel` | `string` | The label once the fields have been sent. |
| `onSend` | `() => void` | Called when Send is pressed while every field is sure. |
| `ExtractedField.key` | `string` | Ties the field to the `FieldZone` it was read from. |
| `ExtractedField.confidence` | `number` | 0 to 1. Under `0.6` the field asks the person to check it. |
| `ExtractedField.suggestion` | `string` | What the value starts as when the person checks it. |
| `ExtractedField.fixed` | `boolean` | The person has checked it. Shows "Fixed" with a full bar. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
page is drawn as paper — white ink-on-paper in light mode, a dark document in dark mode — while
the rest of the component follows the theme tokens. A highlighted source region tints and rings
with the accent, and an unsure one with the warning tint, so each keeps its contrast against the
ink; in Soft the document, panel and buttons are rounder.


# Funnel chart (/docs/components/funnel-chart)

A funnel chart shows how many people reach each `stage` in order. Each bar grows in a moment
after the chart appears, the stage that loses the largest share of the one before it is marked
in red, and the agent's `insight` sits below. With more than one `view`, a segment switch redraws
the bars top to bottom and crossfades the note.

<Preview>
  <FunnelChartExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { FunnelChart } from './funnel-chart/FunnelChart';

<FunnelChart
  title="Signup to paid"
  stages={['Signed up', 'Opened a file', 'Ran the agent', 'Invited a teammate', 'Paid']}
  views={[
    { key: 'all', label: 'All', values: [12400, 9180, 6420, 2310, 1490], insight: 'The biggest drop is after the first agent run.' },
    { key: 'team', label: 'Teams', values: [4100, 3570, 2980, 1890, 1210], insight: 'Teams convert well.' },
  ]}
  defaultView="all"
  shareLabel="of signups"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [FunnelChartComponent] -->
stages = ['Signed up', 'Opened a file', 'Ran the agent', 'Invited a teammate', 'Paid'];
views = [
  { key: 'all', label: 'All', values: [12400, 9180, 6420, 2310, 1490], insight: 'The biggest drop is after the first agent run.' },
  { key: 'team', label: 'Teams', values: [4100, 3570, 2980, 1890, 1210], insight: 'Teams convert well.' },
];

<FunnelChart
  title="Signup to paid"
  [stages]="stages"
  [views]="views"
  defaultView="all"
  shareLabel="of signups"
  (viewChange)="onView($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/funnel_chart.dart';

FunnelChart(
  title: 'Signup to paid',
  stages: const ['Signed up', 'Opened a file', 'Ran the agent', 'Invited a teammate', 'Paid'],
  views: const [
    FunnelChartView(key: 'all', label: 'All', values: [12400, 9180, 6420, 2310, 1490], insight: 'The biggest drop is after the first agent run.'),
    FunnelChartView(key: 'team', label: 'Teams', values: [4100, 3570, 2980, 1890, 1210], insight: 'Teams convert well.'),
  ],
  defaultView: 'all',
  shareLabel: 'of signups',
)
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | Like "Signup to paid". |
| `stages` | `string[]` | The stages in order, like "Signed up" then "Opened a file". |
| `views` | `FunnelChartView[]` | One set of numbers per view. With more than one, a switch picks between them. |
| `view` | `string` | Key of the view shown. Leave it out to let the switch change it. |
| `defaultView` | `string` | Defaults to the first view. |
| `onViewChange` | `(key) => void` | Called when the switch picks a view. |
| `shareLabel` | `string` | Ends a stage's tip, like "of signups" in "51.8% of signups". |
| `startLabel` | `string` | The first stage's tip. Defaults to "Starting point". |
| `format` | `(n) => string` | Writes a count. Defaults to whole numbers like 12,400. |
| `view.key` | `string` | Identifies the view. |
| `view.label` | `string` | On the switch, like "Teams". |
| `view.values` | `number[]` | How many reached each stage, in order. |
| `view.insight` | `string` | The agent's note under the funnel for this view. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface and the bars run from the first chart colour (`--vo-c1`, the accent) down to the
next (`--vo-c2`), so each stage reads a shade apart; the biggest drop uses the bad tone and the
agent's note tints with the accent — all from the theme tokens. In the default style the bars carry
a light accent edge on the track; in Soft they are flat fills.


# Grid (/docs/components/grid)

A grid is a layout primitive for arranging cards or any other components. Give it a fixed column
count with `cols`, or set `fit` to pack as many columns as fit at a minimum width (`min`) so it
reflows on its own with no breakpoints. `gap` sets the gutter. A child spans more than one column
with `span` (`2`, `3`, `4`) or the full row with `span="full"`. The grid is its own container, so it
collapses to one column when it gets narrow — whatever the page around it does.

<Preview>
  <GridExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Grid, GridItem } from './grid/Grid';

<Grid cols={3} gap={4}>
  <GridItem span={2}>spans two</GridItem>
  <div>…</div>
  <div>…</div>
</Grid>

<Grid fit min="200px">
  <div>…</div>
  <div>…</div>
</Grid>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [GridComponent, GridItemDirective] -->
<Grid [cols]="3" [gap]="4">
  <div gridItem="2">spans two</div>
  <div>…</div>
  <div>…</div>
</Grid>

<Grid [fit]="true" min="200px">
  <div>…</div>
  <div>…</div>
</Grid>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/grid.dart';

VoGrid(
  cols: 3,
  gap: 16,
  children: [
    VoGridItem(span: 2, child: cell('spans two')),
    cell('…'),
    cell('…'),
  ],
),

VoGrid(
  fit: true,
  min: 200,
  children: [cell('…'), cell('…')],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cols` | `number` | A fixed column count. Ignored when `fit` is set. `3` by default. |
| `fit` | `boolean` | Pack as many columns as fit at `min` width, reflowing with no column count. |
| `min` | `string` | Minimum column width when `fit` is set. `200px` by default. |
| `gap` | `1–8 \| string` | The gutter: a core spacing step or a raw CSS length. `4` by default. |
| `span` (on a child) | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| full` | Make a child span more than one column, or the full row. |

In React and Flutter a spanning child is wrapped in `GridItem` / `VoGridItem`; in Angular it carries
the `gridItem` directive.

## Theming [#theming]

The grid is pure layout — it adds no color, shadow or border of its own, so the children it holds
(cards, charts, tables) carry the look. Spacing flows through the shared `--vo-s-*` tokens. It works
unchanged in light and dark and in both the Soft and Blueprint styles.


# Health score (/docs/components/health-score)

One score for a design system, with the checks behind it. A half-gauge shows the overall score
(green from 90, the accent from 80, red below). Point at a check — or tab to it — and the gauge
swings to that check's score and names it; leave the list and it swings back. Open a check to see
why, and, when it is `fixable` and you pass `onFix`, fix it from there: the button spins until your
promise settles, then you update the check's `score` and `detail`.

<Preview>
  <HealthScoreExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { HealthScore, type HealthScoreCheck } from './health-score/HealthScore';

const checks: HealthScoreCheck[] = [
  { label: 'Token usage', score: 96, detail: 'All colours come from the library' },
  { label: 'Contrast', score: 88, detail: '2 text pairs below AA', fixable: true },
  { label: 'Component reuse', score: 74, detail: '11 detached instances in Checkout' },
];

<HealthScore
  checks={checks}
  title="Design system health"
  onFix={async (check, i) => {
    await repair(check);
    // then update the check's score and detail in your state
  }}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [HealthScoreComponent] -->
checks: HealthScoreCheck[] = [
  { label: 'Token usage', score: 96, detail: 'All colours come from the library' },
  { label: 'Contrast', score: 88, detail: '2 text pairs below AA', fixable: true },
];
fix = async (check: HealthScoreCheck, i: number) => { await this.repair(check); };

<HealthScore
  [checks]="checks"
  title="Design system health"
  [onFix]="fix"
  (openChange)="opened = $event"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/health_score.dart';

HealthScore(
  checks: const [
    HealthScoreCheck(label: 'Token usage', score: 96, detail: 'All colours come from the library'),
    HealthScoreCheck(label: 'Contrast', score: 88, detail: '2 text pairs below AA', fixable: true),
  ],
  title: 'Design system health',
  onFix: (check, i) async {
    await repair(check);
    // then update the checks you pass in from your state
  },
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checks` | `HealthScoreCheck[]` | The checks behind the score. |
| `title` | `string` | Beside the gauge. Defaults to `"Design system health"`. |
| `score` | `number` | The gauge score. Defaults to the average of the checks. |
| `status` | `string` | The line under the title. Defaults to a line built from the checks. |
| `open` | `string[]` | The open checks, by key (controlled). Leave out to let each row toggle itself. |
| `defaultOpen` | `string[]` | The checks open at first (uncontrolled). |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: string[]) => void` | Called when the set of open checks changes. |
| `onFix` | `(check, index) => void \| Promise` | A check's Fix button. Return a promise and it spins until it settles; then update the check's score and detail. |
| `check.key` | `string` | Identifies the check. Defaults to its label. |
| `check.label` | `string` | Like "Contrast". |
| `check.score` | `number` | 0 to 100. From 90 green, from 80 the accent, below that red. |
| `check.detail` | `string` | One line under the check when it is open. |
| `check.fixable` | `boolean` | Adds a Fix button to the open check (needs `onFix`). |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card,
rows, bars and gauge track all come from the theme tokens; the gauge fill follows the score (its green
and red are the component's own `--vo-hs-ok` / `--vo-hs-bad`, the accent in between), and an open or
hovered row picks up the row tint. In Soft the card and the Fix pill are rounder.


# Human handoff (/docs/components/human-handoff)

The agent passes a conversation to a person: why it handed off (`reason`), who has it (`assignee`,
with a `people` list for **Reassign**), when the reply is due (`secondsLeft` counts down and the bar
empties, turning orange under five minutes), the `summary` and `facts` they need to pick it up, and
the `message` the customer was told (editable in place when you pass `onMessageChange`). A `status`
row at the foot says where it stands — neutral while it waits, amber when the person can't take it,
green once they have.

<Preview>
  <HumanHandoffExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { HumanHandoff, type HandoffPerson } from './human-handoff/HumanHandoff';

const billing: HandoffPerson[] = [
  { name: 'Alex Rivera', color: 'var(--vo-av-m)', team: 'Billing', presence: 'Available', tone: 'ok' },
  { name: 'Maya Chen', color: 'var(--vo-av-l)', team: 'Billing', presence: 'Out until 2pm', tone: 'warn' },
];

<HumanHandoff
  reason="Refund over $500 needs a person"
  assignee={billing[0]}
  people={billing}
  onReassign={(p) => reassign(p)}
  secondsLeft={846}
  targetSeconds={900}
  summary="Dana was charged twice and wants one charge back."
  facts={[{ label: 'Amount', value: '$588.00' }]}
  message="Thanks, Dana. I've passed your conversation to our billing team."
  messageLabel="Sent to Dana"
  onMessageChange={(text) => save(text)}
  status={{ tone: 'ok', title: 'With Alex · agent paused', detail: "The agent won't reply while Alex has it" }}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [HumanHandoffComponent] -->
billing: HandoffPerson[] = [
  { name: 'Alex Rivera', color: 'var(--vo-av-m)', team: 'Billing', presence: 'Available', tone: 'ok' },
];

<HumanHandoff
  reason="Refund over $500 needs a person"
  [assignee]="billing[0]"
  [people]="billing"
  (reassign)="reassign($event)"
  [secondsLeft]="846"
  [targetSeconds]="900"
  summary="Dana was charged twice and wants one charge back."
  [facts]="facts"
  message="Thanks, Dana. I've passed your conversation to our billing team."
  messageLabel="Sent to Dana"
  [editable]="true"
  (messageChange)="save($event)"
  [status]="status"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/human_handoff.dart';

HumanHandoff(
  reason: 'Refund over \$500 needs a person',
  assignee: const HandoffPerson(
    name: 'Alex Rivera', color: VoAvatar.mint, team: 'Billing',
    presence: 'Available', tone: HandoffPresenceTone.ok,
  ),
  people: billing,
  onReassign: (p) => reassign(p),
  secondsLeft: 846,
  targetSeconds: 900,
  summary: 'Dana was charged twice and wants one charge back.',
  facts: const [HandoffFact(label: 'Amount', value: '\$588.00')],
  message: "Thanks, Dana. I've passed your conversation to our billing team.",
  messageLabel: 'Sent to Dana',
  onMessageChange: (text) => save(text),
  status: const HandoffStatus(
    tone: HandoffStatusTone.ok,
    title: 'With Alex · agent paused',
    detail: "The agent won't reply while Alex has it",
  ),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | `string` | Why the agent handed off, like "Refund over $500 needs a person". |
| `assignee` | `HandoffPerson \| null` | Who has it, or `null` while the agent is still finding someone. |
| `finding` | `{ title; detail? }` | The two lines shown while `assignee` is `null`. |
| `people` | `HandoffPerson[]` | The people it can go to instead. Leave it out to hide **Reassign**. |
| `onReassign` | `(person) => void` | Called when a row is picked in **Reassign**. |
| `secondsLeft` | `number` | Seconds until the reply is due. Whole minutes; orange under five; overdue at 0 or less. |
| `targetSeconds` | `number` | The whole window, for the bar and the "15 min target" line. Defaults to `900`. |
| `summary` | `string` | What the person needs to pick it up. |
| `facts` | `{ label; value }[]` | A few key facts, as label and value rows. |
| `link` | `{ label; href?; onClick?; tip? }` | A link to the whole conversation. |
| `message` | `string` | What the agent told the customer. |
| `messageLabel` | `string` | The label over the message, like "Sent to Dana". |
| `onMessageChange` | `(text) => void` | Adds **Edit**: the message turns editable, and **Save** calls this with the new text. |
| `edited` | `boolean` | Adds "· edited" to the message label. |
| `status` | `HandoffStatus` | The foot row: `tone` (`wait \| warn \| ok`), `title`, `detail?` and an optional `person`. |

`HandoffPerson` is `{ name; initials?; color?; team?; presence?; tone?: ok \| warn }` — `name` is the
key, `tone` puts a green or orange dot before the presence.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface; the countdown bar, the presence dot and the foot row take their colours from the
`--vo-*` tokens — amber from the warn tokens under five minutes or when the person is out, green from
the ok tokens once they have it. The two columns stack when the card is narrow.


# Icon (/docs/components/icon)

Draw an icon by its `name`, or pass your own `path` / SVG for a glyph the set does not have. Icons
use `currentColor`, so they take the colour of the surrounding text; `size` ranges from `xs` to `xl`.

<IconExample />

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { VisunoIcon } from '@visuno/icon/VisunoIcon';

<VisunoIcon name="chevron-right" />
<VisunoIcon name="circle-check" size="l" style={{ color: 'var(--vo-ok)' }} />
<VisunoIcon name="rocket" label="Launch" />        {/* labelled, announced as an image */}

{/* your own glyph — a custom path or children on the 24×24 grid */}
<VisunoIcon path="M5 9h14M5 15h14" />
<VisunoIcon label="Custom"><path d="M4 12h16M12 4v16" /></VisunoIcon>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [VoIconComponent] -->
<Icon name="chevron-right"></Icon>
<Icon name="circle-check" size="l"></Icon>
<Icon name="rocket" label="Launch"></Icon>

<!-- your own glyph -->
<Icon path="M5 9h14M5 15h14"></Icon>
<Icon svg="<path d='M4 12h16M12 4v16' />"></Icon>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/icon.dart';

const VoIcon('chevron-right'),
const VoIcon('circle-check', size: VoIconSize.l, color: Color(0xFF16A34A)),
const VoIcon('rocket', label: 'Launch'),

// your own glyph
const VoIcon.custom(path: 'M5 9h14M5 15h14'),
const VoIcon.custom(svg: "<path d='M4 12h16M12 4v16' />"),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | A canonical icon name (e.g. `chevron-right`, `circle-check`). Any of ~5,200 resolves. Optional when you pass `path` or SVG. |
| `size` | `xs \| s \| m \| l \| xl` | Rendered size: 12 · 14 · 16 (default) · 18 · 24 px. |
| `path` | `string` | A custom SVG path (`d` of one `<path>`) drawn on the 24×24 grid. |
| `svg` / `children` | `markup / nodes` | Custom SVG shapes for a glyph the set does not have. Takes precedence over `name`. |
| `label` | `string` | An accessible label. With it the icon is announced as an image; without it it is decorative (hidden from assistive tech). |
| `color` (Flutter) / `style` (web) | `Color / CSS` | Tint the icon. By default it inherits `currentColor` from the surrounding text. |

Only the ~113 names the library itself uses are compiled into each bundle; every other name resolves
on demand on the web. On Angular and Flutter, names outside the compiled set are drawn by passing
`path` or `svg`, so any of the ~5,200 icons — and your own — render everywhere.

## Theming [#theming]

An icon has no colour of its own: it strokes with `currentColor`, so it matches the text it sits in
and switches with light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) automatically. Set a colour by styling the
element (web) or the `color` parameter (Flutter). The 24×24 grid, 1.75 stroke width and round caps
are shared across all four frameworks, so the same glyph looks identical in each.


# Image generation (/docs/components/image-generation)

Image generation is a prompt with style chips, a shape and how many pictures, and an optional
model; the pictures it makes resolve the way an image model works — Composing (a grid of dots in
the picture's colours grows out of grain), Adding detail (the blur lifts while a scan line sweeps
down and leaves the picture behind it) and Upscaling (the last softness and grain go). Every
picture moves at its own speed, one can fail with Retry, and a finished one can be upscaled,
varied, downloaded, opened larger or used as a reference. Beside it sit a gallery of earlier
pictures, newest first, and a few style presets; narrower, they take the feed's place under a
Create / Gallery / Styles switch. `onGenerate` makes the pictures and reports how far each has come.

<Preview>
  <ImageGenerationExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ImageGeneration, type GenerateRequest, type GenerationUpdate } from './image-generation/ImageGeneration';

<ImageGeneration
  title="Spring lookbook"
  gallery={gallery}
  presets={presets}
  onGenerate={(request: GenerateRequest, update) => {
    // call update(slot, …) for each picture as your model works
    update(0, { progress: 0.5, image });
    update(0, { progress: 1, image });
  }}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ImageGenerationComponent] -->
<ImageGeneration
  title="Spring lookbook"
```
