```html
  [gallery]="gallery"
  [presets]="presets"
  [generate]="onGenerate"
  (action)="handle($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/image_generation.dart';

ImageGeneration(
  title: 'Spring lookbook',
  gallery: gallery,
  presets: presets,
  onGenerate: (request) {
    // kick off your model for request.count pictures in request.shape
  },
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The project, shown after the section in the header. |
| `section` | `string` | The first part of the header. Defaults to `Images`. |
| `prompt` / `defaultPrompt` | `string` | The prompt in the composer (controlled or uncontrolled). |
| `styles` | `string[]` | The style chips under the prompt. Defaults to Editorial, Poster, Surreal and 35mm. |
| `selectedStyles` / `defaultSelectedStyles` | `string[]` | The chips that are on. |
| `shape` / `defaultShape` | `1:1 \| 3:4 \| 16:9` | The picture's shape. |
| `count` / `defaultCount` | `number` | How many pictures Generate makes, 1 to 4. |
| `models` | `ImageModel[]` | The models in the model menu. Leave it out to hide the menu. |
| `gallery` | `GeneratedImage[]` | Earlier pictures, newest first. Pictures made here join them at the top. |
| `presets` | `ImageStylePreset[]` | The Styles tab. Picking one sets the style chips. |
| `onGenerate` | `(request, update) => void` | Makes the pictures: call `update(slot, …)` for each one as it goes. Also called for Retry and Vary with count 1. |
| `onAction` | `(action, image) => void` | Called for each action on a picture (`upscale`, `download`, `reference`, `like`, `dislike`, `copy`). |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
panels sit on a surface with the card shadow; a picture's placeholder gradient and the scan line
read against either theme. In Blueprint the dots are square cells and the picture shows through
them at half strength with a hard scan line in the accent's mark; in Soft the composer, chips and
tiles are rounder. With reduced motion a picture fades in once it is done rather than resolving
step by step.


# Inline text diff (/docs/components/inline-text-diff)

A piece of copy with the agent's edits marked inline — the old words struck, the suggestion added.
Each edit opens a small toolbar to `accept` or `reject` it, and the header takes the rest all at
once. An edit the agent isn't sure of is tinted and shows a `note` above its buttons. Once every edit
is decided, the buttons give way to a short `doneLabel`.

<Preview>
  <InlineTextDiffExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { InlineTextDiff, type TextPart } from './inline-text-diff/InlineTextDiff';

const parts: TextPart[] = [
  { key: 'a', from: 'Pick', to: 'Choose' },
  ' a plan that ',
  { key: 'b', from: 'fits your team', to: 'grows with your studio' },
  { key: 'c', from: 'you can cancel', to: 'your first month is free',
    note: "Not in the pricing brief: there is no free month" },
  '.',
];

<InlineTextDiff title="Pricing intro" parts={parts} doneLabel="Saved to Pricing v4" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [InlineTextDiffComponent] -->
title = 'Pricing intro';
parts: TextPart[] = [
  { key: 'a', from: 'Pick', to: 'Choose' },
  ' a plan that ',
  { key: 'b', from: 'fits your team', to: 'grows with your studio' },
];

<InlineTextDiff
  [title]="title"
  [parts]="parts"
  doneLabel="Saved to Pricing v4"
  (decisionsChange)="onDecisions($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/inline_text_diff.dart';

InlineTextDiff(
  title: 'Pricing intro',
  doneLabel: 'Saved to Pricing v4',
  parts: const [
    EditPart(TextEdit(key: 'a', from: 'Pick', to: 'Choose')),
    TextRun(' a plan that '),
    EditPart(TextEdit(key: 'b', from: 'fits your team', to: 'grows with your studio')),
    TextRun('.'),
  ],
  onDecisionsChange: (d) {},
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | What the copy is, like "Pricing intro". |
| `parts` | `TextPart[]` | The copy in order: plain strings, with the edits between them. |
| `decisions` | `Record<string, EditDecision>` | Controlled map of what was decided for each edit, by key. Leave an edit out while it waits. |
| `defaultDecisions` | `Record<string, EditDecision>` | The uncontrolled initial decisions. |
| `onDecisionsChange` | `(decisions) => void` | Called whenever the decisions change, with the full map by key. |
| `doneLabel` | `string` | The line that replaces the buttons once every edit is decided. |
| `labels` | `{ accept?; reject?; acceptAll?; rejectAll? }` | Overrides for the button labels. |
| `TextEdit.from` | `string` | The words the copy has now, shown struck. |
| `TextEdit.to` | `string` | The words the agent suggests instead. |
| `TextEdit.note` | `string` | Why the agent isn't sure of this one; the edit is marked and the note shows above its buttons. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The struck
and added words tint from the `--vo-del` and `--vo-add` tokens, an unsure edit uses the `--vo-warn`
tokens, and the toolbar sits on a raised surface with the pop shadow — so it all reads against the
dark stage; in Soft the card and its pills are rounder.


# Launch checklist (/docs/components/launch-checklist)

A launch checklist runs the pre-flight checks before something ships. Each check is a row with a
glyph — a waiting ring, a spinner while it runs, a pass or a fail — plus a `label` and a quiet
`note`. A progress bar across the top carries one segment per check, tinted as each result lands.
A failed check shows a **Fix** button; the `status` line defaults to a count, "Checking" while one
runs, then what is left to fix or "All clear, ready to ship".

<Preview>
  <LaunchChecklistExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { LaunchChecklist, type LaunchCheck } from './launch-checklist/LaunchChecklist';

const checks: LaunchCheck[] = [
  { label: 'Contrast meets AA', state: 'ok', note: 'All 14 text pairs pass' },
  { label: 'Uses library tokens', state: 'bad', note: '3 raw hex values', onFix: fixTokens },
  { label: 'Links resolve', state: 'wait' },
];

<LaunchChecklist
  title="Ready to ship pricing?"
  checks={checks}
  action={{ label: 'Run checks', icon: 'play', onClick: run }}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [LaunchChecklistComponent] -->
checks: LaunchCheck[] = [
  { label: 'Contrast meets AA', state: 'ok', note: 'All 14 text pairs pass' },
  { label: 'Uses library tokens', state: 'bad', note: '3 raw hex values', canFix: true },
  { label: 'Links resolve', state: 'wait' },
];

<LaunchChecklist
  title="Ready to ship pricing?"
  [checks]="checks"
  [action]="{ label: 'Run checks', icon: 'play' }"
  (run)="run()"
  (fix)="fixCheck($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/launch_checklist.dart';

LaunchChecklist(
  title: 'Ready to ship pricing?',
  checks: const [
    LaunchCheck(label: 'Contrast meets AA', state: CheckState.ok, note: 'All 14 text pairs pass'),
    LaunchCheck(label: 'Uses library tokens', state: CheckState.bad, note: '3 raw hex values', canFix: true),
    LaunchCheck(label: 'Links resolve', state: CheckState.wait),
  ],
  action: LaunchAction(label: 'Run checks', icon: Icons.play_arrow, onPressed: run),
  onFix: (i) => fixCheck(i),
);
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The line above the checks, like "Ready to ship pricing?". |
| `checks` | `LaunchCheck[]` | The checks, one row and one progress segment each. |
| `status` | `string` | The line under the title. Defaults to a count, "Checking" while one runs, then what is left to fix. |
| `action` | `{ label; icon?; accent?; disabled? }` | The button beside the title, like Run checks, Run again or Ship it. `accent` tints the ship step. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a thread (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |
| `check.label` | `string` | What is checked, like "Contrast meets AA". |
| `check.state` | `wait \| run \| ok \| bad` | Not run yet, checking or fixing, passed, or failed. |
| `check.note` | `string` | The quiet line under the label, or what is wrong. |
| `check.onFix` | `() => void` | React: shows a Fix button on a failed check. Angular uses `canFix` + `(fix)`; Flutter uses `canFix` + `onFix`. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
progress segments and glyphs take their colour from the theme tokens — `--vo-ok` for a pass,
`--vo-bad` for a fail, the accent mark while running — so results read the same on either
background; in Soft the rows and buttons are rounder. The glyph crossfades in as each state lands,
and the bar transition is skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion`.


# Line chart (/docs/components/line-chart)

A line chart plots a few `series` over the same `points` in time. The first series is the main one —
a solid line with a soft fill — and the rest are dashed, to compare against. The lines draw in from
the left while the big number counts up; move the pointer over the chart for a readout that follows
the cursor, and use the legend to toggle a series off (one always stays on).

<Preview>
  <LineChartExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { LineChart } from './line-chart/LineChart';

<LineChart
  label="Active editors"
  points={['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun']}
  series={[
    { key: 'this', label: 'This year', values: [820, 910, 1040, 1210, 1320, 1620] },
    { key: 'last', label: 'Last year', values: [610, 660, 690, 800, 850, 960] },
  ]}
  unit="editors"
  compareLabel="vs last year"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [LineChartComponent] -->
series: LineChartSeries[] = [
  { key: 'this', label: 'This year', values: [820, 910, 1040, 1210, 1320, 1620] },
  { key: 'last', label: 'Last year', values: [610, 660, 690, 800, 850, 960] },
];

<LineChart
  label="Active editors"
  [series]="series"
  [points]="['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun']"
  unit="editors"
  compareLabel="vs last year"
  (visibleChange)="onVisibleChange($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/line_chart.dart';

LineChart(
  label: 'Active editors',
  points: const ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun'],
  series: const [
    LineChartSeries(seriesKey: 'this', label: 'This year', values: [820, 910, 1040, 1210, 1320, 1620]),
    LineChartSeries(seriesKey: 'last', label: 'Last year', values: [610, 660, 690, 800, 850, 960]),
  ],
  unit: 'editors',
  compareLabel: 'vs last year',
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | The name over the big number, like "Active editors". |
| `series` | `LineChartSeries[]` | The series to plot. The first is the main one (solid, with a fill); the rest are dashed. |
| `points` | `string[]` | One name per point, shown in the hover readout, like the months. |
| `axis` | `string[]` | Labels spread along the bottom. Defaults to every other point. |
| `range` | `[number, number]` | The values at the bottom and top of the chart. Defaults to the data's range with a little room. |
| `unit` | `string` | What the values count, like "editors" in "1,620 editors". |
| `compareLabel` | `string` | Ends the readout's comparison of the first two series, like "vs last year". |
| `format` | `(n: number) => string` | Writes a value. Defaults to whole numbers like 1,620. |
| `visible` / `defaultVisible` | `string[]` | Keys of the series shown. Leave out to let the legend toggle them; one always stays on. |
| `onVisibleChange` | `(keys: string[]) => void` | Fires when the legend toggles a series. |
| `series[].key` | `string` | Names the series in `visible`. |
| `series[].label` | `string` | The legend's label, like "This year". |
| `series[].values` | `number[]` | One value per point, oldest first. |
| `series[].color` | `string` | Overrides the palette colour for that series. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The first
line and its fill use the accent; the rest take the chart palette (`--vo-c2`, `--vo-c3`, …). The grid
lines, the pointer rule and the dark tooltip pill all come from the theme tokens, so the chart reads
on either background. In Flutter the lines are drawn with a `CustomPainter` and the draw-in and
count-up run on an `AnimationController`.


# Live answer (/docs/components/live-answer)

A live answer is a question and the reply that streams in beneath it, word by word. A `[1]` after a
word turns into a numbered citation you can hover or pin, which lights up its entry in the sources
list. Each turn moves through `waiting`, `thinking`, `answering` and `done`; once it is `done` it
gains the copy, rate and retry actions, the sources toggle and — on the last turn — the suggested
`followUps`. Picking a follow-up adds a new turn below, so the thread grows instead of being replaced.

<Preview>
  <LiveAnswerExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { LiveAnswer, type AnswerTurn } from './live-answer/LiveAnswer';

const turns: AnswerTurn[] = [
  {
    question: 'Where are people dropping off in onboarding?',
    state: 'done',
    text: 'Most people leave at the workspace step [1]. Five of eight people paused there [2].',
    thoughts: ['Read the funnel', 'Matched the interview notes'],
    thoughtFor: 2,
    sources: [
      { n: 1, title: 'Funnel data', detail: 'Amplitude, last 30 days' },
      { n: 2, title: 'Session notes', detail: 'Notion, 8 interviews' },
    ],
  },
];

<LiveAnswer
  turns={turns}
  followUps={['Show the drop-off by device']}
  onFollowUp={(q) => ask(q)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [LiveAnswerComponent] -->
turns: AnswerTurn[] = [
  {
    question: 'Where are people dropping off in onboarding?',
    state: 'done',
    text: 'Most people leave at the workspace step [1].',
    sources: [{ n: 1, title: 'Funnel data', detail: 'Amplitude, last 30 days' }],
  },
];

<LiveAnswer
  [turns]="turns"
  [followUps]="['Show the drop-off by device']"
  (followUp)="ask($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/live_answer.dart';

LiveAnswer(
  turns: const [
    AnswerTurn(
      question: 'Where are people dropping off in onboarding?',
      state: AnswerState.done,
      text: 'Most people leave at the workspace step [1].',
      sources: [
        AnswerSource(n: 1, title: 'Funnel data', detail: 'Amplitude, last 30 days'),
      ],
    ),
  ],
  followUps: const ['Show the drop-off by device'],
  onFollowUp: ask,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `turns` | `AnswerTurn[]` | The thread: a question and its answer, newest last. |
| `followUps` | `string[]` | Suggested next questions, shown under the last answer once it is `done`. |
| `onFollowUp` | `(question) => void` | Called when a follow-up is picked. |
| `onRetry` | `(index) => void` | Adds a Try again button under each answer; called with the turn's index. |
| `onRate` | `(index, rating) => void` | Called when an answer is rated `good`, `bad` or back to `null`. |
| `onCopy` | `(index, text) => void` | Called after an answer is copied, with its text without the citations. |
| `onSourceClick` | `(source) => void` | Called when a source in the list is clicked, besides pinning it. |
| `turn.state` | `waiting \| thinking \| answering \| done` | `waiting` shows nothing, `thinking` the Thinking line, `answering` streams the text, `done` adds sources and actions. |
| `turn.text` | `string` | The answer so far. `[1]` after a word cites source 1; a blank line starts a new paragraph. |
| `turn.thoughts` | `string[]` | What the agent did before it answered, under a toggle that counts them. |
| `turn.sources` | `AnswerSource[]` | The sources, each with its number `n`, `title`, `detail`, badge `mark` and `color`. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
answer text, the question bubble, the citation chips and the sources list all draw from the theme
tokens, so an active citation and its source row share the one accent tint; in Soft the chips and
follow-up buttons are rounder.


# Metric insight (/docs/components/metric-insight)

A metric with its trend line, a one-line read on why it moved, and a breakdown of what moved it.
A range switch (`7d` / `30d` / `90d`) re-rolls the big number and the change tag and redraws the
line in place; the pointer reads off the nearest point; a marker sits where a release happened; and
**Why did it move?** opens a breakdown of the drivers behind the change. Set `explaining` while you
fetch those drivers and the button shows the agent "Looking into it".

<Preview>
  <MetricInsightExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { MetricInsight, type MetricRange } from './metric-insight/MetricInsight';

const ranges: MetricRange[] = [
  { key: '7', label: '7d', points: [22.8, 24.6, 25.9, 26.3], value: 26.3, change: 3.5, insight: 'Up all week.' },
  {
    key: '30', label: '30d', points: [18.2, 19.0, 23.4, 26.3], value: 26.3, change: 8.1,
    insight: 'Jumped after the pricing page update on Sep 18.',
    marker: { at: 0.58, label: 'Sep 18' },
  },
];

<MetricInsight
  label="Trial to paid"
  ranges={ranges}
  defaultRange="30"
  drivers={[{ label: 'Annual plan shown first', percent: 54 }]}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [MetricInsightComponent] -->
ranges: MetricRange[] = [
  { key: '7', label: '7d', points: [22.8, 24.6, 25.9, 26.3], value: 26.3, change: 3.5, insight: 'Up all week.' },
  { key: '30', label: '30d', points: [18.2, 19.0, 23.4, 26.3], value: 26.3, change: 8.1,
    insight: 'Jumped after the pricing page update on Sep 18.', marker: { at: 0.58, label: 'Sep 18' } },
];

<MetricInsight
  label="Trial to paid"
  [ranges]="ranges"
  defaultRange="30"
  [drivers]="[{ label: 'Annual plan shown first', percent: 54 }]"
  (rangeChange)="onRange($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/metric_insight.dart';

MetricInsight(
  label: 'Trial to paid',
  defaultRange: '30',
  ranges: const [
    MetricRange(key: '7', label: '7d', points: [22.8, 24.6, 25.9, 26.3], value: 26.3, change: 3.5, insight: 'Up all week.'),
    MetricRange(
      key: '30', label: '30d', points: [18.2, 19.0, 23.4, 26.3], value: 26.3, change: 8.1,
      insight: 'Jumped after the pricing page update on Sep 18.',
      marker: MetricMarker(at: 0.58, label: 'Sep 18'),
    ),
  ],
  drivers: const [MetricDriver(label: 'Annual plan shown first', percent: 54)],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | The metric's name, like "Trial to paid". |
| `ranges` | `MetricRange[]` | The ranges to switch between. |
| `range` | `string` | The range on show, by key. Leave it out to let the switch pick it. |
| `defaultRange` | `string` | The range the switch starts on. Defaults to the first. |
| `onRangeChange` | `(key) => void` | Fires when the range changes. |
| `format` | `(value) => string` | Formats the large number and the hovered point. Defaults to one decimal and a `%`. |
| `formatChange` | `(change) => string` | Formats the change. Defaults to `"+8.1 pts"`. |
| `drivers` | `MetricDriver[]` | What moved the number, under "Why did it move?". Leave it out to hide the button. |
| `explaining` | `boolean` | Shows "Looking into it" and keeps the breakdown shut while you fetch the drivers. |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the breakdown is open. Leave it out to let the button toggle it. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Whether the breakdown starts open. Defaults to `false`. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open) => void` | Fires when the breakdown is toggled. |
| `MetricRange` | `{ key; label; points: number[]; value; change; insight; marker?: { at; label } }` | One range: its switch label, its values (oldest first), the number and change, the one-line insight, and an optional chart marker (`at` is 0 to 1 across). |
| `MetricDriver` | `{ label; percent; color? }` | One contributor to the change. `percent` is its share, 0 to 100. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface with the panel shadow; the line, the area fill and the marker all take the accent
mark, the change tag tints green or red from the theme's `ok`/`bad` tokens, and the driver bars take
their own colours (or the accent), so the whole thing reads against the stage in either mode.


# Modal (/docs/components/modal)

A modal is a centred dialog over a dimmed backdrop. It closes on the backdrop, its corner close
button or Escape; while it is open the page scroll is locked and focus is held inside the panel,
returning to the trigger when it closes. Give it a `title` and optional `subtitle`, a body, and an
optional `footer` row of buttons. `size` is `sm` (420px), `md` (560px, the default) or `lg` (820px).

<Preview>
  <ModalExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Modal } from './modal/Modal';

const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Delete project…</button>
<Modal
  open={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  title="Delete this project?"
  size="sm"
  footer={
    <>
      <button className="vo-pill vo-ghost vo-sm" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</button>
      <button className="vo-pill vo-primary vo-sm" onClick={confirm}>Delete</button>
    </>
  }
>
  <p>This removes the project and all its runs. This can't be undone.</p>
</Modal>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ModalComponent] -->
<Modal
  [open]="open"
  size="sm"
  [hasFooter]="true"
  (close)="open = false"
>
  <span vo-modal-title>Delete this project?</span>
  <p>This removes the project and all its runs. This can't be undone.</p>
  <ng-container vo-modal-footer>
    <button class="vo-pill vo-ghost vo-sm" (click)="open = false">Cancel</button>
    <button class="vo-pill vo-primary vo-sm" (click)="confirm()">Delete</button>
  </ng-container>
</Modal>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/modal.dart';

showVoModal(
  context: context,
  builder: (ctx) => VoModal(
    title: 'Delete this project?',
    size: VoModalSize.sm,
    footer: [
      TextButton(onPressed: () => Navigator.pop(ctx), child: const Text('Cancel')),
      FilledButton(onPressed: () { confirm(); Navigator.pop(ctx); }, child: const Text('Delete')),
    ],
    child: const Text("This removes the project and all its runs. This can't be undone."),
  ),
);
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the modal is on screen. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | Called by the backdrop, the close button or Escape. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | The heading at the top. Leave it out for a bare panel (then set `ariaLabel`). |
| `subtitle` | `ReactNode` | A quieter line under the title. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | A row of buttons pinned to the bottom. |
| `size` | `sm \| md \| lg` | How wide the panel may grow. `md` (560px) by default. |
| `hideClose` | `boolean` | Hide the corner close button (Escape and the backdrop still close it). |
| `disableBackdropClose` | `boolean` | Keep the modal open when the backdrop is clicked. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | For screen readers when there is no visible `title`. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The panel
uses the active theme's raised surface, text and shadow tokens; the backdrop dims with the ink token.
Motion is paused for readers who prefer reduced motion — the dialog simply appears instead of rising in.


# Model picker (/docs/components/model-picker)

A trigger names the picked model and how hard it thinks, over the open list of
`models`. Each shows its `speed`, `quality` and `cost` as five-step meters, with the
real numbers (`speedDetail`, `qualityDetail`, `costDetail`) on hover. The thinking
effort sits under them as a small dropdown. A model that can't take the request can
set a `status` of `checking` or `busy` and offer a way out through `suggestion` — a
short notice with its own buttons, the last one filled.

<Preview>
  <ModelPickerExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ModelPicker, type ModelOption } from './model-picker/ModelPicker';

const models: ModelOption[] = [
  { id: 'opus', name: 'Opus 5.5', color: 'var(--vo-pl)', note: 'Deepest reasoning, slower',
    speed: 2, quality: 5, cost: 5, speedDetail: '38 tokens a second', costDetail: '$0.021 a reply' },
  { id: 'sonnet', name: 'Sonnet 5.5', color: 'var(--vo-accent)', note: 'Balanced, the default',
    speed: 4, quality: 4, cost: 2, speedDetail: '74 tokens a second', costDetail: '$0.006 a reply' },
];

const [value, setValue] = useState('sonnet');

<ModelPicker models={models} value={value} onValueChange={setValue} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ModelPickerComponent] -->
models: ModelOption[] = [
  { id: 'opus', name: 'Opus 5.5', color: 'var(--vo-pl)', note: 'Deepest reasoning, slower',
    speed: 2, quality: 5, cost: 5 },
  { id: 'sonnet', name: 'Sonnet 5.5', color: 'var(--vo-accent)', note: 'Balanced, the default',
    speed: 4, quality: 4, cost: 2 },
];
value = 'sonnet';

<ModelPicker [models]="models" [value]="value" (valueChange)="value = $event" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/model_picker.dart';

final models = const [
  ModelOption(id: 'opus', name: 'Opus 5.5', note: 'Deepest reasoning, slower',
      speed: 2, quality: 5, cost: 5),
  ModelOption(id: 'sonnet', name: 'Sonnet 5.5', note: 'Balanced, the default',
      speed: 4, quality: 4, cost: 2),
];
String value = 'sonnet';

ModelPicker(
  models: models,
  value: value,
  onValueChange: (id) => setState(() => value = id),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `models` | `ModelOption[]` | The models to choose from. |
| `value` | `string` | The picked model's id. Leave it out to let the list hold its own. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | The picked model's id to start on when uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(id) => void` | Called when a row is picked, busy or not, so you can check the model first. |
| `efforts` | `ThinkingEffort[]` | The thinking efforts. Defaults to Off, Low, Medium and High. |
| `effort` / `defaultEffort` | `string` | The picked effort's label, controlled or to start on. |
| `onEffortChange` | `(effort) => void` | Called when the effort changes. |
| `suggestion` | `{ text; actions: { label; onClick }[] }` | A way out when the picked model can't take the request. The last button is filled. |
| `note` | `string` | The confirmation under the picker, shown with a green check. |
| `label` | `string` | The label beside the trigger. Defaults to "Model for this chat". |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Whether the list is open. Leave it out to let the trigger and Escape open and close it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open) => void` | Called when the list opens or closes. |
| `ModelOption.speed/quality/cost` | `number` | Each from 1 to 5. For cost, 5 is the most expensive. |
| `ModelOption.status` | `ready \| checking \| busy` | `checking` spins beside the name; `busy` turns the row amber, both showing `statusText`. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style
(`data-style="soft"`). The trigger and panel sit on a surface with the card shadow;
each model's tile takes its own `color` with a letter colour that reads on it, the
picked row's filled meters take the accent, and a busy row and its notice take the
warn tint — all from the theme tokens, so it reads against the dark stage.


# Number field (/docs/components/number-field)

Type a number, or step it with the minus and plus buttons (hold to repeat). Give it a `min`, `max`
and `step`, an optional `unit`, and it clamps an out-of-range value and says so — "Set to 100 (max)".

<Preview>
  <NumberFieldExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { NumberField } from '@visuno/number-field/NumberField';

<NumberField label="Quantity" value={qty} min={1} max={99} onChange={setQty} />
<NumberField label="Opacity" defaultValue={60} min={0} max={100} step={5} unit="%" />
<NumberField label="Seats" defaultValue={10} min={1} max={50} size="sm" />
<NumberField label="Locked" value={8} disabled />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [NumberFieldComponent] -->
<NumberField label="Quantity" [value]="qty" [min]="1" [max]="99"
  (valueChange)="qty = $event"></NumberField>
<NumberField label="Opacity" [defaultValue]="60" [min]="0" [max]="100"
  [step]="5" unit="%"></NumberField>
<NumberField label="Seats" [defaultValue]="10" [min]="1" [max]="50" size="sm"></NumberField>
<NumberField label="Locked" [value]="8" [disabled]="true"></NumberField>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/number_field.dart';

NumberField(label: 'Quantity', value: qty, min: 1, max: 99, onChanged: (v) => setQty(v)),
const NumberField(label: 'Opacity', defaultValue: 60, min: 0, max: 100, step: 5, unit: '%'),
const NumberField(label: 'Seats', defaultValue: 10, min: 1, max: 50, size: NumberFieldSize.sm),
const NumberField(label: 'Locked', value: 8, disabled: true),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | The current value (controlled). Leave out for an uncontrolled field. |
| `defaultValue` | `number` | The starting value when uncontrolled. Defaults to `min`, else 0. |
| `min` / `max` | `number` | The limits. Out-of-range input is clamped, with a brief note. |
| `step` | `number` | How much the buttons and the arrow keys change the value. 1 by default. |
| `unit` | `string` | A unit shown after the number, like `px`, `%` or `GB`. |
| `label` | `string` | A label above the field. |
| `size` | `sm \| md` | `sm` is compact, `md` (the default) roomier. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Greys the field out and blocks input. |
| `onChange` / `valueChange` | `callback` | Called with the clamped value whenever it changes. |

Type freely, then it settles on blur or Enter; the up and down arrow keys step by `step`, and the
minus/plus buttons repeat while held.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The field,
its hairline and the steppers all draw from the shared `--vo-*` tokens; the number is set in the
tabular-numerals face so digits don't jitter as they change.


# OTP field (/docs/components/otp-field)

A one-time code as a row of single-character boxes. Typing auto-advances, Backspace steps back, the
arrows move between boxes, and pasting a full code fills them all at once. Set `status` to show the
code as verified or rejected.

<Preview>
  <OtpFieldExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { OtpField } from './otp-field/OtpField';

const [code, setCode] = useState('');

<OtpField
  value={code}
  onChange={setCode}
  onComplete={(v) => verify(v)}
/>

<OtpField value={code} onChange={setCode} status="error" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [OtpFieldComponent] -->
<OtpField
  [value]="code"
  (valueChange)="code = $event"
  (complete)="verify($event)"
></OtpField>

<OtpField [value]="code" status="success"></OtpField>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/otp_field.dart';

OtpField(
  value: code,
  onChanged: (v) => setState(() => code = v),
  onComplete: (v) => verify(v),
),

OtpField(value: code, status: OtpStatus.error),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `length` | `number` | How many boxes / characters. Six by default. |
| `value` | `string` | The current code, up to `length` characters. |
| `onChange` / `valueChange` / `onChanged` | `callback` | Fires with the new value as the person types, pastes or deletes. |
| `onComplete` / `complete` | `callback` | Fires once the last box is filled, with the full code. |
| `numeric` | `boolean` | Only digits may be entered, and a paste keeps just its digits. On by default. |
| `status` | `default \| success \| error` | Tints the boxes green or red and shows a mark. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Greys the boxes out and blocks input. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). Boxes use
the field tokens, the accent for focus, and the success/danger tokens for `status`; in Blueprint the
boxes are squared off, in Soft they are rounded. The code is set in the monospace token.


# Permission gate (/docs/components/permission-gate)

The agent asks before it acts: one card with the question, the `scopes` to tick, and a footer
with how long the grant lasts (`durations`) and the two answers. Once allowed it gives way to a
shorter result row — a spinner while the agent is `working`, a green check when done — with a
Revoke button; declining shows an undoable notice. A follow-up ask mid-run (`followUp`) turns the
icon tile amber.

<Preview>
  <PermissionGateExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { PermissionGate, type PermissionScope } from './permission-gate/PermissionGate';

const scopes: PermissionScope[] = [
  { key: 'read', label: 'Read frames', detail: 'Pricing, Checkout' },
  { key: 'edit', label: 'Edit frames', detail: 'Only on a new page' },
  { key: 'publish', label: 'Publish library', detail: 'Affects 4 other files', risk: 'Risky' },
];

<PermissionGate
  bare={false}
  title="Allow the agent to edit Figma?"
  subtitle="It needs this to apply the pricing fixes"
  scopes={scopes}
  defaultValue={['read', 'edit']}
  onAllow={(keys, duration) => grant(keys, duration)}
  onDecline={skip}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [PermissionGateComponent] -->
scopes: PermissionScope[] = [
  { key: 'read', label: 'Read frames', detail: 'Pricing, Checkout' },
  { key: 'edit', label: 'Edit frames', detail: 'Only on a new page' },
  { key: 'publish', label: 'Publish library', detail: 'Affects 4 other files', risk: 'Risky' },
];

<PermissionGate
  [bare]="false"
  title="Allow the agent to edit Figma?"
  subtitle="It needs this to apply the pricing fixes"
  [scopes]="scopes"
  [defaultValue]="['read', 'edit']"
  (allowEvent)="grant($event.keys, $event.duration)"
  (declineEvent)="skip()"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/permission_gate.dart';

PermissionGate(
  bare: false,
  title: 'Allow the agent to edit Figma?',
  subtitle: 'It needs this to apply the pricing fixes',
  defaultValue: const ['read', 'edit'],
  scopes: const [
    PermissionScope(key: 'read', label: 'Read frames', detail: 'Pricing, Checkout'),
    PermissionScope(key: 'edit', label: 'Edit frames', detail: 'Only on a new page'),
    PermissionScope(key: 'publish', label: 'Publish library', detail: 'Affects 4 other files', risk: 'Risky'),
  ],
  onAllow: (keys, duration) => grant(keys, duration),
  onDecline: skip,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | The question, like "Allow the agent to edit Figma?". |
| `subtitle` | `ReactNode` | Why it asks. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | The glyph in the tile beside the question. Defaults to a shield. |
| `scopes` | `PermissionScope[]` | The things to allow: `{ key, label, detail?, risk?, riskDetail? }`. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string[]` | Keys of the ticked scopes. Leave `value` out to let the checkboxes hold their own. |
| `onValueChange` | `(keys) => void` | Fires when the ticked scopes change. |
| `durations` | `string[]` | How long the grant lasts, in the footer dropdown. Defaults to This task, Today, Always. |
| `durationDetails` | `Record<string, string>` | The quiet line under each duration in its menu. |
| `duration` / `defaultDuration` | `string` | The picked duration. |
| `status` / `defaultStatus` | `asking \| allowed \| declined` | Which view shows. Leave `status` out to let the buttons move it. |
| `onAllow` | `(keys, duration) => void \| Promise` | Called on Allow; the button spins until a returned promise settles. |
| `onDecline` / `onRevoke` / `onUndo` | `() => void` | Called by the decline, Revoke and Undo buttons. |
| `allowedTitle` / `allowedDetail` | `string` | The two lines on the allowed row, like "Done. 6 frames edited". |
| `working` | `boolean` | The agent is still working: a spinner on a neutral row instead of the green check. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode` | Quiet text at the end of the allowed row, like an elapsed time "0:04". |
| `followUp` | `boolean` | A follow-up ask mid-run, for one more scope: the icon tile turns amber. |
| `declineLabel` | `string` | The decline button. Defaults to "Not now". |
| `declinedTitle` / `declinedDetail` | `ReactNode` | Shown after declining. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The scopes,
footer and result row all draw from the shared `--vo-*` tokens: the ticked box and primary button take
the accent, the risk tag and the follow-up tile the warn tint, and the allowed row the ok tint; in Soft
the card, pills and tick boxes are rounder.


# Plan review (/docs/components/plan-review)

The plan an agent posts before it starts work: each step is a line you can rewrite, skip (it stays,
struck through) or add to. The footer's **Approve plan** hands it off; from there the numbers turn
into a spinner, a check, or a retry clock, and a step can open a quiet line under it reporting what it
found or what it waits on. In `review` the steps are editable; in `running` the agent works through
them; in `done` the footer offers **See changes**.

<Preview>
  <PlanReviewExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { PlanReview, type PlanReviewStep } from './plan-review/PlanReview';

const [steps, setSteps] = useState<PlanReviewStep[]>([
  { id: '1', text: 'Read the pricing frames and the brand tokens' },
  { id: '2', text: 'Compare against the three competitor pages' },
  { id: '3', text: 'Simplify the plan cards to one CTA each' },
]);

<PlanReview
  title="Plan: redesign the pricing page"
  steps={steps}
  onStepsChange={setSteps}
  phase="review"
  onApprove={run}
  onRequestChanges={askForChanges}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [PlanReviewComponent] -->
steps: PlanReviewStep[] = [
  { id: '1', text: 'Read the pricing frames and the brand tokens' },
  { id: '2', text: 'Compare against the three competitor pages' },
  { id: '3', text: 'Simplify the plan cards to one CTA each' },
];

<PlanReview
  title="Plan: redesign the pricing page"
  [steps]="steps"
  phase="review"
  (stepsChange)="steps = $event"
  (approve)="run()"
  (requestChanges)="askForChanges()"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/plan_review.dart';

List<PlanReviewStep> steps = const [
  PlanReviewStep(id: '1', text: 'Read the pricing frames and the brand tokens'),
  PlanReviewStep(id: '2', text: 'Compare against the three competitor pages'),
  PlanReviewStep(id: '3', text: 'Simplify the plan cards to one CTA each'),
];

PlanReview(
  title: 'Plan: redesign the pricing page',
  steps: steps,
  phase: PlanPhase.review,
  onStepsChange: (next) => setState(() => steps = next),
  onApprove: run,
  onRequestChanges: askForChanges,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | Like "Plan: redesign the pricing page". |
| `steps` | `PlanReviewStep[]` | The steps. Leave it out (with `defaultSteps`) to let the person edit, skip and add steps on their own. |
| `defaultSteps` | `PlanReviewStep[]` | The initial steps when uncontrolled. |
| `onStepsChange` | `(steps) => void` | Emitted whenever the list changes (edit, skip, add). |
| `phase` | `review \| running \| done` | `review` (steps editable), `running` (agent works through them) or `done`. |
| `status` | `string` | The line under the title. Defaults to how many steps are left in and roughly how long they take. |
| `note` | `string` | The quiet line in the footer. Defaults to a hint for each phase. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode` | Quiet text at the end of the header, like an elapsed time "0:04". |
| `onApprove` | `() => void` | The **Approve plan** button, in `review`. |
| `onRequestChanges` | `() => void` | The **Ask for changes** button, in `review`. |
| `onStop` | `() => void` | The **Stop** button, in `running`. |
| `onSeeChanges` | `() => void` | The **See changes** button, in `done`. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |
| `step.skipped` | `boolean` | Left out of the plan; it stays in the list, struck through. |
| `step.edited` | `boolean` | Marks a step the person rewrote. |
| `step.state` | `run \| retry \| done` | `run` while the agent works on it, `retry` while it waits out a problem, `done` once it has. |
| `step.detail` | `string` | The line the step reports under it. Opens and crossfades when it changes. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). It sits
flat in a chat thread by default; set `bare={false}` for a card of its own. The step numbers, the
running tint, the amber retry and the green done mark all come from the theme tokens, so each state
reads at a glance, and in Soft the rows and buttons are rounder.


# Progress (/docs/components/progress)

Progress shows a long run three ways at once: a ring for the whole run, a segment per step, and a
bar for how far the step in hand has got. The `state` colours it — grey while indeterminate or
paused, the accent while running, red with a Retry on error, green when complete — and the controls
follow (Pause, Resume, Run again). An optional `meter` underneath warns in words as it fills.

<Preview>
  <ProgressExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Progress } from './progress/Progress';

const steps = [
  { label: 'Reading files', unit: 'Files', total: 2000 },
  { label: 'Embedding', unit: 'Chunks', total: 5400 },
  { label: 'Writing', unit: 'Shards', total: 16 },
];

<Progress
  title="Indexing the docs"
  state="running"
  steps={steps}
  step={1}
  stepProgress={0.4}
  meter={{ label: 'Credits this month', value: 8558, max: 10000, warnAt: 0.75, note: 'Resets Dec 1' }}
  onPause={pause}
  onResume={resume}
  onRetry={retry}
  onRestart={restart}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ProgressComponent] -->
<VoProgress
  title="Indexing the docs"
  state="running"
  [steps]="steps"
  [step]="1"
  [stepProgress]="0.4"
  [meter]="meter"
  (pause)="onPause()"
  (resume)="onResume()"
  (retry)="onRetry()"
  (restart)="onRestart()"
></VoProgress>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/progress.dart';

Progress(
  title: 'Indexing the docs',
  state: ProgressState.running,
  steps: const [
    ProgressStep(label: 'Reading files', unit: 'Files', total: 2000),
    ProgressStep(label: 'Embedding', unit: 'Chunks', total: 5400),
  ],
  step: 1,
  stepProgress: 0.4,
  meter: const ProgressMeter(
    label: 'Credits this month', value: 8558, max: 10000, warnAt: 0.75, note: 'Resets Dec 1',
  ),
  onPause: pause,
  onResume: resume,
  onRetry: retry,
  onRestart: restart,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The run's name, like "Indexing the docs". |
| `state` | `indeterminate \| running \| paused \| error \| complete` | Colours the run and picks the control shown. |
| `steps` | `ProgressStep[]` | The steps, each `{ label, unit, total }`. |
| `step` | `number` | The step in hand, from `0`. |
| `stepProgress` | `number` | How far the step in hand has got, `0` to `1`. |
| `valueText` | `string` | The line under the title. Defaults to "Step 3 of 5, …". |
| `error` | `string` | What failed, shown over the bar while `state` is `error`. |
| `onPause` / `onResume` / `onRetry` / `onRestart` | `callback` | The controls, wired to the matching state. |
| `meter` | `ProgressMeter` | A meter under the run, with thresholds that warn in words. |

A `ProgressMeter` is `{ label, value, max, unit?, warnAt?, dangerAt?, dangerLabel?, note? }`: it
reads "On track" until `value / max` crosses `warnAt` ("Running low") and then `dangerAt` (the
`dangerLabel`, or "Almost out").

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the ring, segments and bar are squared off with hairline tracks; in Soft they are rounded
with a softer fill. The state colours and the meter's warn and danger bands come from the theme, so
they read correctly on either background.


# Prompt library (/docs/components/prompt-library)

The studio's saved prompts, each with blanks written as `{key}`. Opening one lays its blanks out as
fields — typed, or picked from a short list — and the prompt fills in as they change: filled blanks
take the accent colour, empty ones read by name. A prompt can't be used until every blank has a
value; try it empty and each missing blank turns red and says what it needs.

<Preview>
  <PromptLibraryExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { PromptLibrary, type SavedPrompt } from './prompt-library/PromptLibrary';

const prompts: SavedPrompt[] = [
  {
    id: 'rewrite',
    title: 'Rewrite a section',
    template: 'Rewrite {section} on {page} so it reads {tone}.',
    blanks: {
      section: { label: 'Section', placeholder: 'Like the plan cards' },
      page: { label: 'Page', options: ['Pricing v4', 'Home', 'Checkout'] },
      tone: { label: 'Tone', options: ['clearer', 'friendlier', 'shorter'] },
    },
  },
];

<PromptLibrary
  prompts={prompts}
  subtitle="Shared with Visuno Studio"
  onUse={(text) => send(text)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [PromptLibraryComponent] -->
prompts: SavedPrompt[] = [
  {
    id: 'rewrite',
    title: 'Rewrite a section',
    template: 'Rewrite {section} on {page} so it reads {tone}.',
    blanks: {
      section: { label: 'Section', placeholder: 'Like the plan cards' },
      page: { label: 'Page', options: ['Pricing v4', 'Home', 'Checkout'] },
      tone: { label: 'Tone', options: ['clearer', 'friendlier', 'shorter'] },
    },
  },
];

<PromptLibrary
  [prompts]="prompts"
  subtitle="Shared with Visuno Studio"
  (usePrompt)="send($event.text)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/prompt_library.dart';

PromptLibrary(
  prompts: const [
    SavedPrompt(
      id: 'rewrite',
      title: 'Rewrite a section',
      template: 'Rewrite {section} on {page} so it reads {tone}.',
      blanks: {
        'section': PromptBlank(label: 'Section', placeholder: 'Like the plan cards'),
        'page': PromptBlank(label: 'Page', options: ['Pricing v4', 'Home', 'Checkout']),
        'tone': PromptBlank(label: 'Tone', options: ['clearer', 'friendlier', 'shorter']),
      },
    ),
  ],
  subtitle: 'Shared with Visuno Studio',
  onUse: (text, prompt, values) => send(text),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prompts` | `SavedPrompt[]` | The saved prompts to list. |
| `title` | `string` | The list's heading. Defaults to "Prompt library". |
| `subtitle` | `string` | The line under the title, like "Shared with Visuno Studio". |
| `open` | `string \| null` | The open prompt's id, or `null` for the list. Leave it out to let the component hold its own. |
| `defaultOpen` | `string \| null` | The id to open at first when uncontrolled. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(id: string \| null) => void` | Called when a prompt opens or the list comes back (`null`). |
| `values` | `Record<string, string>` | The open prompt's blanks, by key. A picked blank left out starts on its first option. |
| `onValuesChange` | `(values) => void` | Called whenever a blank's value changes. |
| `onUse` | `(text, prompt, values) => void` | Called with the filled prompt once every blank has a value. |
| `onUndo` | `() => void` | Called when the used notice is undone. |
| `SavedPrompt.template` | `string` | The prompt, with each blank written as `{key}`. |
| `SavedPrompt.blanks` | `Record<string, PromptBlank>` | The blanks, keyed by `{key}`. |
| `PromptBlank.label` | `string` | The field's label. Lowercased, it also stands in the prompt while the blank is empty. |
| `PromptBlank.placeholder` | `string` | For a typed blank: the hint in the empty field. |
| `PromptBlank.options` | `string[]` | For a picked blank: the choices, in a dropdown that starts on the first. |
| `PromptBlank.error` | `string` | What the field says when used empty. Defaults to "Fill in the \<label\>". |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface, the prompt on a chip, and a filled blank takes the accent tint (`--vo-accent-bg`)
while an empty one is outlined and a needed one turns `--vo-bad` — all from the theme tokens, so it
reads in either mode; in Soft the card, fields and pills are rounder.


# Prompt starters (/docs/components/prompt-starters)

Prompt starters are suggested first prompts shown as cards, two to a row. Picking one writes its
full `prompt` into the field word by word and marks the card as picked; pressing Send emits the
prompt and clears the field with a sent line. Pass `onShuffle` to add a Shuffle button and swap in
another set of `starters` — a new set staggers the cards in again.

<Preview>
  <PromptStartersExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { PromptStarters, type Starter } from './prompt-starters/PromptStarters';

const starters: Starter[] = [
  { icon: 'grid', tone: 'blue', title: 'Audit a page', description: 'Check the pricing page', prompt: 'Audit pricing for spacing and contrast' },
  { icon: 'edit', tone: 'purple', title: 'Rewrite copy', description: 'Shorten the intro', prompt: 'Make the onboarding intro shorter' },
];

<PromptStarters
  starters={starters}
  onSend={(prompt) => run(prompt)}
  onShuffle={() => setStarters(next())}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [PromptStartersComponent] -->
starters: Starter[] = [
  { icon: 'grid', tone: 'blue', title: 'Audit a page', description: 'Check the pricing page', prompt: 'Audit pricing for spacing and contrast' },
];

<PromptStarters
  [starters]="starters"
  [onShuffle]="true"
  (send$)="run($event)"
  (shuffle)="starters = next()"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/prompt_starters.dart';

PromptStarters(
  starters: const [
    Starter(
      icon: Icons.grid_view,
      tone: StarterTone.blue,
      title: 'Audit a page',
      description: 'Check the pricing page',
      prompt: 'Audit pricing for spacing and contrast',
    ),
  ],
  onSend: (prompt) => run(prompt),
  onShuffle: () => setState(() => starters = next()),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `starters` | `Starter[]` | The starters to show, two to a row. Pass a new set to stagger them in again. |
| `value` | `string \| null` | The title of the picked starter. Leave it out to let the cards pick it. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` | Initial picked title when uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(title: string \| null) => void` | Called with the picked starter's title, or `null` when cleared. |
| `onSend` | `(prompt: string) => void` | Called with the prompt when Send is pressed. |
| `onShuffle` | `() => void` | Adds a Shuffle button under the field. Swap in another set of starters when called. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | The field's empty text. Defaults to `Pick a starter or type your own`. |
| `sentLabel` | `string` | Shown in the field once the prompt is sent. Defaults to `Sent to the agent`. |
| `Starter.icon` | `IconName` | The card's icon. |
| `Starter.tone` | `blue \| purple \| green \| orange \| red \| yellow \| pink \| teal` | Colours the icon. |
| `Starter.title` | `string` | A few words, like "Audit a page". |
| `Starter.description` | `string` | One quiet line under the title. |
| `Starter.prompt` | `string` | The full prompt it writes into the field when picked. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The cards
sit on a chip fill that lifts to a surface with a faint ring when picked; the field is a pill on a
surface with the shared shadow, and the Send button uses the accent tokens (a disabled hatch until a
starter is picked). All colours, radii and spacing come from the `--vo-*` tokens.


# Proposal card (/docs/components/proposal-card)

A proposal card is a change the agent proposes, posted in the thread. It shows a `from` value
changing to the chosen option, a confidence meter that fills in a moment after the card appears
and then follows the chosen option, and the other `options` behind an "other options" fold. Accept,
Not now and Undo move it between `open`, `accepted` and `dismissed`. By default it sits flat in a
chat thread; set `bare` to `false` to give it a card of its own.

<Preview>
  <ProposalCardExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ProposalCard, type ProposalOption } from './proposal-card/ProposalCard';

const options: ProposalOption[] = [
  { color: '#5b6472', label: '#5B6472', badge: '5.9 : 1', tone: 'ok', name: 'Suggested', description: 'Balanced with the primary', confidence: 84 },
  { color: '#475161', label: '#475161', badge: '7.4 : 1', tone: 'ok', name: 'Darker', description: 'Stronger than the primary', confidence: 62 },
];

<ProposalCard
  title="Raise contrast on the secondary button"
  subtitle="Pricing, frame 2 of 3"
  from={{ color: '#c9cfd8', label: '#C9CFD8', badge: '2.1 : 1', tone: 'bad' }}
  options={options}
  acceptedLabel="Applied to 3 buttons"
  onAccept={(option, i) => apply(option, i)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ProposalCardComponent] -->
options: ProposalOption[] = [
  { color: '#5b6472', label: '#5B6472', badge: '5.9 : 1', tone: 'ok', name: 'Suggested', description: 'Balanced with the primary', confidence: 84 },
  { color: '#475161', label: '#475161', badge: '7.4 : 1', tone: 'ok', name: 'Darker', description: 'Stronger than the primary', confidence: 62 },
];

<ProposalCard
  title="Raise contrast on the secondary button"
  subtitle="Pricing, frame 2 of 3"
  [from]="{ color: '#c9cfd8', label: '#C9CFD8', badge: '2.1 : 1', tone: 'bad' }"
  [options]="options"
  acceptedLabel="Applied to 3 buttons"
  (accepted)="apply($event.option, $event.index)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/proposal_card.dart';

ProposalCard(
  title: 'Raise contrast on the secondary button',
  subtitle: 'Pricing, frame 2 of 3',
  from: const ProposalValue(color: Color(0xFFC9CFD8), label: '#C9CFD8', badge: '2.1 : 1', tone: ProposalTone.bad),
  options: const [
    ProposalOption(color: Color(0xFF5B6472), label: '#5B6472', badge: '5.9 : 1', tone: ProposalTone.ok, name: 'Suggested', description: 'Balanced with the primary', confidence: 84),
    ProposalOption(color: Color(0xFF475161), label: '#475161', badge: '7.4 : 1', tone: ProposalTone.ok, name: 'Darker', description: 'Stronger than the primary', confidence: 62),
  ],
  acceptedLabel: 'Applied to 3 buttons',
  onAccept: (option, i) => apply(option, i),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | What the agent wants to change. |
| `subtitle` | `ReactNode` | Where, like "Pricing, frame 2 of 3". |
| `icon` | `IconName` | The icon in the tile. Defaults to a wand. |
| `from` | `ProposalValue` | How it is now — a swatch, its label and a tag. |
| `options` | `ProposalOption[]` | The changes on offer, the agent's pick first. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `number` | Index of the option shown as the change. Leave `value` out to let the list pick it. |
| `onValueChange` | `(index) => void` | Called when another option is chosen. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Whether the other options are listed. Leave `open` out to let the toggle open them. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open) => void` | Called when the fold toggles. |
| `status` / `defaultStatus` | `open \| accepted \| dismissed` | Leave `status` out to let Accept, Not now and Undo move it. |
| `onStatusChange` | `(status) => void` | Called when the status changes. |
| `onAccept` | `(option, index) => void` | Called with the chosen option when Accept is pressed. |
| `onDismiss` / `onUndo` | `() => void` | Called by Not now and Undo. |
| `acceptedLabel` | `string` | Shown once accepted, like "Applied to 3 buttons". |
| `dismissedLabel` | `string` | Shown once dismissed. |
| `confidenceLabel` | `string` | Label beside the confidence meter. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The diff
chip, confidence meter and tags take their colours from the theme tokens — the current value reads as
`bad` and the options as `ok` by default — and the icon tile uses the accent tint, so the card reads
against the dark stage; in Soft the swatches, tile and pills are rounder.


# Radar chart (/docs/components/radar-chart)

A radar chart compares a run with its baseline on a handful of eval scores: the baseline draws itself
as an outline, then this run grows out of the middle filled over it, on grey scale rings. Each axis
takes a `label`, this run's `value` and the `baseline` it is measured against, both 0 to 100; a score
under `weakBelow` is flagged "Weak". Pointing at or tabbing to an axis shows its two scores and the
change in the line below, and the legend shows and hides either series (one always stays).

<Preview>
  <RadarChartExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { RadarChart } from './radar-chart/RadarChart';

const axes = [
  { label: 'Accuracy', value: 88, baseline: 84 },
  { label: 'Instruction following', short: 'Instructions', value: 86, baseline: 80 },
  { label: 'Tool use', value: 62, baseline: 78 },
  { label: 'Speed', value: 74, baseline: 66 },
  { label: 'Cost efficiency', short: 'Cost', value: 82, baseline: 58 },
  { label: 'Safety', value: 91, baseline: 90 },
];

<RadarChart axes={axes} subtitle="Run 48 against run 41" pulse={2} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [RadarChartComponent] -->
axes: RadarAxis[] = [
  { label: 'Accuracy', value: 88, baseline: 84 },
  { label: 'Instruction following', short: 'Instructions', value: 86, baseline: 80 },
  { label: 'Tool use', value: 62, baseline: 78 },
  { label: 'Speed', value: 74, baseline: 66 },
  { label: 'Cost efficiency', short: 'Cost', value: 82, baseline: 58 },
  { label: 'Safety', value: 91, baseline: 90 },
];

<RadarChart [axes]="axes" subtitle="Run 48 against run 41" [pulse]="2" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/radar_chart.dart';

RadarChart(
  axes: const [
    RadarAxis(label: 'Accuracy', value: 88, baseline: 84),
    RadarAxis(label: 'Instruction following', short: 'Instructions', value: 86, baseline: 80),
    RadarAxis(label: 'Tool use', value: 62, baseline: 78),
    RadarAxis(label: 'Speed', value: 74, baseline: 66),
    RadarAxis(label: 'Cost efficiency', short: 'Cost', value: 82, baseline: 58),
    RadarAxis(label: 'Safety', value: 91, baseline: 90),
  ],
  subtitle: 'Run 48 against run 41',
  pulse: 2,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `axes` | `RadarAxis[]` | Five to seven axes, clockwise from the top. Each is `{ label, short?, value, baseline }`. |
| `title` | `string` | The bold heading. Defaults to `Eval scores`. |
| `subtitle` | `string` | The quieter line beside the title, like "Run 48 against run 41". |
| `seriesLabels` | `[string, string]` | The legend's names for the two series. Defaults to `['This run', 'Baseline']`. |
| `weakBelow` | `number` | A score under this is flagged "Weak". Defaults to `70`. |
| `note` | `ReactNode` | The note under the chart, shown while no axis is pointed at. Defaults to the average and its change. |
| `pulse` | `number` | An axis to call out once the chart is drawn: its label pulses (by index). |

A `RadarAxis` is `{ label: string; short?: string; value: number; baseline: number }`; `short` is
shown instead of `label` on a narrow card, and `value`/`baseline` are 0 to 100.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). This run
and the baseline take the chart palette tokens (`--vo-c1`, `--vo-c2`), the rings and spokes read from
the line tokens, and the card, the "Weak" tag and the readout line come from the theme tokens. The
baseline draws itself and this run's fill scales in from the middle on load; with
`prefers-reduced-motion` the chart appears already drawn.


# Radial goals (/docs/components/radial-goals)

Radial goals are concentric rings, one per agent, each its share of its own target. The overall
score sits in the middle. Past the target a ring goes round again from the top, with a marker where
it ends, so an agent that is ahead reads as a second lap. Hovering or focusing a ring — or its
legend row — dims the rest and rolls the middle to that agent's share. A `ranges` switch (like Week
and Month) repaints every ring.

<Preview>
  <RadialGoalsExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { RadialGoals, type RadialGoal } from './radial-goals/RadialGoals';

const goals: RadialGoal[] = [
  { key: 'support', label: 'Support agent', unit: 'tickets', value: 412, target: 375 },
  { key: 'qa', label: 'QA agent', unit: 'checks', value: 136, target: 160 },
  { key: 'research', label: 'Research agent', unit: 'reports', value: 18, target: 24 },
];

const [range, setRange] = useState('w');

<RadialGoals
  goals={goals}
  subtitle="This week"
  ranges={[{ value: 'w', label: 'Week' }, { value: 'm', label: 'Month' }]}
  range={range}
  onRangeChange={setRange}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [RadialGoalsComponent] -->
<RadialGoals
  [goals]="goals"
  subtitle="This week"
  [ranges]="ranges"
  [range]="range"
  (rangeChange)="range = $event"
></RadialGoals>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/radial_goals.dart';

RadialGoals(
  goals: const [
    RadialGoal(key: 'support', label: 'Support agent', unit: 'tickets', value: 412, target: 375),
    RadialGoal(key: 'qa', label: 'QA agent', unit: 'checks', value: 136, target: 160),
    RadialGoal(key: 'research', label: 'Research agent', unit: 'reports', value: 18, target: 24),
  ],
  subtitle: 'This week',
  ranges: const [
    RadialGoalRange(value: 'w', label: 'Week'),
    RadialGoalRange(value: 'm', label: 'Month'),
  ],
  range: range,
  onRangeChange: (r) => setState(() => range = r),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `goals` | `RadialGoal[]` | Two to five agents, outermost first. Three read best — the fewer the rings, the thicker they are. |
| `title` | `string` | The heading above the rings. Defaults to `"Agent goals"`. |
| `subtitle` | `string` | The line under the title. Defaults to `"N of M on target"`. |
| `ranges` | `{ value; label }[]` | The period switch options, like Week and Month. Leave out for no switch. |
| `range` | `string` | The selected range value (controlled). Leave out to let the switch pick it. |
| `onRangeChange` | `(range: string) => void` | Called with the new range value when the switch changes. |

Each `RadialGoal` carries a `key`, a `label` (like "Support agent"), a `unit` (what it counts, like
"tickets"), the `value` done, its `target`, and an optional `color`. The share is `value / target`;
at or past the target the ring's row shows an "on target" chip, and the ring draws a second lap with
a marker. Colours fall back to the chart palette (the accent, then green, orange, violet and red).

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The ring
tracks use the chip token and the laps and dots use the chart palette, so the rings read on either
surface; the "on target" chip uses the ok tokens. In Soft the panel and the legend rows are rounder.
Respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`, the sweep and the middle readout settle without animating.


# Reasoning trail (/docs/components/reasoning-trail)

A reasoning trail is the structured record the agent leaves after it thinks: a plan it works
through, the notes it took, the sources it read, or the edits it made. Pick what it shows with
`view`. The header counts the seconds and shimmers while the run is live, folds the trail away, and
settles on "Reasoned for Ns" once it finishes.

<Preview>
  <ReasoningTrailExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ReasoningTrail } from './reasoning-trail/ReasoningTrail';

<ReasoningTrail
  running
  view="plan"
  plan={[
    { label: 'Open the onboarding file', detail: '4 frames', state: 'done' },
    { label: 'Compare with the design system', state: 'now' },
    { label: 'Draft fixes for review', state: 'next' },
  ]}
  sources={[{ label: 'Onboarding.fig', kind: 'figma', tip: '4 frames read' }]}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ReasoningTrailComponent] -->
<ReasoningTrail
  [running]="true"
  view="plan"
  [plan]="plan"
  [sources]="sources"
  (viewChange)="view = $event"
></ReasoningTrail>

// plan: PlanStep[] = [
//   { label: 'Open the onboarding file', detail: '4 frames', state: 'done' },
//   { label: 'Compare with the design system', state: 'now' },
//   { label: 'Draft fixes for review', state: 'next' },
// ];
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/reasoning_trail.dart';

ReasoningTrail(
  running: true,
  view: ReasoningTrailView.plan,
  plan: const [
    PlanStep(label: 'Open the onboarding file', detail: '4 frames', state: PlanStepState.done),
    PlanStep(label: 'Compare with the design system', state: PlanStepState.now),
    PlanStep(label: 'Draft fixes for review', state: PlanStepState.next),
  ],
  sources: const [Source(label: 'Onboarding.fig', kind: SourceKind.figma, tip: '4 frames read')],
)
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `running` | `boolean` | Shimmers the title and counts the seconds while true. |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds to show. Leave it out to let the trail count while it runs. |
| `title` | `string` | Header text. Defaults to "Reasoning" while running and "Reasoned for Ns" after. |
| `plan` | `PlanStep[]` | The plan. Each step has a `label`, an optional `detail`, and a `state` of done, now or next. |
| `notes` | `string[]` | The agent's notes, one per line. |
| `sources` | `Source[]` | The files and links it read. Each has a `label`, an optional `kind`, and an optional `tip`. |
| `edits` | `Edit[]` | The changed files. Each has a `file`, an optional `detail`, and `removed` and `added` lines. |
| `view` | `plan \| notes \| sources \| edits` | Which part to show. Leave it out to start on the first one there is. |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the trail is open. Leave it out to let the header toggle it. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set false to give it a card of its own. |
| `onViewChange` / `viewChange` | `callback` | Fires when the shown view changes. |
| `onOpenChange` / `openChange` | `callback` | Fires when the trail opens or folds. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the header, chips and edit blocks are squared off with hairline edges; in Soft they are
rounded. The timeline rail, the pulse on the current step, and the shimmer on the title all take
their colors from the tokens; added and removed lines use the add and remove colors.


# Response versions (/docs/components/response-versions)

An answer with its earlier versions a click away. The arrows page through every `versions` entry
(oldest first); a different version fades the old text out, then the new one arrives word by word.
The regenerate button calls `onRegenerate` so you can add a version and show it, and the copy button
copies the version on screen. While `streaming` is set the new words fade in as they arrive, paging
waits, and the `status` beside the buttons shimmers.

<Preview>
  <ResponseVersionsExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ResponseVersions } from './response-versions/ResponseVersions';

const [versions, setVersions] = useState(['Pricing that grows with your team.']);
const [version, setVersion] = useState(0);

<ResponseVersions
  prompt="Write a headline for the pricing page"
  versions={versions}
  version={version}
  onVersionChange={setVersion}
  status="Writing a new version"
  onRegenerate={() => setVersions((v) => [...v, next()])}
  onCopy={(text) => console.log(text)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ResponseVersionsComponent] -->
versions = ['Pricing that grows with your team.'];

<ResponseVersions
  prompt="Write a headline for the pricing page"
  [versions]="versions"
  [version]="version"
  (versionChange)="version = $event"
  (regenerateClick)="regenerate()"
  (copyText)="onCopy($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/response_versions.dart';

ResponseVersions(
  prompt: 'Write a headline for the pricing page',
  versions: versions,
  version: version,
  onVersionChange: (i) => setState(() => version = i),
  status: 'Writing a new version',
  onRegenerate: regenerate,
  onCopy: (text) => debugPrint(text),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | `ReactNode` | The person's message the answer replies to, shown as a bubble above it. |
| `versions` | `string[]` | Every version of the answer so far, oldest first. |
| `version` | `number` | Which version is showing. Leave it out to let the arrows page through them. |
| `defaultVersion` | `number` | The version shown at first when `version` is left out. Defaults to `0`. |
| `onVersionChange` | `(index) => void` | Called when the arrows move to another version. |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | The version showing is still being written. New words fade in as they arrive and paging waits. |
| `status` | `string` | Quiet text beside the buttons, like "Writing a new version". It shimmers while streaming. |
| `onRegenerate` | `() => void` | Called by the regenerate button. Add a version and show it to answer it. Leave it out to hide the button. |
| `onCopy` | `(text) => void` | Called with the text after it is copied to the clipboard. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The prompt
bubble, the muted count and status, and the icon buttons all take their colour from the theme tokens;
each new word fades in, the regenerate glyph turns a full circle, and copy flips to a check in the
`--vo-ok` colour. Reduced motion drops the word fade, the spin and the status shimmer.


# Rewrite toolbar (/docs/components/rewrite-toolbar)

Click a sentence in the document and a small toolbar offers rewrites — `Clearer`, `Shorter`,
`Friendlier` by default. Pick one and `onRewrite` is called; while it works the toolbar says
Rewriting, then the answer is written in beside the old sentence word by word, struck-through
old against the new. Keep it with Accept or put it back with Undo. The toolbar sits above the
sentence, or under it when above would cover the header.

<Preview>
  <RewriteToolbarExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { RewriteToolbar } from './rewrite-toolbar/RewriteToolbar';

<RewriteToolbar
  title="Onboarding intro"
  defaultSentences={sentences}
  onRewrite={async (sentence, action, index) => rewrite(sentence, action)}
  onSentencesChange={setSentences}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [RewriteToolbarComponent] -->
sentences = ['First sentence.', 'Second sentence.'];
onRewrite = (s: string, action: string) => ask(s, action); // Promise<string> | string

<RewriteToolbar
  title="Onboarding intro"
  [sentences]="sentences"
  [onRewrite]="onRewrite"
  (sentencesChange)="sentences = $event"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/rewrite_toolbar.dart';

RewriteToolbar(
  title: 'Onboarding intro',
  sentences: sentences,
  onRewrite: (sentence, action, index) async => rewrite(sentence, action),
  onSentencesChange: (next) => setState(() => sentences = next),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | The document's name shown in the header. |
| `kind` | `string` | The file type tag in front of the name. Defaults to `DOC`. |
| `sentences` / `defaultSentences` | `string[]` | The text, one sentence each, so a click picks a sentence. |
| `onSentencesChange` | `(sentences) => void` | Called with every sentence once a rewrite is accepted. |
| `selected` / `defaultSelected` | `number \| null` | Index of the sentence with the toolbar on it, or `null`. |
| `onSelectedChange` | `(index) => void` | Called when the selected sentence changes. |
| `actions` | `RewriteAction[]` | The toolbar's buttons. Defaults to Clearer, Shorter and Friendlier. |
| `onRewrite` | `(sentence, action, index) => Promise<string> \| string` | Writes the new sentence. If it rejects, the sentence is left as it was. |
| `onAsk` | `(sentence, index) => void` | The wand at the end of the toolbar. Left out, it rewrites with the first action. |
| `askLabel` | `string` | The tip on the wand. Defaults to `Ask the agent`. |
| `askShortcut` | `string` | The shortcut shown in that tip. Defaults to `⌘K`. |
| `ref` | `RewriteToolbarHandle` | Drive it from a shortcut or demo: `rewrite(action)`, `accept()`, `undo()`. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
document sits on a surface panel; the floating toolbar uses the ink/on-ink tokens so it reads as a
dark pill over the text, and the picked sentence tints with `--vo-sel`. The struck-through old text
uses the bad token for its line, and the new words fade and de-blur in as they arrive.


# Rich text editor (/docs/components/rich-text-editor)

A minimal editor for a draft an agent helps with: a formatting toolbar (heading, bold, italic,
inline code, link, lists and quote), the text, and a quiet foot with the word count and undo. Select
text and press **Ask AI** — or `⌘J`/`Ctrl+J`, or type `/` on a new line — and a suggestion streams in
beside the text, the old words struck through and the new ones arriving word by word, to accept with
`Tab` (or `Enter`) or discard with `Esc`. Pass your own `ai` to call a model; the default streams a
canned demo.

<Preview>
  <RichTextEditorExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { RichTextEditor, type RichTextEditorHandle } from './rich-text-editor/RichTextEditor';

const ref = useRef<RichTextEditorHandle>(null);

<RichTextEditor
  ref={ref}
  defaultValue="<h2>Pricing launch</h2><p>New pricing goes live on March 3.</p>"
  onValueChange={(html) => save(html)}
  onSuggestion={({ action, accepted }) => track(action, accepted)}
/>;

// drive it from your own shortcuts or a command menu
ref.current?.select('New pricing goes live on March 3.');
ref.current?.ask('shorter');
```

Pass your model as `ai` to replace the demo writer — return a string, a promise, or an async
iterable of chunks to stream the suggestion in as the model answers.

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [RichTextEditorComponent] -->
<RichTextEditor
  [defaultValue]="'<h2>Pricing launch</h2><p>New pricing goes live on March 3.</p>'"
  (valueChange)="onChange($event)"
  (suggestion)="onSuggestion($event)"
/>
```

```ts
// drive it through the component instance (e.g. a @ViewChild)
editor.select('New pricing goes live on March 3.');
editor.askAi('shorter');
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/rich_text_editor.dart';

final controller = RichTextEditorController();

RichTextEditor(
  controller: controller,
  onChanged: (text) => save(text),
  onSuggestion: (r) => track(r.action, r.accepted),
);

// drive it through the controller
controller.type('New pricing goes live on March 3.');
controller.select('New pricing goes live on March 3.');
controller.ask('shorter');
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string` | The text as HTML: paragraphs, one heading level (`h2`), lists, quotes, and inside them bold, italic, inline code and links. Anything else is cleaned out, as on paste. |
| `onValueChange` / `onChange` | `(html) => void` | Called with the HTML after each change the person makes. Not while a suggestion is on screen. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Shown while the editor is empty. |
| `label` | `string` | The text box's accessible name. Defaults to `Draft`. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | The quiet hint beside the word count, on wide editors. |
