| `ai` | `RichTextAi \| false` | Writes the AI's suggestions. Defaults to a demo that streams canned text; pass your model call, or `false` to hide the AI. |
| `aiActions` | `RichTextAiAction[]` | The AI menu. Defaults to Improve writing, Make shorter, Fix grammar and Continue writing. |
| `onSuggestion` | `({ action, text, accepted }) => void` | Called when a suggestion is accepted or discarded. |
| `ref` | `RichTextEditorHandle` | A handle to drive the editor: `focus`, `getHTML`, `getText`, `setHTML`, `select`, `type`, `newLine`, `format`, `openAi`, `ask`, `accept`, `discard`, `undo`, `redo`. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The editor
keeps one height so it sits still, and its quiet text (word count, placeholder, struck words) comes up
toward the foreground in dark mode to stay legible. The suggestion's new words use the accent tint with
a blur-in that is reduced to an instant reveal under `prefers-reduced-motion`. In Soft the toolbar's
active format and the suggestion pick up a hairline of the accent mark.

<Callout>
The Flutter port approximates the contenteditable surface (which the web uses natively): the body is a
read-oriented rich view driven through a `RichTextEditorController`, with the same toolbar, word count
and streamed Ask-AI flow. See the file header for the full list of approximations.
</Callout>


# Run cost (/docs/components/run-cost)

A run cost shows the credits a run has used against its budget, as a number and a meter. A cap
marks where the agent pauses, drawn as a line across the bar; when the spend reaches it the status
turns amber and the run pauses. The breakdown under the bar shows the tokens and tool calls behind
the number, and the button starts, stops, resumes or raises the cap by status.

<Preview>
  <RunCostExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { RunCost } from './run-cost/RunCost';

<RunCost
  used={1620}
  budget={2000}
  capAt={90}
  status="running"
  rows={[
    { label: 'Input tokens', value: 14200 },
    { label: 'Output tokens', value: 3600 },
    { label: 'Tool calls', value: 7 },
  ]}
  onAction={() => stop()}
  onCapChange={(on) => setCap(on)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [RunCostComponent] -->
<RunCost
  [used]="1620"
  [budget]="2000"
  [capAt]="90"
  status="running"
  [rows]="rows"
  (action)="stop()"
  (capChange)="cap = $event"
></RunCost>

// rows: RunCostRow[] = [
//   { label: 'Input tokens', value: 14200 },
//   { label: 'Output tokens', value: 3600 },
//   { label: 'Tool calls', value: 7 },
// ];
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/run_cost.dart';

RunCost(
  used: 1620,
  budget: 2000,
  capAt: 90,
  status: RunCostStatus.running,
  rows: const [
    RunCostRow('Input tokens', 14200),
    RunCostRow('Output tokens', 3600),
    RunCostRow('Tool calls', 7),
  ],
  onAction: stop,
  onCapChange: (on) => setCap(on),
)
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `used` | `number` | Credits used so far. |
| `budget` | `number` | The whole budget, like 2000. |
| `capAt` | `number` | Where the agent pauses, as a percentage of the budget. Defaults to 90. |
| `capOn` | `boolean` | Whether the cap is on. Leave it out to let the switch change it. |
| `status` | `idle \| running \| stopped \| paused \| spent` | running is blue, paused amber, spent red. |
| `statusLabel` | `string` | Words in the status tag. Defaults by status. |
| `rows` | `RunCostRow[]` | The breakdown under the bar; each row has a `label` and a `value`. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | Words on the button. Defaults by status. |
| `title` | `string` | Defaults to "Credits used". |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set false to give it a card of its own. |
| `onAction` / `action` | `callback` | Called by the button. |
| `onCapChange` / `capChange` | `callback` | Fires when the cap switch changes. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the bar, the tag and the toggle are squared off; in Soft they are rounded. The fill takes
the accent mark while running and the warning mark once paused at the cap, and the status tag tints
to match its state, all from the tokens.


# Run queue (/docs/components/run-queue)

A run queue shows a batch of agent jobs moving through three parts. The job running is raised on
its own card with its agent, its steps, a progress bar and the time left. The jobs up next wait
below, each with when it should start, and the jobs done sit under them with how long each took and
a green tick. A failed step turns its job red and offers a Retry; a Detailed / Compact switch folds
the running job's steps away; and once every job is done a summary takes the running job's place.

<Preview>
  <RunQueueExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { RunQueue } from './run-queue/RunQueue';

const jobs = [
  { id: 'email', title: 'Draft the launch email', agent: 'Copy agent', state: 'running', time: '4.2s',
    steps: [
      { label: 'Outline', state: 'done', meta: 'done' },
      { label: 'Draft', state: 'running' },
      { label: 'Proofread', state: 'queued' },
    ] },
  { id: 'post', title: 'Schedule the posts', agent: 'Social agent', state: 'queued', time: 'in ~4s' },
];

<RunQueue title="Launch prep" jobs={jobs} summary="12.8s in all" onRetry={(j, s) => retry(j, s)} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [RunQueueComponent] -->
jobs: RunJob[] = [
  { id: 'email', title: 'Draft the launch email', agent: 'Copy agent', state: 'running', time: '4.2s',
    steps: [
      { label: 'Outline', state: 'done', meta: 'done' },
      { label: 'Draft', state: 'running' },
      { label: 'Proofread', state: 'queued' },
    ] },
  { id: 'post', title: 'Schedule the posts', agent: 'Social agent', state: 'queued', time: 'in ~4s' },
];
```

```html
<RunQueue
  title="Launch prep"
  [jobs]="jobs"
  summary="12.8s in all"
  (retry)="onRetry($event)"
  (densityChange)="onDensity($event)"
></RunQueue>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/run_queue.dart';

RunQueue(
  title: 'Launch prep',
  summary: '12.8s in all',
  onRetry: (job, step) => retry(job, step),
  jobs: const [
    RunJob(id: 'email', title: 'Draft the launch email', agent: 'Copy agent', state: RunState.running, time: '4.2s', steps: [
      RunStep(label: 'Outline', state: RunState.done, meta: 'done'),
      RunStep(label: 'Draft', state: RunState.running),
      RunStep(label: 'Proofread', state: RunState.queued),
    ]),
    RunJob(id: 'post', title: 'Schedule the posts', agent: 'Social agent', state: RunState.queued, time: 'in ~4s'),
  ],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jobs` | `RunJob[]` | The jobs in the queue. Each has a title, an agent, an icon, a state, an optional progress, a time, a note, and its steps. |
| `title` | `string` | The queue's name over its status line. |
| `status` | `string` | Overrides the status line. Defaults to "1 of 4 done" or "All 4 done". |
| `summary` | `string` | The line under "All N jobs done" once every job is done, like "18.4s in all · 1 retry". |
| `density` | `detailed \| compact` | detailed lists the running job's steps, compact folds them away. Left out, the switch changes it. |
| `onDensityChange` / `densityChange` | `callback` | Fires when the Detailed / Compact switch changes. |
| `onRetry` / `retry` | `callback` | Called by a failed step's Retry button with the job's and the step's index. Without it, failed steps show no button. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread, with no card. False by default. |

A `RunJob` state is queued, running, failed, or done. A `RunStep` has a label, a state, and an
optional meta shown once the step is done. Progress defaults to the share of a job's steps that are
done.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the running job gets a hairline in the accent and the progress bars fill in steps. A
failed job turns red with a hatched fill; the step glyphs are a spinner while running, a tick when
done, and a cross on failure.


# Run summary (/docs/components/run-summary)

A run summary closes out an agent run: a title glyph and a quiet subtitle, a line on what the run
did, and `stats` that count up from zero. Under them, `changes` list the files the run touched and
`needs` carry what is still on the person, each with an optional action button. "Undo all" greys out
the changes and swaps the glyph; leave `undone` out to let the button toggle it, or control it.

<Preview>
  <RunSummaryExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { RunSummary } from './run-summary/RunSummary';

<RunSummary
  subtitle="Finished in 12m 40s"
  summary="Pricing cards now use spacing tokens"
  stats={[
    { label: 'files', value: 6 },
    { label: 'cost', value: 0.84, prefix: '$', decimals: 2 },
  ]}
  changes={[{ file: 'PricingCard.tsx', added: 24, removed: 18 }]}
  needs={[
    {
      key: 'badge',
      text: 'The yearly badge overlaps the price on mobile',
      action: { label: 'Review', onClick: review },
    },
  ]}
  onOpenChanges={open}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [RunSummaryComponent] -->
stats: RunStat[] = [
  { label: 'files', value: 6 },
  { label: 'cost', value: 0.84, prefix: '$', decimals: 2 },
];

<RunSummary
  subtitle="Finished in 12m 40s"
  summary="Pricing cards now use spacing tokens"
  [stats]="stats"
  [changes]="changes"
  [needs]="needs"
  (openChanges)="open()"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/run_summary.dart';

RunSummary(
  subtitle: 'Finished in 12m 40s',
  summary: 'Pricing cards now use spacing tokens',
  stats: const [
    RunStat(label: 'files', value: 6),
    RunStat(label: 'cost', value: 0.84, prefix: '\$', decimals: 2),
  ],
  changes: const [RunChange(file: 'PricingCard.tsx', added: 24, removed: 18)],
  needs: [
    RunNeed(
      key: 'badge',
      text: 'The yearly badge overlaps the price on mobile',
      action: RunNeedAction(label: 'Review', onClick: review),
    ),
  ],
  onOpenChanges: open,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The title while the changes stand. Defaults to `Run complete`. |
| `undoneTitle` | `string` | The title once the changes are undone. Defaults to `Changes undone`. |
| `subtitle` | `string` | The quiet line under the title, like `Finished in 12m 40s`. |
| `summary` | `ReactNode` | One line on what the run did. |
| `stats` | `RunStat[]` | `{ label; value; prefix?; suffix?; decimals? }` — each counts up from zero. |
| `changes` | `RunChange[]` | `{ file; added; removed }` — the files the run changed, under "What changed". |
| `needs` | `RunNeed[]` | `{ key; text; action?: { label; onClick; busy? } }` — what is left for the person. |
| `undone` | `boolean` | Whether the changes are undone. Leave it out to let "Undo all" toggle it. |
| `onUndoneChange` | `(undone) => void` | Fires when "Undo all" / "Redo" toggles the state. |
| `onDetails` | `() => void` | Adds a button in the corner that opens the run's details. |
| `onOpenChanges` | `() => void` | The main button, "Open changes". |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat thread (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The glyph,
the `+`/`−` diffs and the "Needs you" dot all take their colour from the theme tokens (`--vo-ok`,
`--vo-add`, `--vo-del`, `--vo-warn-mark`), so the summary reads the same against any surface; in Soft
the card and its pills are rounder.


# Scatter chart (/docs/components/scatter-chart)

A scatter chart plots every `run` as a dot by its `x` (cost along the bottom) and `y` (eval score up
the side), sized by its `size` (tokens). Each `series` has a colour and a shape, so it reads without
colour too. Dashed median lines cut the plot into four named `quadrants`; pointing snaps to the
nearest run and shows a tooltip, and a drag draws a box that selects the runs in it. Pass `ringed`
ids to circle outliers, and an `onAsk` handler to add "Ask the agent why" to a selection.

<Preview>
  <ScatterChartExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ScatterChart } from './scatter-chart/ScatterChart';

<ScatterChart
  runs={[
    { id: 12, series: 'opus', x: 0.41, y: 92, size: 44 },
    { id: 13, series: 'sonnet', x: 0.14, y: 88, size: 20 },
    { id: 14, series: 'haiku', x: 0.05, y: 74, size: 9 },
  ]}
  series={[
    { key: 'opus', label: 'Opus', shape: 'circle' },
    { key: 'sonnet', label: 'Sonnet', shape: 'square' },
    { key: 'haiku', label: 'Haiku', shape: 'triangle' },
  ]}
  subtitle="48 runs this week, sized by tokens"
  ringed={[30, 31, 32]}
  onAsk={(runs) => `Looked at ${runs.length} runs…`}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ScatterChartComponent] -->
<ScatterChart
  [runs]="runs"
  [series]="series"
  subtitle="48 runs this week, sized by tokens"
  [ringed]="[30, 31, 32]"
  (selectedChange)="onSelected($event)"
  (ask)="answer($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/scatter_chart.dart';

ScatterChart(
  runs: const [
    ScatterRun(id: 12, series: 'opus', x: 0.41, y: 92, size: 44),
    ScatterRun(id: 13, series: 'sonnet', x: 0.14, y: 88, size: 20),
    ScatterRun(id: 14, series: 'haiku', x: 0.05, y: 74, size: 9),
  ],
  series: const [
    ScatterSeries(key: 'opus', label: 'Opus', shape: ScatterShape.circle),
    ScatterSeries(key: 'sonnet', label: 'Sonnet', shape: ScatterShape.square),
    ScatterSeries(key: 'haiku', label: 'Haiku', shape: ScatterShape.triangle),
  ],
  subtitle: '48 runs this week, sized by tokens',
  ringed: const [30, 31, 32],
  onAsk: (runs) {},
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runs` | `ScatterRun[]` | Each run is a dot: `id`, `series`, `x` (along), `y` (up) and `size`. |
| `series` | `ScatterSeries[]` | `key`, `label`, optional `color` and `shape` (`circle \| square \| triangle`). |
| `title` | `string` | The bold heading. Defaults to "Cost vs quality". |
| `subtitle` | `string` | The quieter line beside the title. |
| `xDomain` / `yDomain` | `[number, number]` | The `[min, max]` of each axis. |
| `xTicks` / `yTicks` | `number[]` | Where the labels and gridlines go. A narrow chart keeps the two ends and the middle. |
| `xTitle` / `yTitle` | `string` | The axis titles, clear of the ticks. |
| `formatX` / `formatY` / `formatSize` | `(n) => string` | Writes the axis values and the tooltip's token count. |
| `quadrants` | `[string, string, string, string]` | The four names the medians make, from the top left, clockwise. A narrow chart leaves them out. |
| `ringed` | `(string \| number)[]` | Runs to ring, like outliers the agent found. |
| `note` | `string` | The line under the chart while nothing is selected. |
| `selected` | `(string \| number)[]` | The selected runs, by id. Leave it out to let the chart hold the selection. |
| `onSelectedChange` | `(ids) => void` | Fires when the drag selection changes. |
| `onAsk` | `(runs) => string \| Promise<string>` | Adds "Ask the agent why" to a selection; the answer streams in. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The dots
take the chart palette (`--vo-c1`…`--vo-c6`); the gridlines, axes, median lines and the selection box
are mixed from the line and foreground tokens, and the tooltip sits on the ink token — so the chart
reads on either theme without any hard-coded colours.


# Score breakdown (/docs/components/score-breakdown)

A single score out of 100, with a half-circle gauge split into one segment per `factor`, each
sized by its `weight` and filled by the points it `earned`. The rows under it say what each earned
and why; the weakest factor is flagged in words, and an `improvable` row offers **Improve**, which
asks the agent (`onImprove`) for a proposal you can **Apply** to lift that factor's points — and the
whole score with it.

<Preview>
  <ScoreBreakdownExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ScoreBreakdown, type ScoreFactor, type ScoreProposal } from './score-breakdown/ScoreBreakdown';

const factors: ScoreFactor[] = [
  { key: 'accuracy', label: 'Accuracy', weight: 40, earned: 34, note: '2 wrong refund amounts in 120 tickets' },
  { key: 'speed', label: 'Speed', weight: 20, earned: 11, note: 'Median reply 6.4s, target under 4s', improvable: true },
  { key: 'cost', label: 'Cost', weight: 20, earned: 16, note: '$0.11 a ticket, budget $0.12' },
  { key: 'safety', label: 'Safety', weight: 20, earned: 19, note: 'No policy breaks, 1 tone flag' },
];

<ScoreBreakdown
  factors={factors}
  title="Support agent quality"
  previous={77}
  onImprove={async (f) => ({ text: 'Cache the search results…', gain: 'About 2.1s faster a reply', to: 17 })}
  onApply={(f, p) => update(f.key, p.to)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ScoreBreakdownComponent] -->
factors: ScoreFactor[] = [
  { key: 'accuracy', label: 'Accuracy', weight: 40, earned: 34, note: '2 wrong refund amounts in 120 tickets' },
  { key: 'speed', label: 'Speed', weight: 20, earned: 11, note: 'Median reply 6.4s, target under 4s', improvable: true },
];

<ScoreBreakdown
  [factors]="factors"
  title="Support agent quality"
  [previous]="77"
  (improveRequest)="$event.resolve({ text: 'Cache the search results…', gain: 'About 2.1s faster a reply', to: 17 })"
  (applyProposal)="update($event.factor, $event.proposal)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/score_breakdown.dart';

ScoreBreakdown(
  factors: const [
    ScoreFactor(key: 'accuracy', label: 'Accuracy', weight: 40, earned: 34, note: '2 wrong refund amounts in 120 tickets'),
    ScoreFactor(key: 'speed', label: 'Speed', weight: 20, earned: 11, note: 'Median reply 6.4s, target under 4s', improvable: true),
  ],
  title: 'Support agent quality',
  previous: 77,
  onImprove: (f) async => const ScoreProposal(text: 'Cache the search results…', gain: 'About 2.1s faster a reply', to: 17),
  onApply: (f, p) => update(f.key, p.to),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `factors` | `ScoreFactor[]` | The parts of the score; their `weight`s add up to 100. |
| `title` | `string` | The gauge label and heading. Defaults to `"Quality score"`. |
| `previous` | `number` | Last period's score, for the change shown beside the band word. |
| `since` | `string` | What the change is measured against. Defaults to `"since last week"`. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `string[]` | The open rows, by key (controlled / initial). |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: string[]) => void` | Fires when a row opens or closes. |
| `onImprove` | `(factor) => ScoreProposal \| Promise<…>` | Called by **Improve**; while it waits the row says the agent is looking. |
| `onApply` | `(factor, proposal) => void` | Called by **Apply**; update the factor's `earned` and `note`. |
| `improvingLabel` | `string` | What the row says while the agent works. Defaults to `"Looking into it"`. |
| `factor.weight` / `factor.earned` | `number` | The points a factor can earn and did earn. |
| `factor.note` | `string` | The agent's one-line note, like `"Median reply 6.4s, target under 4s"`. |
| `factor.improvable` | `boolean` | Adds an **Improve** button to the open row. |
| `factor.detail` | `string` | A line shown first in the open row, like what was changed. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The gauge
segments and the row swatches use the chart palette (`--vo-c1`…`--vo-c6`); the band chip, the Weakest
flag and the proposal card tint from the theme tokens (`--vo-ok`, `--vo-warn`, `--vo-surface`,
`--vo-line`), so the breakdown reads on either background. In Soft the rows and buttons are rounder.


# Search input (/docs/components/search-input)

A search field with a leading icon and a clear button. Optional scope chips narrow the search; a
dropdown shows recent queries while the field is empty and live results as you type, with an
optional agent answer on top. Press Enter to search, or pick a result.

<Preview>
  <SearchInputExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { SearchInput } from '@visuno/search-input/SearchInput';

<SearchInput
  placeholder="Search…"
  scopes={[{ value: 'all', label: 'All' }, { value: 'docs', label: 'Docs', icon: 'file-text' }]}
  results={results}
  recent={['design tokens', 'dark mode']}
  answer="3 matches for “tokens” in Docs."
  onSearch={(q, scope) => run(q, scope)}
  onSelect={(value) => open(value)}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [SearchInputComponent] -->
<SearchInput
  placeholder="Search…"
  [scopes]="scopes"
  [results]="results"
  [recent]="['design tokens', 'dark mode']"
  answer="3 matches for “tokens” in Docs."
  (search)="run($event.query, $event.scope)"
  (select)="open($event)"
></SearchInput>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/search_input.dart';

SearchInput(
  placeholder: 'Search…',
  scopes: const [SearchScope('all', label: 'All'), SearchScope('docs', label: 'Docs', icon: 'file-text')],
  results: results,
  recent: const ['design tokens', 'dark mode'],
  answer: '3 matches for “tokens” in Docs.',
  onSearch: (q, scope) => run(q, scope),
  onSelect: open,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `onValueChange` | `string` / `callback` | The text in the field. Omit `value` to let the component keep it. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Placeholder shown while the field is empty. |
| `scopes` | `SearchScope[]` | Scope chips before the field. The active one narrows the search. Each has a `value`, optional `label` and `icon`. |
| `scope` / `onScopeChange` | `string` / `callback` | The active scope's value. |
| `results` | `SearchResult[]` | Live results for the current query. Each has a `value`, optional `label`, `detail` and `icon`. |
| `recent` | `string[]` | Earlier queries, shown while the field is empty. |
| `answer` | `node` | The agent's answer for the current query, shown above the results. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Shows a spinner in the field while results load. |
| `onSearch` | `(query, scope) => void` | Called on submit (Enter) or a recent pick. |
| `onSelect` | `(value) => void` | Called with a result's value when it is picked. |
| `onClear` | `callback` | Called when the field is cleared. |

## Theming [#theming]

The field, scope chips and dropdown all draw from the shared `--vo-*` tokens, so they work in light
and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The field shows focus
with its own edge (no extra ring); the agent answer sits on a faint accent tint.


# Segmented Control (/docs/components/segmented-control)

A segmented control picks one of a few options. A white knob slides to the picked one. As `tabs`
(the default) it switches a panel; as a `radio` group it sets an option. The arrow keys move along
and pick, and Home and End jump to the ends. The `label` is required and names the group for screen
readers.

The example below is a "Pricing launch" planner: the control switches the panel beneath it between a
day agenda, a week list and a month grid, and picking a day in the week or month view opens it.

<Preview>
  <SegmentedControlExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from './segmented-control/SegmentedControl';

const views = [
  { value: 'day', label: 'Day' },
  { value: 'week', label: 'Week' },
  { value: 'month', label: 'Month' },
];

const [view, setView] = useState('day');

// tabs (the default): switch the panel below from your own state
<SegmentedControl id="view" label="View" options={views} value={view} onValueChange={setView} />
<div id="view-panel" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby={`view-${view}`}>
  {view === 'day' ? <DayAgenda /> : view === 'week' ? <WeekList /> : <MonthGrid />}
</div>

// radio: set an option rather than switch a view
<SegmentedControl label="Density" as="radio" options={views} defaultValue="week" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [SegmentedControlComponent] -->
<SegmentedControl id="view" label="View" [options]="views"
  [value]="view" (valueChange)="view = $event" />
<div id="view-panel" role="tabpanel" [attr.aria-labelledby]="'view-' + view">
  @switch (view) {
    @case ('day') { <ex-day-agenda /> }
    @case ('week') { <ex-week-list /> }
    @default { <ex-month-grid /> }
  }
</div>

<SegmentedControl label="Density" as="radio" [options]="views" defaultValue="week" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/segmented_control.dart';

SegmentedControl(
  label: 'View',
  options: const [
    SegmentOption(value: 'day', label: 'Day'),
    SegmentOption(value: 'week', label: 'Week'),
    SegmentOption(value: 'month', label: 'Month'),
  ],
  value: view,
  onValueChange: (v) => setState(() => view = v),
),
// switch the panel below from `view`
if (view == 'day') const DayAgenda()
else if (view == 'week') const WeekList()
else const MonthGrid(),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{ value: string; label: ReactNode }[]` | The choices, in order, left to right. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string` | The picked value. Pass `value` with `onValueChange` for a controlled control. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | Fires with the new value when the pick changes. |
| `label` | `string` | Names the group for screen readers, like `View`. Required. |
| `as` | `tabs \| radio` | `tabs` (the default) when it switches a panel, `radio` when it sets an option. |
| `id` | `string` | Ties the tabs to their panel: give the panel an id of the form "id-panel" and point its aria-labelledby at "id-value". Defaults to a generated id. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
track and sliding knob take the active theme's surface and accent colors; in Blueprint the control
is squared off, in Soft it is a pill with a rounder knob.


# Slider (/docs/components/slider)

Drag a thumb to set a value, or two thumbs for a `[low, high]` range. Give it discrete `step`s and
a labelled scale with `stops`, and mark a suggested value with `recommended`. Keyboard works too —
arrows step, Page keys jump by ten, Home/End go to the ends.

<Preview>
  <SliderExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Slider } from './slider/Slider';

<Slider label="Quality" value={v} onValueChange={setV} showValue />

<Slider
  label="Autonomy"
  step={20}
  value={a}
  onValueChange={setA}
  stops={[{ value: 0, label: 'Off' }, { value: 100, label: 'Full' }]}
  recommended={80}
/>

<Slider label="Budget" range={[20, 70]} onRangeChange={setR} format={(v) => `$${v}`} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [SliderComponent] -->
<Slider label="Quality" [value]="v" (valueChange)="v = $event" [showValue]="true"></Slider>

<Slider
  label="Autonomy"
  [step]="20"
  [value]="a"
  (valueChange)="a = $event"
  [stops]="[{ value: 0, label: 'Off' }, { value: 100, label: 'Full' }]"
  [recommended]="80"
></Slider>

<Slider label="Budget" [range]="[20, 70]" (rangeChange)="r = $event"></Slider>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/slider.dart';

VoSlider(label: 'Quality', value: v, onValueChanged: (x) => setState(() => v = x), showValue: true),

VoSlider(
  label: 'Autonomy',
  step: 20,
  value: a,
  onValueChanged: (x) => setState(() => a = x),
  stops: const [SliderStop(value: 0, label: 'Off'), SliderStop(value: 100, label: 'Full')],
  recommended: 80,
),

VoSlider(label: 'Budget', range: (20, 70), onRangeChanged: (r) => setState(() => range = r)),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `min` / `max` | `number` | The ends of the track. `0` and `100` by default. |
| `step` | `number` | Step between values. `1` by default; `0` for a continuous track. |
| `value` / `onValueChange` | `number` / `callback` | A single thumb. The value and its change handler. |
| `range` / `onRangeChange` | `[number, number]` / `callback` | Two thumbs for a `[low, high]` range. |
| `stops` | `{ value, label }[]` | A labelled scale drawn under the track. Click a stop to jump to it (single value). |
| `recommended` | `number` | A value marked on the track as the agent's suggestion. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | Shows the value in a bubble above the active thumb. |
| `format` | `(value) => string` | Formats the displayed value, e.g. `` v => `$${v}` ``. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Turns off interaction and dims the slider. |
| `label` | `string` | Accessible name for the slider. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The fill
and thumbs take the accent, the rail and ticks the field/line tokens, and the recommended mark the
accent's ring colour — all from `--vo-*`, so it recolours with the theme automatically.


# Source stack (/docs/components/source-stack)

An answer with its sources folded into one quiet pill. Open the pill to see each source as a row —
its favicon, where it came from and a small bar for how much it counted — and use the filter chips
to pick by `kind` (`web`, `file`, `figma`, …). Each source takes a `title`, a `host`, a `relevance`
from 0 to 1, a `mark` for the favicon square and its `color`; give one an `onOpen` and it grows an
open button on hover. Leave `open` and `filter` out to let the pill and chips drive themselves.

<Preview>
  <SourceStackExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { SourceStack, type StackSource } from './source-stack/SourceStack';

const sources: StackSource[] = [
  { kind: 'web', title: 'Baymard: pricing page UX', host: 'baymard.com', relevance: 0.92, mark: 'B', color: 'var(--vo-pb)', onOpen: () => open(url) },
  { kind: 'file', title: 'Q3 conversion export.csv', host: 'Drive', relevance: 0.84, mark: 'CSV', color: 'var(--vo-pm)' },
];

<SourceStack sources={sources}>
  Annual plans convert about 18% better when the monthly price is shown crossed out.
</SourceStack>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [SourceStackComponent] -->
sources: StackSource[] = [
  { kind: 'web', title: 'Baymard: pricing page UX', host: 'baymard.com', relevance: 0.92, mark: 'B', color: 'var(--vo-pb)', onOpen: () => this.open(url) },
  { kind: 'file', title: 'Q3 conversion export.csv', host: 'Drive', relevance: 0.84, mark: 'CSV', color: 'var(--vo-pm)' },
];

<SourceStack
  [sources]="sources"
  message="Annual plans convert about 18% better when the monthly price is shown crossed out."
  (openChange)="onOpenChange($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/source_stack.dart';

SourceStack(
  message: 'Annual plans convert about 18% better when shown crossed out.',
  sources: [
    StackSource(kind: 'web', title: 'Baymard: pricing page UX', host: 'baymard.com', relevance: 0.92, mark: 'B', color: c.accentMark, onOpen: () => open(url)),
    StackSource(kind: 'file', title: 'Q3 conversion export.csv', host: 'Drive', relevance: 0.84, mark: 'CSV', color: c.fg2),
  ],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` / `message` | `ReactNode` / `string` | The answer the sources back up, shown above the pill. |
| `sources` | `StackSource[]` | The sources, drawn as rows when the stack is open. |
| `filters` | `SourceFilter[]` | The chips above the list. Defaults to All, Web, Files and Figma. |
| `filter` | `string` | The chosen filter. Leave it out to let the chips switch it. |
| `defaultFilter` | `string` | The filter to start on when uncontrolled. Defaults to `all`. |
| `onFilterChange` | `(filter) => void` | Called when a chip is picked. |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the list is open. Leave it out to let the pill toggle it. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Whether it starts open when uncontrolled. Defaults to `false`. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open) => void` | Called when the pill toggles the list. |
| `source.kind` | `string` | What kind of source it is; the chips pick by this, like `web`, `file` or `figma`. |
| `source.title` | `string` | The source's name. |
| `source.host` | `string` | Where it came from, like `baymard.com` or `Drive`. |
| `source.relevance` | `number` | 0 to 1, drawn as a small bar. |
| `source.mark` | `string` | One to three letters in the favicon square, like `B` or `CSV`. |
| `source.color` | `string` | The favicon colour, any CSS colour. |
| `source.onOpen` | `() => void` | Adds an open button that shows on hover. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The pill
and rows ride the shared `--vo-*` tokens; the filter chips are white with a dimmed edge that steps up
on the picked one, and the relevance bars fill with `--vo-accent-mark`. In Soft the chips and rows are
rounder. The entrance stagger and the one-time auto-open are skipped under reduced motion.


# Stat cards (/docs/components/stat-cards)

Stat cards are a row of numbers that matter. Each card has an icon, a label, the value in large
type, its change against the period before (green from zero, red below), and a sparkline in its own
colour. A `period` switch along the top rolls the numbers to their new values and redraws every
line.

<Preview>
  <StatCardsExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { StatCards } from './stat-cards/StatCards';

const stats = [
  {
    icon: 'spark',
    label: 'Agent runs',
    values: [
      { value: 1842, change: 12.4, points: [980, 1120, 1070, 1260, 1410, 1550, 1842] },
      { value: 7320, change: 8.1, points: [5200, 5600, 5900, 6100, 6600, 6950, 7320] },
    ],
  },
  { icon: 'coins', label: 'Cost', prefix: '$', values: [/* one entry per period */] },
];

const periods = [
  { label: '7 days', compare: 'vs previous 7 days' },
  { label: '30 days', compare: 'vs previous 30 days' },
];

<StatCards stats={stats} periods={periods} defaultPeriod={0} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [StatCardsComponent] -->
<StatCards
  [stats]="stats"
  [periods]="periods"
  [defaultPeriod]="0"
  (periodChange)="onPeriod($event)"
></StatCards>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/stat_cards.dart';

StatCards(
  stats: [
    StatCardsStat(
      icon: IconName.spark,
      label: 'Agent runs',
      values: [
        StatCardsValue(value: 1842, change: 12.4, points: [980, 1120, 1260, 1410, 1842]),
        StatCardsValue(value: 7320, change: 8.1, points: [5200, 5900, 6600, 6950, 7320]),
      ],
    ),
  ],
  periods: const [
    StatCardsPeriod(label: '7 days', compare: 'vs previous 7 days'),
    StatCardsPeriod(label: '30 days', compare: 'vs previous 30 days'),
  ],
  defaultPeriod: 0,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stats` | `StatCardsStat[]` | The cards. Each has an `icon`, `label`, one `values` entry per period, and optional `prefix`, `suffix` and `color`. |
| `periods` | `StatCardsPeriod[]` | The switch options. Each has a `label` and an optional `compare` line shown on hover. |
| `period` | `number` | The period on show, by index. Leave it out to let the switch pick it. |
| `defaultPeriod` | `number` | The period shown first when uncontrolled. Defaults to `0`. |
| `onPeriodChange` | `(period: number) => void` | Called with the new index when the switch changes. |
| `sparkRange` | `[number, number]` | The bottom and top of every sparkline. Defaults to each card's own range. |

Each `StatCardsStat` carries `values: { value, change, points }[]` — one entry per period, in the
same order as `periods` — where `value` is the number, `change` is the percent against the period
before, and `points` is the sparkline oldest first.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the cards are squared off with hairline borders; in Soft they are rounded panels with a
softer shadow. The sparkline colours fall back to the chart palette (the accent, then violet, green
and orange) unless a card sets its own `color`.


# Status pill (/docs/components/status-pill)

A status pill shows a single line of what the agent is up to. Its `state` picks the glyph and
colour — `thinking`, `reading` and `working` shimmer while they run — and a new `state`, `label`,
`file` or `action` fades the old line out before the new one arrives. The `bar` variant is taller
and draws a `progress` track along its bottom.

<Preview>
  <StatusPillExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { StatusPill } from './status-pill/StatusPill';

<StatusPill state="reading" label="Reading repository" meta="2 of 4" />
<StatusPill state="working" label="Editing" file={{ name: 'PricingCard.tsx', type: 'tsx' }} />
<StatusPill state="waiting" label="Needs your review" action={{ label: 'Open', onClick: open }} />
<StatusPill variant="bar" state="working" label="Writing tests" progress={80} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [StatusPillComponent] -->
<StatusPill state="reading" label="Reading repository" meta="2 of 4" />
<StatusPill state="working" label="Editing" [file]="{ name: 'PricingCard.tsx', type: 'tsx' }" />
<StatusPill state="waiting" label="Needs your review" [action]="{ label: 'Open', onClick: open }" />
<StatusPill variant="bar" state="working" label="Writing tests" [progress]="80" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/status_pill.dart';

const StatusPill(state: StatusPillState.reading, label: 'Reading repository', meta: '2 of 4'),
const StatusPill(state: StatusPillState.working, label: 'Editing', file: StatusFile('PricingCard.tsx', type: 'tsx')),
StatusPill(state: StatusPillState.waiting, label: 'Needs your review', action: StatusAction('Open', onClick: open)),
const StatusPill(variant: StatusPillVariant.bar, state: StatusPillState.working, label: 'Writing tests', progress: 80),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | What the agent is doing, in a few words. Required. |
| `state` | `idle \| thinking \| reading \| working \| waiting \| done` | Picks the glyph and colour. `thinking`, `reading` and `working` shimmer while they run. |
| `meta` | `string` | Quiet detail after the label, like "2 of 4". Changing only this does not restart the pill. |
| `file` | `{ name: string; type?: string }` | A file chip after the label. |
| `action` | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` | A button at the end, for when the agent needs the person. |
| `progress` | `number` | 0 to 100, drawn as a track along the bottom of the `bar` variant. |
| `variant` | `pill \| bar` | `pill` hugs its content; `bar` is taller and leaves room for the progress track. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The pill
sits on a surface with the shared shadow, so it picks up the theme's surface and token colours; in
Soft it is rounder, and in dark it reads against the dark stage.


# Steering (/docs/components/steering)

Steering shows a run you can nudge while it works: its `steps`, the log of what you told it and
what it said back, and a message box. A message waits for the step in progress, then the agent
takes it up from the next one — so you change its course without starting over. When your steer
touches work already done, the agent raises an amber heads-up with `actions` (like *Leave it* or
*Redo the Pro card*) and settles on an `answer` once you choose.

<Preview>
  <SteeringExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Steering, type SteerStep, type SteerMessage } from './steering/Steering';

const [steps, setSteps] = useState<SteerStep[]>([
  { id: 'read', title: 'Read Pricing v4', detail: '3 frames, 14 layers', status: 'done' },
  { id: 'pro', title: 'Update the Pro card', detail: 'Setting the accent to violet', status: 'running' },
  { id: 'team', title: 'Update the Team card', status: 'queued' },
]);
const [messages, setMessages] = useState<SteerMessage[]>([]);

<Steering
  title="Redesign the pricing page"
  steps={steps}
  messages={messages}
  onSend={(text) =>
    setMessages((m) => [...m, { id: crypto.randomUUID(), from: 'you', text, state: 'queued' }])
  }
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [SteeringComponent] -->
steps: SteerStep[] = [
  { id: 'read', title: 'Read Pricing v4', detail: '3 frames, 14 layers', status: 'done' },
  { id: 'pro', title: 'Update the Pro card', detail: 'Setting the accent to violet', status: 'running' },
  { id: 'team', title: 'Update the Team card', status: 'queued' },
];
messages: SteerMessage[] = [];

<Steering
  title="Redesign the pricing page"
  [steps]="steps"
  [messages]="messages"
  (sendMessage)="queue($event)"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/steering.dart';

Steering(
  title: 'Redesign the pricing page',
  steps: const [
    SteerStep(id: 'read', title: 'Read Pricing v4', detail: '3 frames, 14 layers', status: SteerStepStatus.done),
    SteerStep(id: 'pro', title: 'Update the Pro card', detail: 'Setting the accent to violet', status: SteerStepStatus.running),
    SteerStep(id: 'team', title: 'Update the Team card', status: SteerStepStatus.queued),
  ],
  messages: messages,
  onSend: (text) => setState(() => messages = [...messages, SteerMessage(id: text, from: SteerFrom.you, text: text, state: SteerMessageState.queued)]),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The run's goal, like "Redesign the pricing page". |
| `steps` | `SteerStep[]` | The steps of the run, each `queued`, `running` or `done`. |
| `messages` | `SteerMessage[]` | What you sent and what the agent said back, in order. |
| `onSend` | `(text) => void` | Called with the text when a message is sent. Add it to `messages` as `queued`, then mark it `applied` once taken up. |
| `value` | `string` | The message being written. Leave it out to let the box keep its own draft. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` | Called as the draft changes. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Defaults to "Steer the agent while it works", and "The run has finished" once every step is done. |
| `status` | `string` | The line under the title. Defaults to "Step 2 of 4", or "Done". |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds to show as `m:ss`. Leave it out to let the clock count until every step is done. |
| `summary` | `string \| false` | Shown once every step is done. Defaults to "Done in 0:14 · 1 change from you"; `false` hides it. |
| `SteerStep` | `{ id; title; detail?; status; fromYou? }` | A step; `fromYou` tags one your steer added. |
| `SteerMessage` | `{ id; from; text; state?; warn?; actions?; answer? }` | A log line; the agent's can carry an amber `warn`, `actions` and an `answer`. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface with the panel shadow; the running glyph spins in the accent, a done step turns
the tick green, your messages sit in a chip bubble on the right, and the agent's heads-up tints
amber until you answer it. All colours, radii and spacing come from the theme tokens, so in Soft the
card, pills and message box are rounder.


# Step Loader (/docs/components/step-loader)

A step loader shows an agent's work as named steps. The step running now sits beside a small
loader; a track below fills as steps finish; and the row expands to the full list, each line
switching to its `done` text once complete. When `current` reaches the number of steps, every step
is done and the row shows the `doneLabel`.

<Preview>
  <StepLoaderExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { StepLoader } from './step-loader/StepLoader';

const steps = [
  { label: 'Reading Figma frames', done: 'Read 4 frames' },
  { label: 'Generating components', done: 'Made 6 components' },
  { label: 'Writing tests' },
];

<StepLoader steps={steps} current={1} loader="radar" />
<StepLoader steps={steps} current={steps.length} doneLabel="Ready for review" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [StepLoaderComponent] -->
<StepLoader [steps]="steps" [current]="1" loader="radar" />
<StepLoader [steps]="steps" [current]="steps.length" doneLabel="Ready for review" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/step_loader.dart';

StepLoader(
  steps: const [
    Step('Reading Figma frames', done: 'Read 4 frames'),
    Step('Generating components', done: 'Made 6 components'),
    Step('Writing tests'),
  ],
  current: 1,
  loader: StepLoaderGlyph.radar,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `{ label: string; done?: string }[]` | The steps. `label` shows while running, `done` once finished (falls back to `label`). |
| `current` | `number` | Index of the step running now. `steps.length` or more means every step is done. |
| `loader` | `radar \| dots \| ring \| bars` | The loader glyph beside the running step. `radar` by default. |
| `doneLabel` | `string` | Label once every step is done. `Ready for review` by default. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Whether the full list is open. Leave `open` out to let the row toggle it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `callback` | Fires when the row opens or closes the list. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
track and loader take the accent color from the active theme; in Soft the row and track are softer
and more rounded than in Blueprint.


# Task table (/docs/components/task-table)

Agent tasks in a table you can sort by any column. Pick rows with the checkboxes — or the
select-all in the header — and the header turns into what you can do to the selection: `pause`,
`retry` or `cancel`. Rows glide to their new places when the order changes, cancelled rows slide
away, and when the last task is gone the table says so.

<Preview>
  <TaskTableExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { TaskTable, type Task } from './task-table/TaskTable';

const tasks: Task[] = [
  { id: '1', name: 'Audit pricing contrast', status: 'running',
    agent: { name: 'Design', initials: 'DS', color: 'var(--vo-av-b)' }, cost: 0.42, updated: 2 },
  { id: '2', name: 'Export tokens to CSS', status: 'done',
    agent: { name: 'Code', initials: 'CO', color: 'var(--vo-av-m)' }, cost: 0.18, updated: 14 },
];

<TaskTable
  tasks={tasks}
  onAction={(action, ids) => run(action, ids)}
  emptyAction={{ label: 'Bring them back', onClick: reset }}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [TaskTableComponent] -->
tasks: Task[] = [
  { id: '1', name: 'Audit pricing contrast', status: 'running',
    agent: { name: 'Design', initials: 'DS', color: 'var(--vo-av-b)' }, cost: 0.42, updated: 2 },
];

<TaskTable
  [tasks]="tasks"
  (action)="run($event.action, $event.ids)"
  (selectedChange)="selected = $event"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/task_table.dart';

TaskTable(
  tasks: const [
    Task(
      id: '1',
      name: 'Audit pricing contrast',
      status: TaskStatus.running,
      agent: TaskAgent(name: 'Design', initials: 'DS', color: Color(0xFF126FE6)),
      cost: 0.42,
      updated: 2,
    ),
  ],
  onAction: (action, ids) => run(action, ids),
);
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tasks` | `Task[]` | The tasks to show. Each has an `id`, `name`, `status`, `agent`, `cost` and `updated`. |
| `title` | `string` | The name in the header. Defaults to `"Agent tasks"`. |
| `summary` | `string` | The quiet line beside the name. Defaults to a count of tasks and how many are running. |
| `selected` / `defaultSelected` | `string[]` | The ids of the selected tasks. Leave `selected` out to let the checkboxes and rows drive it. |
| `onSelectedChange` | `(ids) => void` | Called when the selection changes. |
| `sort` / `defaultSort` | `{ key; desc? }` | The column the rows are sorted by. Defaults to `updated`, newest first. |
| `onSortChange` | `(sort) => void` | Called when a header sets the sort. |
| `onAction` | `(action, ids) => void` | A bulk action (`pause` \| `retry` \| `cancel`). The selection clears after it; cancelled rows slide away first. |
| `empty` / `emptyAction` | `ReactNode` / `{ label; onClick }` | What shows when there are no tasks, and an optional button under it. |

`Task.status` is one of `running`, `failed`, `queued`, `paused` or `done`. `Task.agent` is
`{ name, initials, color }`, where `color` is an avatar token like `var(--vo-av-b)`.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface and every colour comes from the theme tokens: the status pills tint from the
accent (Running), `--vo-ok` (Done) and `--vo-bad` (Failed), with Queued and Paused staying muted;
the checkbox fills with the accent and its tick springs in. The table reflows into a stacked layout
inside a narrow card via a container query, so it reads on a phone as well as full width.


# Terminal stream (/docs/components/terminal-stream)

A compact terminal for the shell commands an agent runs: the working directory and how the run is
going in the header, each command with its output streaming in under it and an exit code or a check
with how long it took, and a summary at the foot once it is over. Notes and edits sit between the
commands — a note the agent writes about what went wrong, and the edit that fixes it. Long output
folds to its last lines. The terminal keeps one height (420px) and its output scrolls, staying on
the newest line unless the reader has scrolled up.

<Preview>
  <TerminalStreamExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { TerminalStream, type TerminalEntry } from './terminal-stream/TerminalStream';

const entries: TerminalEntry[] = [
  { command: 'npm run build', status: 'ok', duration: '6.1 s', output: ['✓ built in 6.1s'] },
  { kind: 'note', text: 'The test expects whole dollars. Dropping the cents for round amounts.' },
  { kind: 'edit', file: 'src/lib/price.ts', added: 2, removed: 1, status: 'done',
    diff: ['- return `$${n.toFixed(2)}`', '+ return `$${v}`'] },
  { command: 'npm test', status: 'ok', duration: '2.9 s', output: [{ text: 'Tests  24 passed (24)', tone: 'ok' }] },
];

<TerminalStream cwd="~/acme/web" entries={entries} onStop={stop} onCopy={save} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [TerminalStreamComponent] -->
entries: TerminalEntry[] = [
  { command: 'npm run build', status: 'ok', duration: '6.1 s', output: ['✓ built in 6.1s'] },
  { kind: 'note', text: 'Dropping the cents for round amounts.' },
  { command: 'npm test', status: 'ok', duration: '2.9 s', output: [{ text: 'Tests  24 passed (24)', tone: 'ok' }] },
];

<TerminalStream [cwd]="'~/acme/web'" [entries]="entries" (stop)="onStop()" (copy)="onCopy($event)" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/terminal_stream.dart';

TerminalStream(
  cwd: '~/acme/web',
  entries: const [
    TerminalCommand(
      command: 'npm run build',
      status: TerminalCommandStatus.ok,
      duration: '6.1 s',
      output: [TerminalLine('✓ built in 6.1s', tone: TerminalTone.ok)],
    ),
    TerminalNote('Dropping the cents for round amounts.'),
    TerminalCommand(
      command: 'npm test',
      status: TerminalCommandStatus.ok,
      duration: '2.9 s',
      output: [TerminalLine('Tests  24 passed (24)', tone: TerminalTone.ok)],
    ),
  ],
  onStop: stop,
  onCopy: (text) => save(text),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cwd` | `string` | The working directory, shown in the header, like `~/acme/web`. |
| `entries` | `TerminalEntry[]` | Commands, notes and edits, oldest first. |
| `status` | `running \| passed \| failed \| stopped` | The run as a whole. Left out, it is derived from the entries. |
| `elapsed` | `string` | How long the run has taken, like `0:18`. Shown beside Running and in the summary. |
| `summary` | `string \| false` | The line at the foot once the run is over. `false` hides it. |
| `tail` | `number` | How many lines a folded output keeps showing. Default `4`. |
| `onStop` | `() => void` | Adds the Stop button while the run is going. |
| `onCopy` | `(text) => void` | Called with the whole run as text when it is copied. |
| `entry.command` | `string` | A command, like `npm run build`, with its `output` and `status`. |
| `entry.output` | `(string \| { text; tone? })[]` | What it printed; `tone` is `ok`, `bad` or `muted`. |
| `entry.status` | `running \| ok \| failed \| stopped` | A spinner, a check, an `Exit N` tag, or a Stopped tag. |
| `note.text` | `string` | A line from the agent between commands. The newest shimmers while the run goes on. |
| `edit.file` | `string` | A file the agent edits, with its `added`/`removed` counts and a `diff`. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The output
is 12px monospace on a 1.8 line height, the state tag and left rail take the accent while the run is
live and turn green or red once it is over, and a block cursor blinks after the newest line — all drawn
from the theme tokens. In the Blueprint style the rail thins and the cursor marches; Soft rounds the
corners and the scrollbar.


# Thinking States (/docs/components/thinking-states)

A thinking state is a small animated mark beside a status line. Pick one of ten marks with
`variant`; give it `steps` and, with more than one, they take turns every `interval` unless you
drive the index with `current`. An elapsed-seconds counter sits at the end of the line and counts
by itself unless you set `seconds` or hide it with `seconds={false}`.

The marks are `orbit` (a light running round a ring, the line shimmering), `morph` (a rectangle,
circle and triangle in turn), `scan` (a column sweeping rows of dots), `stream` (dots filling in,
the line typed out behind a caret), `matrix` (a dot grid twinkling at random), `stack` (pages
shuffling to the front), `pulse` (a core breathing with sonar rings growing out of it), `wave`
(bars rising and falling in a travelling waveform), `bounce` (three dots hopping in turn) and
`spiral` (dots lighting up along an inward spiral toward the centre).

<Preview>
  <ThinkingStatesExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ThinkingStates } from './thinking-states/ThinkingStates';

const steps = ['Thinking', 'Reading 3 files', 'Planning the change'];

<ThinkingStates variant="orbit" steps={steps} />
<ThinkingStates variant="stream" steps={steps} interval={2600} />
<ThinkingStates variant="scan" steps={steps} seconds={false} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ThinkingStatesComponent] -->
<ThinkingStates variant="orbit" [steps]="steps" />
<ThinkingStates variant="stream" [steps]="steps" [interval]="2600" />
<ThinkingStates variant="scan" [steps]="steps" [seconds]="false" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/thinking_states.dart';

const steps = ['Thinking', 'Reading 3 files', 'Planning the change'];

ThinkingStates(variant: ThinkingVariant.orbit, steps: steps),
ThinkingStates(variant: ThinkingVariant.stream, steps: steps, interval: 2600),
ThinkingStates(variant: ThinkingVariant.scan, steps: steps, seconds: false),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `orbit \| morph \| scan \| stream \| matrix \| stack \| pulse \| wave \| bounce \| spiral` | Which indicator to draw. `orbit` by default. |
| `steps` | `string[]` | The status lines. With more than one they take turns unless `current` is set. |
| `current` | `number` | Index of the line to show. Leave it out to let the lines take turns by themselves. |
| `interval` | `number` | Milliseconds each line shows for when they take turns. `2600` by default. |
| `seconds` | `number \| false` | Seconds shown at the end of the line. Counts by itself when left out; `false` hides it. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
marks and the typed line use the active theme's accent and text colors; the counter is set in the
numeric style. Motion is paused for readers who prefer reduced motion — the line is shown whole
rather than typed.


# Thinking (/docs/components/thinking)

A thinking trace is the reasoning log an agent writes as it works. Each step arrives on a line that
spins while it runs and turns into a green check once it finishes, with what it found written under
it and how long it took at its right. The header counts seconds while it runs; once the last step
lands it becomes a summary of the work and the trace folds itself away.

<Preview>
  <ThinkingExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Thinking } from './thinking/Thinking';

<Thinking
  running={running}
  title="Checking the pricing page"
  summary="3 cards to fix, 2 changes planned"
  steps={[
    { label: 'Measure the plan cards', state: 'done', result: '3 cards are off the 8px grid', time: '1.4s' },
    { label: 'Plan the fix', state: 'running' },
  ]}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ThinkingComponent] -->
<Thinking
  [running]="running"
  title="Checking the pricing page"
  summary="3 cards to fix, 2 changes planned"
  [steps]="steps"
></Thinking>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/thinking.dart';

Thinking(
  running: running,
  title: 'Checking the pricing page',
  summary: '3 cards to fix, 2 changes planned',
  steps: const [
    ThinkingStep(label: 'Measure the plan cards', state: ThinkingStepState.done, result: '3 cards are off the 8px grid', time: '1.4s'),
    ThinkingStep(label: 'Plan the fix', state: ThinkingStepState.running),
  ],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `ThinkingStep[]` | The steps the agent has taken so far. Each has a `label`, a `state` of `running`, `retry` or `done`, an optional `result` and `time`. |
| `running` | `boolean` | Spins, counts seconds and keeps the trace open while true. |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds to show. Leave it out to let it count while running. |
| `title` | `string` | The header while it runs, like "Checking the pricing page". |
| `summary` | `string` | The header once it is done. Defaults to the number of steps. |
| `collapseWhenDone` | `boolean` | Folds the trace away a moment after it finishes. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | Whether the trace is open. Leave `open` out to let the header toggle it. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
running step turns in the accent with a soft halo, finished steps and the rail between them turn
green, and a slow step waits in amber. In Blueprint the marks are squared off and the result writes
in with a plain fade instead of a blur.


# Thread panel (/docs/components/thread-panel)

A thread panel holds several conversations with an agent, one tab each, with a reply field
under the open one. The tabs switch which thread is shown and an underline slides to the open
one; switching staggers that thread's messages in, and a later message glides into view. Each
`agent` message can carry `sources` — the files or pages it used — and a `thinking` message
shimmers while the agent works on a reply.

<Preview>
  <ThreadPanelExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ThreadPanel, type Thread } from './thread-panel/ThreadPanel';

const [threads, setThreads] = useState<Thread[]>([
  {
    id: 'onboarding',
    title: 'Onboarding',
    color: 'var(--vo-ok-mark)',
    messages: [
      { from: 'user', text: 'Why is the workspace step losing people?' },
      { from: 'agent', text: 'Moving the team-name step after the first project should help.' },
    ],
  },
]);

<ThreadPanel
  threads={threads}
  onSend={(text, threadId) =>
    setThreads((prev) =>
      prev.map((t) =>
        t.id === threadId ? { ...t, messages: [...t.messages, { from: 'user', text }] } : t,
      ),
    )
  }
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ThreadPanelComponent] -->
threads: Thread[] = [
  {
    id: 'onboarding',
    title: 'Onboarding',
    color: 'var(--vo-ok-mark)',
    messages: [
      { from: 'user', text: 'Why is the workspace step losing people?' },
      { from: 'agent', text: 'Moving the team-name step after the first project should help.' },
    ],
  },
];

<ThreadPanel [threads]="threads" (sendMessage)="add($event)" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/thread_panel.dart';

List<Thread> threads = const [
  Thread(
    id: 'onboarding',
    title: 'Onboarding',
    messages: [
      ThreadMessage(from: ThreadFrom.user, text: 'Why is the workspace step losing people?'),
      ThreadMessage(from: ThreadFrom.agent, text: 'Moving the team-name step after should help.'),
    ],
  ),
];

ThreadPanel(
  threads: threads,
  onSend: (text, threadId) => setState(() {/* add the message to that thread */}),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `threads` | `Thread[]` | The conversations, one tab each. |
| `value` | `string` | The id of the open thread. Leave it out to let the tabs switch it. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | The thread open at first when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first thread. |
| `onValueChange` | `(id) => void` | Called when a tab opens another thread. |
| `onSend` | `(text, threadId) => void` | Called with the reply and the open thread's id. Add the message to that thread to show it. |
| `draft` | `string` | The reply being written. Leave it out to let the field keep its own. |
| `defaultDraft` | `string` | The reply written at first when uncontrolled. |
| `onDraftChange` | `(text) => void` | Called as the reply field changes. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | The reply field's placeholder. Defaults to `Reply to the agent`. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Sits flat in a chat column (the default). Set `false` to give it a card of its own. |
| `Thread.color` | `string` | The dot in front of the title, any CSS colour. Defaults to a quiet grey. |
| `ThreadMessage.sources` | `Source[]` | Files or pages the agent used, shown as chips above its reply. |
| `ThreadMessage.thinking` | `boolean` | Shows a shimmering line while the agent works on a reply. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The
open tab's underline uses the accent mark token and the reply field sits on a surface with an
inset field line, so it reads against the dark stage; in Soft the field is rounder (squircle).


# Toast stack (/docs/components/toast-stack)

A toast stack collects notifications into a deck: the newest sits in front, older ones peek out
behind it. Hover the deck — or move the focus into it — and it fans out into a readable list; move
away and it folds back up. Each toast takes an `icon`, a `tone` for the badge colour, a `title`, an
optional `detail` line and a `time`. Pass the toasts oldest-first; dismiss one with its close button.

<Preview>
  <ToastStackExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ToastStack, type StackToast } from './toast-stack/ToastStack';

const [toasts, setToasts] = useState<StackToast[]>([
  { id: 1, icon: 'ok', tone: 'ok', title: 'Tests passed', detail: '42 of 42 in 38s', time: '2m' },
  { id: 2, icon: 'pr', tone: 'merge', title: 'PR #412 is ready', detail: 'Use shared spacing tokens', time: 'now' },
]);

<ToastStack toasts={toasts} onDismiss={(id) => setToasts((t) => t.filter((x) => x.id !== id))} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ToastStackComponent] -->
toasts: StackToast[] = [
  { id: 1, icon: 'ok', tone: 'ok', title: 'Tests passed', detail: '42 of 42 in 38s', time: '2m' },
  { id: 2, icon: 'pr', tone: 'merge', title: 'PR #412 is ready', time: 'now' },
];

<ToastStack [toasts]="toasts" (dismiss)="toasts = toasts.filter(t => t.id !== $event)" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/toast_stack.dart';

List<StackToast> toasts = const [
  StackToast(id: 1, icon: Icons.check_circle_outline, tone: ToastStackTone.ok, title: 'Tests passed', detail: '42 of 42 in 38s', time: '2m'),
  StackToast(id: 2, icon: Icons.merge, tone: ToastStackTone.merge, title: 'PR #412 is ready', time: 'now'),
];

ToastStack(
  toasts: toasts,
  onDismiss: (id) => setState(() => toasts = toasts.where((t) => t.id != id).toList()),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toasts` | `StackToast[]` | Oldest first. The last one sits in front. |
| `onDismiss` | `(id) => void` | Called when a toast's close button is pressed. Remove it from `toasts` and it slides away. |
| `expanded` | `boolean` | Fans the stack out. Leave it out to fan it while the pointer is over it. |
| `max` | `number` | How many toasts stay mounted. Older ones drop off the back. Defaults to `6`. |
| `toast.id` | `string \| number` | Identity of the toast; a new one rises in, a removed one slides away. |
| `toast.icon` | `IconName` | The icon in the round badge. |
| `toast.tone` | `neutral \| ok \| warn \| bad \| merge \| blue \| purple \| …` | Colours the badge. Defaults to `neutral`. |
| `toast.title` | `string` | The bold first line. |
| `toast.detail` | `string` | The quiet line under the title. |
| `toast.time` | `string` | A short time like `now` or `2m`, shown until the close button takes its place. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). Each toast
sits on a surface with the toast shadow and its badge tint comes from the theme tokens, so the deck
reads against the dark stage; in Soft the cards are rounder. The fan-out and the arrival and dismiss
motion are tuned down when the viewer prefers reduced motion.


# Toast (/docs/components/toast)

A toast is a short message on a surface. Its `tone` picks the icon and colour — `loading` spins —
and it takes a `title`, an optional `description` and an optional `action` button. Pass a new `id`
to slide a new toast in and the old one away; keep the same `id` to change the text in place.

<Preview>
  <ToastExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Toast, type ToastData } from './toast/Toast';

const [toast, setToast] = useState<ToastData | null>(null);

setToast({ id: 1, tone: 'success', title: 'Deploy succeeded', description: 'Live in production.' });
setToast({
  id: 2,
  tone: 'error',
  title: 'Build failed',
  action: { label: 'Retry', onClick: retry, variant: 'primary' },
});

<Toast toast={toast} onDismiss={() => setToast(null)} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ToastComponent] -->
toast: ToastData | null = {
  id: 1, tone: 'success', title: 'Deploy succeeded', description: 'Live in production.'
};

<Toast [toast]="toast" (dismiss)="toast = null" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/toast.dart';

ToastData? toast = const ToastData(
  id: 1, tone: ToastTone.success, title: 'Deploy succeeded', description: 'Live in production.',
);

Toast(toast: toast, onDismiss: (id) => setState(() => toast = null)),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toast` | `ToastData \| null` | The toast to show, or `null` for none. |
| `onDismiss` | `(id) => void` | Called by the close button. The toast leaves either way. |
| `toast.id` | `string \| number` | A new id slides a new toast in and the old one away. Keep it to change text in place. |
| `toast.tone` | `success \| error \| info \| loading` | Picks the icon and its colour. `loading` spins. |
| `toast.title` | `string` | The bold first line. |
| `toast.description` | `string` | The quieter line under the title. Crossfades when it changes. |
| `toast.action` | `{ label; onClick; variant?: ghost \| primary \| ink; busy? }` | A button before the close button, like Undo or Retry. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface with the toast shadow and its tone tints come from the theme tokens, so it reads
against the dark stage; in Soft the card and its buttons are rounder.


# Tool call (/docs/components/tool-call)

The tools an agent calls, shown between its message and its answer. Each call takes a `server`,
a `name` and a `state` — `queued` waits, `running` spins, `done` shows how long it took and what
came back. Click a call to fold its `input` and `output` open or shut. The `reply` fades in once
every call is done.

<Preview>
  <ToolCallExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { ToolCall, type ToolCallItem } from './tool-call/ToolCall';

const calls: ToolCallItem[] = [
  {
    key: 'billing',
    server: 'billing',
    name: 'list_plan_changes',
    icon: 'coins',
    state: 'done',
    duration: '412 ms',
    input: { since: '2026-10-01' },
    output: [{ plan: 'Pro', price: 24 }, { plan: 'Team', price: 48 }],
  },
];

<ToolCall
  message="Checking which plans changed this month."
  calls={calls}
  reply="Two plans changed. I updated their prices."
  defaultOpen={['billing']}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [ToolCallComponent] -->
calls: ToolCallItem[] = [{
  key: 'billing', server: 'billing', name: 'list_plan_changes', icon: 'coins',
  state: 'done', duration: '412 ms',
  input: { since: '2026-10-01' },
  output: [{ plan: 'Pro', price: 24 }, { plan: 'Team', price: 48 }],
}];

<ToolCall
  message="Checking which plans changed this month."
  [calls]="calls"
  reply="Two plans changed. I updated their prices."
  [defaultOpen]="['billing']"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/tool_call.dart';

const calls = [
  ToolCallItem(
    key: 'billing', server: 'billing', name: 'list_plan_changes',
    icon: Icons.monetization_on_outlined,
    state: ToolCallState.done, duration: '412 ms',
    input: {'since': '2026-10-01'}, hasInput: true,
    output: [{'plan': 'Pro', 'price': 24}, {'plan': 'Team', 'price': 48}], hasOutput: true,
  ),
];

ToolCall(
  message: 'Checking which plans changed this month.',
  calls: calls,
  reply: 'Two plans changed. I updated their prices.',
  defaultOpen: const ['billing'],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `ReactNode` | The agent's message before the calls. |
| `calls` | `ToolCallItem[]` | The tools the agent called, each a row that folds open. |
| `reply` | `ReactNode` | The agent's answer after the calls. It fades in once every call is done. |
| `open` | `string[]` | Keys of the calls that are open. Leave it out to let each call toggle itself. |
| `defaultOpen` | `string[]` | The calls open at first when `open` is uncontrolled. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: string[]) => void` | Called with the new open set whenever a call is toggled. |
| `call.server` | `string` | The tool's server or namespace, like `billing`. |
| `call.name` | `string` | The tool's name, like `list_plan_changes`. |
| `call.icon` | `IconName` | The icon in front of the call. |
| `call.state` | `queued \| running \| done` | `queued` waits, `running` spins, `done` shows the time and output. |
| `call.duration` | `string` | How long it took, like `412 ms`. Shown once done. |
| `call.input` | `Json` | What the agent sent, shown as highlighted JSON. |
| `call.output` | `Json` | What came back, shown once done. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The call
rows sit on the stage with a chip-tinted icon badge and chip-tinted JSON blocks; keys, strings and
numbers take their own palette tokens, and the running spinner and fold motion follow the shared
ease. In Soft the rows and JSON blocks are rounder.


# Tooltip (/docs/components/tooltip)

A tooltip is the label that waits a moment under a toolbar button, then follows the pointer
instantly as it moves between them. Buttons come in `groups` with a line between, each with a `tip`
and an optional shortcut (`kbd`). Avatars at the end get a richer card instead — a person's name,
role and what they are doing now, with an agent shown by its thinking dots.

<Preview>
  <TooltipExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from './tooltip/Tooltip';

const groups = [
  [
    { key: 'undo', icon: 'undo', label: 'Undo', kbd: '⌘Z' },
    { key: 'ask', icon: 'spark', label: 'Ask agent', tip: 'Ask the agent', kbd: '⌘J' },
  ],
  [{ key: 'share', icon: 'users', label: 'Share', tip: 'Share with your team' }],
];

const people = [
  { key: 'mira', initials: 'MC', color: 'var(--vo-av-l)', name: 'Mira Chen', role: 'Design lead', status: 'Editing Pricing, frame 2' },
  { key: 'agent', initials: 'AI', color: 'var(--vo-av-p)', name: 'Visuno agent', role: 'Assistant', status: 'Drafting release notes', working: true },
];

<Tooltip groups={groups} people={people} note="Hover a button for its tip." />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [TooltipComponent] -->
<Tooltip
  [groups]="groups"
  [people]="people"
  note="Hover a button for its tip."
></Tooltip>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/tooltip.dart';

Tooltip(
  groups: [
    [
      TooltipTool(key: 'undo', icon: IconName.undo, label: 'Undo', kbd: '⌘Z'),
      TooltipTool(key: 'ask', icon: IconName.spark, label: 'Ask agent', tip: 'Ask the agent', kbd: '⌘J'),
    ],
    [TooltipTool(key: 'share', icon: IconName.users, label: 'Share', tip: 'Share with your team')],
  ],
  people: const [
    TooltipPerson(key: 'mira', initials: 'MC', color: 'var(--vo-av-l)', name: 'Mira Chen', role: 'Design lead', status: 'Editing Pricing, frame 2'),
    TooltipPerson(key: 'agent', initials: 'AI', color: 'var(--vo-av-p)', name: 'Visuno agent', role: 'Assistant', status: 'Drafting release notes', working: true),
  ],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `groups` | `TooltipTool[][]` | The toolbar's buttons, in groups with a line between. Each tool is `{ key, icon, label, tip?, kbd?, onClick? }`. |
| `people` | `TooltipPerson[]` | Avatars at the end. Each is `{ key, initials, color, name, role, status, working? }`; hovering one shows a card. |
| `note` | `ReactNode` | A quiet line under the toolbar. |
| `cardDelay` | `number` | How long a person card waits before it shows. Defaults to `300`. |
| `openTip` | `string \| null` | Shows this tool's tip by key, as if hovered. Leave it out to let the pointer decide. |
| `openCard` | `string \| null` | Shows this person's card by key, as if hovered. |

A tool's `tip` overrides its `label` in the tooltip, so set it only when the tip should say more
than the button's name; the `kbd` shortcut is shown after it. A person's `working: true` swaps the
green status dot for the agent's thinking dots.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the bar and card are squared off with hairline borders; in Soft they are rounded panels.
The tooltip itself and the avatar colours (`--vo-av-*`) come from the theme, so they stay legible on
either background.


# Top pages (/docs/components/top-pages)

A ranked list of a site's most visited pages. Each row shows its rank, title and path, a share bar
against the busiest page, the view count and the percent change (green from `0`, red below). The
running total rolls up, and the `Views` / `Change` sort switch slides the rows into their new order.

<Preview>
  <TopPagesExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { TopPages, type TopPagesPage } from './top-pages/TopPages';

const pages: TopPagesPage[] = [
  { path: '/pricing', title: 'Pricing', views: 18420, change: 24 },
  { path: '/', title: 'Home', views: 15210, change: 3 },
  { path: '/components', title: 'Components', views: 9870, change: 41 },
];

<TopPages pages={pages} site="visuno.dev" period="last 30 days" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [TopPagesComponent] -->
pages: TopPagesPage[] = [
  { path: '/pricing', title: 'Pricing', views: 18420, change: 24 },
  { path: '/', title: 'Home', views: 15210, change: 3 },
];

<TopPages [pages]="pages" site="visuno.dev" period="last 30 days" />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/top_pages.dart';

TopPages(
  pages: const [
    TopPagesPage(path: '/pricing', title: 'Pricing', views: 18420, change: 24),
    TopPagesPage(path: '/', title: 'Home', views: 15210, change: 3),
  ],
  site: 'visuno.dev',
  period: 'last 30 days',
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pages` | `TopPagesPage[]` | The page rows. Each has `path`, `title`, `views` and `change`. |
| `title` | `string` | Header text. Defaults to `Top pages`. |
| `period` | `string` | After the total, like `last 30 days`. |
