| `site` | `string` | Put in front of each path in the row tips, like `visuno.dev`. |
| `sort` | `views \| change` | How the rows are ordered. Leave it out to let the switch change it. |
| `defaultSort` | `views \| change` | The order before the switch is touched. Defaults to `views`. |
| `onSortChange` | `(sort) => void` | Fires when the sort switch changes. |
| `page.path` | `string` | The page's path, like `/pricing`. Also the row's key. |
| `page.title` | `string` | Its name, like `Pricing`. |
| `page.views` | `number` | Views over the period; the share bar is against the busiest page. |
| `page.change` | `number` | Change in percent, like `24` or `-8`. Green from `0`, red below. |
| `page.tip` | `string` | Shown on hover. Defaults to `site` + `path`. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The card
sits on a surface with the shared shadow; the share bars use the accent mark token, the change chips
the `ok` / `bad` tints, and the ranks the mono font — all from the theme tokens, so the list reads
the same against either background. In Soft the card and the sort switch are rounder.


# Trace view (/docs/components/trace-view)

A trace view lays one agent run out as a waterfall. Every span — an LLM call, a tool call, a
retrieval, a sub-agent — sits on a shared time axis, nested under the span that started it with a
tree's guides. Each kind has its own colour, counted in the key. While the run streams, a playhead
marks now and running bars glow at their leading edge; a tool call that runs over its budget turns
amber and hatched and is tagged slow. Open any span to see where it sat in the run, its input, its
output, its latency and its tokens.

<Preview>
  <TraceViewExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { TraceView } from './trace-view/TraceView';

const spans = [
  { id: 'run', name: 'Pricing research', kind: 'agent', start: 0, duration: 4.82, children: [
    { id: 'plan', name: 'Plan the steps', kind: 'llm', start: 0.04, duration: 0.62, tokens: 1240 },
    { id: 'fetch', name: 'fetch_page', kind: 'tool', start: 1.12, duration: 2.46, tokens: 3120 },
  ] },
];

<TraceView title="Pricing research" spans={spans} axis={5} />
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [TraceViewComponent] -->
spans: TraceSpan[] = [
  { id: 'run', name: 'Pricing research', kind: 'agent', start: 0, duration: 4.82, children: [
    { id: 'plan', name: 'Plan the steps', kind: 'llm', start: 0.04, duration: 0.62, tokens: 1240 },
    { id: 'fetch', name: 'fetch_page', kind: 'tool', start: 1.12, duration: 2.46, tokens: 3120 },
  ] },
];
```

```html
<TraceView
  title="Pricing research"
  [spans]="spans"
  [axis]="5"
  (selectedChange)="onSelect($event)"
></TraceView>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/trace_view.dart';

TraceView(
  title: 'Pricing research',
  axis: 5,
  spans: const [
    TraceSpan(id: 'run', name: 'Pricing research', kind: SpanKind.agent, start: 0, duration: 4.82, children: [
      TraceSpan(id: 'plan', name: 'Plan the steps', kind: SpanKind.llm, start: 0.04, duration: 0.62, tokens: 1240),
      TraceSpan(id: 'fetch', name: 'fetch_page', kind: SpanKind.tool, start: 1.12, duration: 2.46, tokens: 3120),
    ]),
  ],
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The run's name, shown over the status line. |
| `spans` | `TraceSpan[]` | The run's top spans, usually one root with everything nested under it. |
| `time` | `number` | Seconds into the run while it streams in. Spans that start later stay hidden, running ones reach this far. Leave it out once the run is over. |
| `axis` | `number` | Seconds the time axis covers. Defaults to the run's length, rounded up to a whole second. |
| `slowAfter` | `number` | A tool call longer than this many seconds turns amber and is tagged slow. Defaults to 2. |
| `status` | `string` | Overrides the status line. Defaults to "Running · 4 spans", then "Done · 7 spans, 1 slow". |
| `selected` | `string` | The id of the open span, whose details show under the waterfall. null closes them. |
| `onSelectedChange` / `selectedChange` | `callback` | Fires with the id of the span opened, or null when the details close. |

A `TraceSpan` has an `id`, a `name`, a `kind` (agent, llm, tool, or retrieval), a `start` and
`duration` in seconds, optional `tokens`, optional `input` and `output` strings, and optional
`children`. An agent span without its own token count adds up every span under it.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). In
Blueprint the bars square off and running bars switch from a sweeping sheen to a steady stripe. Each
kind keeps its colour from the chart palette; a slow bar is amber and hatched in every theme.


# Voice capture (/docs/components/voice-capture)

Speech to text that shows what it heard as it hears it, and lets the person fix the words it was
unsure of. Each word fades in as it arrives and the wave scrolls while it records. Press Done to
move from recording into review, where unsure words are highlighted — tap one to pick from a short
"Did you mean" menu — then Done again to send, or Cancel to drop it. Once recording stops the box
keeps its height: the wave freezes as the whole recording and the words stay where they were.

<Preview>
  <VoiceCaptureExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { VoiceCapture, type HeardWord } from './voice-capture/VoiceCapture';

const words: Array<string | HeardWord> = [
  'Move', 'the', 'yearly',
  { text: 'toggle', alternatives: ['toggle', 'toddle', 'tunnel'] },
  'above', 'the', 'cards',
];

<VoiceCapture
  words={words}
  level={() => analyser.level()}
  onSend={(text) => send(text)}
  onFix={(index, text) => console.log('fixed', index, text)}
  onRecordAgain={() => reset()}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [VoiceCaptureComponent] -->
words: Array<string | HeardWord> = [
  'Move', 'the', 'yearly',
  { text: 'toggle', alternatives: ['toggle', 'toddle', 'tunnel'] },
];

<VoiceCapture
  [words]="words"
  (send)="onSend($event)"
  (fixWord)="onFix($event)"
  (recordAgain)="reset()"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/voice_capture.dart';

VoiceCapture(
  words: const [
    'Move', 'the', 'yearly',
    HeardWord('toggle', alternatives: ['toggle', 'toddle', 'tunnel']),
  ],
  onSend: (text) => send(text),
  onFix: (index, text) => debugPrint('fixed $index $text'),
  onRecordAgain: () => reset(),
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `words` | `Array<string \| HeardWord>` | The words heard so far, in order. Add to the end as they arrive and each one fades in. |
| `state` | `listening \| paused \| review \| sent \| cancelled` | The state. Leave it out to let the buttons move it along. |
| `defaultState` | `VoiceCaptureState` | The state to start in when uncontrolled. Defaults to `listening`. |
| `onStateChange` | `(state) => void` | Called whenever the state moves. |
| `seconds` | `number` | Seconds recorded. Leave it out to let it count while listening. |
| `level` | `number \| (() => number)` | The input level from 0 to 1, drawn into the wave about 20 times a second. Pass a function to read the microphone on every sample. |
| `status` | `string` | The status line. Defaults to Listening, Paused, Check what I heard, Sent or Cancelled. |
| `onSend` | `(text) => void` | Called with the checked transcript when Done is pressed in review. |
| `onFix` | `(index, text) => void` | Called when the person picks one of a word's alternatives. |
| `onRecordAgain` | `() => void` | Called by Record again, once the capture is sent or cancelled. |
| `HeardWord.text` | `string` | The word as heard. |
| `HeardWord.alternatives` | `string[]` | What it might have been instead. Highlights the word and opens a "Did you mean" menu. |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The panel
sits on a surface; the recording dot uses the `--vo-bad` tone and pulses, unsure words are tinted
with `--vo-hl` (and `--vo-hl-ok` once fixed), and the wave is drawn from the `--vo-fg2`, `--vo-faint`
and `--vo-muted` tokens, so it reads in either theme. In Soft the panel and its buttons are rounder.


# Voice orb (/docs/components/voice-orb)

A hands-free voice chat on a card. The orb is a lit glass sphere that swells with whoever is
talking — the accent colour for you, violet for the agent — with what was said underneath and mute
and end below. It draws what you pass through `state`, `level` and `caption`; it never opens the
microphone itself. Talking while muted shows a notice, the way calls do.

<Preview>
  <VoiceOrbExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { VoiceOrb, type VoiceState } from './voice-orb/VoiceOrb';

const [state, setState] = useState<VoiceState>('idle');

<VoiceOrb
  state={state}
  level={level}            // 0..1, from your audio or a made-up curve
  muted={muted}
  onMutedChange={setMuted}
  mutedNotice
  caption={{ speaker: 'Agent', text: 'Yearly is now the default.', id: 't2' }}
  hint="Talk to the agent about Pricing v4"
  elapsed={seconds}
  onStart={start}
  onEnd={end}
  onRestart={start}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [VoiceOrbComponent] -->
<VoiceOrb
  [state]="state"
  [level]="level"
  [muted]="muted"
  (mutedChange)="muted = $event"
  [mutedNotice]="true"
  [caption]="caption"
  hint="Talk to the agent about Pricing v4"
  [elapsed]="seconds"
  (start)="start()"
  (end)="end()"
  (restart)="start()"
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/voice_orb.dart';

VoiceOrb(
  state: state,                       // VoiceState.idle, listening, thinking, speaking, ended
  level: level,                       // 0..1
  muted: muted,
  onMutedChange: (v) => setState(() => muted = v),
  mutedNotice: true,
  caption: const VoiceCaption(speaker: 'Agent', text: 'Yearly is now the default.', id: 't2'),
  hint: 'Talk to the agent about Pricing v4',
  elapsed: seconds,
  onStart: start,
  onEnd: end,
  onRestart: start,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `idle \| listening \| thinking \| speaking \| ended` | Where the chat is. `muted` while `listening` shows as Muted. |
| `level` | `number` | How loud whoever is talking is, 0 to 1. The orb swells with it. |
| `muted` | `boolean` | Your microphone is off; the mute button is pressed and Listening reads as Muted. |
| `onMutedChange` | `(muted) => void` | The mute button and the notice's Unmute call this. |
| `mutedNotice` | `boolean` | Shows "You're muted" with an Unmute button, for when someone talks while muted. |
| `caption` | `{ speaker; text; id? }` | What was said last and who said it. A new `id` (or speaker) starts a new line. |
| `hint` | `string` | Shown before anything is said, like "Talk to the agent about Pricing v4". |
| `elapsed` | `number` | Seconds since the chat started, shown top right. |
| `onStart` / `onEnd` | `() => void` | Start talking, and End. |
| `onRestart` | `() => void` | Start again, from the row shown once the chat has ended. |
| `endedDetail` | `string` | The quiet line under "Voice chat ended". Defaults to the length and "Transcript saved". |
| `labels` | `object` | Overrides for every bit of text (status words, buttons, notice). |

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). The orb's
colours flow from the tokens: the accent is yours, `--vo-pl` (violet) is the agent, and the two are
mixed in oklch so the step between them stays bright. The glass sphere is drawn on a canvas with
WebGL where it can, falling back to layered gradients otherwise; with reduced motion it holds a
single still frame and only redraws when the speaker changes.


# Web search (/docs/components/web-search)

Web search shows an agent researching out loud. Each query is a row with how many results came
back and how long it took; a query that finds nothing is asked again in other words. Under each
query sit the pages it opened, each marked Read, Skimmed, or Skipped with the reason (paywall,
blocked, timeout). Once the run is done the trail folds to one line and the answer streams in,
its bracketed numbers pointing back at the pages that back them up.

<Preview>
  <WebSearchExample />
</Preview>

## Usage [#usage]

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
import { WebSearch } from './web-search/WebSearch';

const queries = [
  { key: 'q1', query: 'stripe usage-based billing limits', status: 'done', results: 5, time: '0.9s',
    pages: [
      { title: 'Meters and billing thresholds', domain: 'stripe.com', date: 'Sep 2026', status: 'read', cite: 1 },
      { title: 'Why SaaS pricing is moving to usage', domain: 'ft.com', status: 'paywall' },
    ] },
];

<WebSearch
  queries={queries}
  done
  answer="Stripe caps metered usage at 100 million events a month [1]."
  bare={false}
/>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- imports: [WebSearchComponent] -->
queries: WebQuery[] = [
  { key: 'q1', query: 'stripe usage-based billing limits', status: 'done', results: 5, time: '0.9s',
    pages: [
      { title: 'Meters and billing thresholds', domain: 'stripe.com', date: 'Sep 2026', status: 'read', cite: 1 },
      { title: 'Why SaaS pricing is moving to usage', domain: 'ft.com', status: 'paywall' },
    ] },
];
```

```html
<WebSearch
  [queries]="queries"
  [done]="true"
  answer="Stripe caps metered usage at 100 million events a month [1]."
  [bare]="false"
  (openChange)="onOpen($event)"
></WebSearch>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'components/web_search.dart';

WebSearch(
  queries: const [
    WebQuery(
      key: 'q1',
      query: 'stripe usage-based billing limits',
      results: 5,
      time: '0.9s',
      pages: [
        WebPage(title: 'Meters and billing thresholds', domain: 'stripe.com', date: 'Sep 2026', status: WebPageStatus.read, cite: 1),
        WebPage(title: 'Why SaaS pricing is moving to usage', domain: 'ft.com', status: WebPageStatus.paywall),
      ],
    ),
  ],
  done: true,
  answer: 'Stripe caps metered usage at 100 million events a month [1].',
  bare: false,
),
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Properties [#properties]

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queries` | `WebQuery[]` | The searches, in order. Each has a key, the query text, a status, a result count, a time, an optional rewritten flag, and its pages. |
| `done` | `boolean` | True once searching and reading are over. The trail folds to its summary line. |
| `answer` | `string` | The answer, with sources cited as numbers in brackets. Each number points at the page with that cite value. |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the trail is open. Left out, it folds once `done` turns true. |
| `onOpenChange` / `openChange` | `callback` | Fires when the trail is opened or closed. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | Without the panel, for a chat stream. True by default. |

A `WebPage` has a `title`, a `domain`, an optional `date`, a `status` (reading, read, skimmed,
paywall, blocked, or timeout), and an optional `cite` number the answer refers to it by.

## Theming [#theming]

Works in light and dark (`data-theme="dark"`) and in the Soft style (`data-style="soft"`). Skipped
pages dim and their tag turns amber; a running page shows a spinner. The site initials stack on the
header, and hovering a citation lights the page that backs it up along with its site mark.


# FAQ (/docs/faq)

Short answers to the questions that come up most. If something isn't covered here,
open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/Visuno/issues/issues).

## General [#general]

<Accordions>

<Accordion title="What is Visuno?">
Visuno is an open-source UI component library for building **agent-powered products**.
Every component ships natively for **React**, **Angular**, and **Flutter**, built from one
shared set of design tokens — so a component looks and behaves the same wherever you use it.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Is it free to use?">
Yes. Visuno is open source under the **MIT licence** — free for personal and commercial
projects, with no attribution required. See the [components repository](https://github.com/Visuno/components)
for the full licence text.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Is Visuno production-ready?">
The React build is the reference implementation and is stable. Angular and Flutter are
native ports that mirror the same props and behaviour. As with any pre-1.0 library, pin a
version and read the [changelog](/docs/changelog) before upgrading.
</Accordion>

</Accordions>

## Frameworks [#frameworks]

<Accordions>

<Accordion title="Which frameworks are supported?">
Three, from a single design source:

| Framework | Form | Package |
|-----------|------|---------|
| **React** | `.tsx` components (React 18+) | `@visuno/react` |
| **Angular** | Standalone components (`vo-*` selectors, Angular 18+) | `@visuno/angular` |
| **Flutter** | Dart widgets, themed to match the web | `visuno` on pub.dev |

The React version is the reference; Angular and Flutter mirror the same props and behaviour.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Do all frameworks get every component?">
That's the goal — one design, three frameworks. React leads, and the Angular and Flutter
ports follow. Each component's docs page shows the code for every framework it currently
ships in, side by side.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Do I need a build step?">
React, Angular, and Flutter use their usual toolchains.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I use it with Next.js / Vite / other React setups?">
Yes. The React components are plain React 18+ components with no framework lock-in, so they
work in Next.js, Vite, Remix, or any React setup.
</Accordion>

</Accordions>

## Theming & styling [#theming--styling]

<Accordions>

<Accordion title="How does dark mode work?">
Set `data-theme="dark"` on a parent element (web), or use `Brightness.dark` in the Flutter
theme. Every component reads the same tokens, so your whole UI flips at once.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What are the two styles?">
The default **Blueprint** style is crisp and squared; **Soft** is rounded and plush. Switch
to Soft on the web with `data-style="soft"` on a parent element.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I customise colours, spacing, and radii?">
Yes. Design tokens drive everything — `--vo-*` custom properties on the web, and
`VoColors` / `VoSpace` / `VoRadius` in Flutter. Override a token once and the change flows
through every component.
</Accordion>

</Accordions>

## Using the components [#using-the-components]

<Accordions>

<Accordion title="How do I add a component to my project?">
Pick a component from the sidebar, copy the snippet for your framework, and drop it in.
Pull the shared core once (tokens + helpers), and every component you add after that just
works.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Are the components accessible?">
Components are built with semantic markup, keyboard support, and reduced-motion handling
where animation is involved. Accessibility notes specific to a component are called out on
its docs page.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How do I report a bug or request a component?">
Open an issue on the [issue tracker](https://github.com/Visuno/issues/issues). Planned
work and what's shipped are tracked on the [roadmap](/docs/roadmap) and
[changelog](/docs/changelog).
</Accordion>

</Accordions>


# Accessibility (/docs/getting-started/accessibility)

Agent interfaces move a lot: things stream in, states change, and panels open and close. Visuno
components are built so that motion and live updates don't lock anyone out. This page covers what the
library handles and what stays your responsibility.

## What the components do [#what-the-components-do]

<Accordions>

<Accordion title="Semantic markup">
Components use the right element for the job — real `<button>`s for actions, headings and lists where
they belong, and ARIA roles only where native semantics fall short. Interactive controls expose a
name, role, and state to assistive tech.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Keyboard support">
Anything you can click, you can reach and operate from the keyboard. Focus order follows reading
order, overlays (modals, popovers) trap focus while open and return it to the trigger on close, and
Escape dismisses transient surfaces.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Visible focus">
Every interactive element has a visible focus ring drawn from the `--vo-focus` token, so keyboard
users can always see where they are. The ring respects the active theme and style.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Reduced motion">
Components that animate — streaming status, shimmering states, fades between lines — honour
`prefers-reduced-motion`. When a viewer asks their OS for less motion, animations are shortened or
removed and content simply appears, with no loss of information.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Live regions">
Components that update on their own (status pills, toasts, live answers) announce changes through
ARIA live regions so screen-reader users hear what changed without having to go looking for it.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Color and contrast">
The default light and dark themes are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast for text and essential UI.
Meaning is never carried by color alone — states also use a glyph, label, or shape.
</Accordion>

</Accordions>

## What stays on you [#what-stays-on-you]

The library gives you accessible building blocks; the composition is yours. A few things to get
right in your app:

- **Labels and text alternatives** — give icon-only buttons an accessible name, and images and charts
  a meaningful description for the data they show.
- **Contrast of custom tokens** — if you override `--vo-*` colors (see [Theming](/docs/getting-started/theming)),
  re-check text and UI contrast against the new values.
- **Heading structure** — keep a sensible heading order on the page around the components.
- **Reading order** — place components in the DOM in the order you want them read and tabbed.

## Per-component notes [#per-component-notes]

Accessibility details specific to a component — which keys it responds to, what it announces, how it
behaves under reduced motion — are called out in the **Theming** and usage sections of that
component's docs page.

<Cards>
  <Card title="Theming" href="/docs/getting-started/theming" description="Tokens, dark mode, and the focus ring." />
  <Card title="FAQ" href="/docs/faq" description="More short answers, including accessibility." />
</Cards>


# Installation (/docs/getting-started/installation)

Visuno ships the same design across **React**, **Angular**, and **Flutter**. Whatever your stack, the
shape is the same: **install the package**, **pull the shared core once** (design tokens + a little
CSS/helpers), then add components one at a time. The React build is the reference; Angular and
Flutter mirror its props and behaviour.

## Prerequisites [#prerequisites]

| Framework | You need |
|-----------|----------|
| **React** | React 18+ and a bundler (Next.js, Vite, Remix — anything). |
| **Angular** | Angular 18+ with standalone components. |
| **Flutter** | Flutter 3+ (Dart 3). |

## Set up [#set-up]

Pick your framework. Each starts by installing the package, then pulling the shared core once.

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

The React components are plain React 18+ components with no framework lock-in, so they work in
Next.js, Vite, Remix, or any React setup.

<Steps>

<Step>

### Install the package [#install-the-package]

<Tabs items={['npm', 'pnpm', 'yarn', 'bun']}>

<Tab value="npm">

```bash
npm install @visuno/react
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="pnpm">

```bash
pnpm add @visuno/react
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="yarn">

```bash
yarn add @visuno/react
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="bun">

```bash
bun add @visuno/react
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step>

### Pull the core [#pull-the-core]

Import the shared tokens and base styles **once**, near the root of your app (e.g. in `layout.tsx`
or your global CSS entry):

```ts
import '@visuno/core/tokens.css';
```

</Step>

<Step>

### Add a component [#add-a-component]

Import the component and drop it in:

```tsx
import { StatusPill } from '@visuno/react/status-pill/StatusPill';

export function Row() {
  return <StatusPill state="working" label="Editing PricingCard.tsx" />;
}
```

</Step>

</Steps>

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

Components are **standalone** — import the one you need directly into your component's `imports`, no
module boilerplate.

<Steps>

<Step>

### Install the package [#install-the-package-1]

<Tabs items={['npm', 'pnpm', 'yarn', 'bun']}>

<Tab value="npm">

```bash
npm install @visuno/angular
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="pnpm">

```bash
pnpm add @visuno/angular
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="yarn">

```bash
yarn add @visuno/angular
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="bun">

```bash
bun add @visuno/angular
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step>

### Pull the core [#pull-the-core-1]

Add the token stylesheet to your global styles **once** (e.g. `styles.css`, or the `styles` array
in `angular.json`):

```css
@import '@visuno/core/tokens.css';
```

</Step>

<Step>

### Add a component [#add-a-component-1]

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { StatusPillComponent } from '@visuno/angular/status-pill';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-row',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [StatusPillComponent],
  template: `<StatusPill state="working" label="Editing PricingCard.tsx" />`,
})
export class RowComponent {}
```

</Step>

</Steps>

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

The Flutter widgets are themed to match the web. Wrap your app in the Visuno theme once, then use
the widgets anywhere.

<Steps>

<Step>

### Install the package [#install-the-package-2]

Add it from the command line:

```bash
flutter pub add visuno
```

Or add it to your `pubspec.yaml` and run `flutter pub get`:

```yaml
dependencies:
  visuno: ^0.1.0
```

</Step>

<Step>

### Apply the theme [#apply-the-theme]

Wrap your app **once** so every widget inherits the shared tokens:

```dart
import 'package:visuno/visuno.dart';

MaterialApp(
  theme: VisunoTheme.dark, // Brightness.dark to match the web's dark mode
  home: const Home(),
);
```

</Step>

<Step>

### Add a widget [#add-a-widget]

```dart
import 'package:visuno/visuno.dart';

const StatusPill(state: StatusPillState.working, label: 'Editing PricingCard.tsx');
```

</Step>

</Steps>

</Tab>

</Tabs>

Install the package and pull the core once, and every component you add after that just works — it
reads the same tokens and inherits your theme automatically.


# Theming (/docs/getting-started/theming)

Every Visuno component reads from one shared set of **design tokens**, so you theme the whole UI from
one place instead of styling components one by one. There are two switches everyone uses out of the
box — **dark mode** and **style** — and underneath them, the tokens you can override to make the
library your own.

## The two switches [#the-two-switches]

On the web (React and Angular) both switches are attributes on a parent element; on Flutter they live
in the theme object. Every component below the switch responds at once.

### Dark mode [#dark-mode]

Set dark mode once, high up, and the whole subtree flips.

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
// Put it on a parent — often <html> or the app root.
<html data-theme="dark">
  {/* every component inside is dark */}
</html>

// Remove the attribute, or use data-theme="light", for light.
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- Put it on a parent — often <html> or the app root. -->
<html data-theme="dark">
  <!-- every component inside is dark -->
</html>

<!-- Remove the attribute, or use data-theme="light", for light. -->
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
import 'package:visuno/visuno.dart';

// Brightness.dark matches the web's dark mode.
MaterialApp(
  theme: VisunoTheme.dark,   // or VisunoTheme.light
  home: const Home(),
);
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

### Style [#style]

Two styles, one design: **Blueprint** (default) is crisp and squared; **Soft** is rounded and plush.

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```tsx
// Switch to Soft with data-style on a parent. Combine it with data-theme freely.
<div data-theme="dark" data-style="soft">
  {/* dark + soft */}
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```html
<!-- Switch to Soft with data-style on a parent. Combine it with data-theme freely. -->
<div data-theme="dark" data-style="soft">
  <!-- dark + soft -->
</div>
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
// Pick the style on the theme; combine with either brightness.
MaterialApp(
  theme: VisunoTheme.dark.copyWith(style: VoStyle.soft),   // or VoStyle.blueprint
  home: const Home(),
);
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

You can combine the switches freely — light/dark × Blueprint/Soft is four looks from the same source.

## The token system [#the-token-system]

Tokens are the single source of truth for every color, space, radius, and motion value. Components
never hardcode these — they read tokens — so overriding a token flows through the whole library.

| Platform | Tokens look like | Where to set them |
|----------|------------------|-------------------|
| **Web** (React / Angular) | `--vo-*` CSS custom properties | On `:root`, or scoped to any parent |
| **Flutter** | `VoColors` / `VoSpace` / `VoRadius` | In the Visuno theme |

### Override a token [#override-a-token]

Change a token once and it flows to every component under it.

<Tabs items={['React', 'Angular', 'Flutter']}>

<Tab value="React">

```css
/* Set --vo-* custom properties on :root, or scope them to a subtree. */
:root {
  --vo-accent: #6d5efc;   /* brand accent */
  --vo-radius: 12px;      /* corner rounding */
  --vo-space: 0.25rem;    /* spacing step */
}

/* Scope an override to theme just part of a page. */
.promo {
  --vo-accent: #e5484d;
}
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Angular">

```css
/* Same mechanism as React — set --vo-* in your global styles or a component's styles. */
:root {
  --vo-accent: #6d5efc;   /* brand accent */
  --vo-radius: 12px;      /* corner rounding */
  --vo-space: 0.25rem;    /* spacing step */
}

/* Scope an override to a host or subtree. */
:host.promo {
  --vo-accent: #e5484d;
}
```

</Tab>

<Tab value="Flutter">

```dart
// Override values on the theme's token objects.
VisunoTheme.dark.copyWith(
  colors: VoColors.dark.copyWith(accent: const Color(0xFF6D5EFC)),
  radius: VoRadius.all(12),
);
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## How it fits together [#how-it-fits-together]

1. **Tokens** hold the raw values (color, space, radius, motion).
2. **The two switches** (`data-theme`, `data-style` on the web; the theme object on Flutter) select
   which set of token values is active.
3. **Components** read tokens only — so flip a switch or override a token, and every component
   updates in lockstep.

Change a token once and the change is everywhere — that is the whole point of the system.

<Cards>
  <Card title="Accessibility" href="/docs/getting-started/accessibility" description="Contrast, keyboard, focus, and reduced motion." />
  <Card title="Browse components" href="/docs/components/status-pill" description="Each page has a Theming note for that component." />
</Cards>


# Using with AI (/docs/getting-started/using-with-ai)

Visuno is built for agent products, and it works well **with** coding agents too. The docs ship in
machine-readable form so an assistant can pull exact component APIs, props, and token rules instead
of guessing. This page shows what's available and how to use it.

## Machine-readable docs [#machine-readable-docs]

Every docs page is available as plain text and Markdown, and the whole site is summarised in two
`llms.txt` files that follow the [llms.txt convention](https://llmstxt.org).

| URL | What it is |
|-----|------------|
| [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt) | An index of the docs — every page with its title and link, for an assistant to crawl. |
| [`/llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) | The entire documentation inlined as one text file, ready to paste into a context window. |
| `/llms.mdx/docs/<path>` | Any single page as raw Markdown (e.g. `/llms.mdx/docs/components/status-pill`). |

These are generated from the same source as the site, so they're always in sync with the live docs.

## Give an assistant the context [#give-an-assistant-the-context]

Pick whichever fits your tool:

- **Paste a page** — grab one component's Markdown from `/llms.mdx/docs/components/<name>` and paste
  it into the chat before you ask for code. The assistant then has the exact props and examples.
- **Point at the index** — give the assistant `/llms.txt` and let it fetch the pages it needs.
- **Drop in everything** — for a big task, paste `/llms-full.txt` so the whole library is in context.

## Prompting tips [#prompting-tips]

The library has a few hard rules; stating them up front keeps generated code correct and on-brand:

- **Reuse, don't reinvent.** Ask the assistant to compose the real components (`StatusPill`, `Button`,
  `Modal`, …) rather than hand-rolling markup. If a component exists, use it.
- **Tokens only — no literals.** Tell it that all color, spacing, radius, and motion come from the
  shared `--vo-*` tokens, and that hardcoded colors or pixel radii are a bug.
- **Name the framework.** Say React, Angular, or Flutter explicitly — the props match across all
  three, but the syntax differs.
- **Respect the two switches.** Output should work in light and dark (`data-theme`) and in both the
  Blueprint and Soft styles (`data-style`) without changes.

### A prompt that works [#a-prompt-that-works]

> You are building UI with the Visuno component library. Use only Visuno components (fetch their APIs
> from `/llms.txt`), style everything through the `--vo-*` design tokens — never hardcode colors,
> spacing, or radii — and make it work in dark mode and the Soft style. Target: **React**. Build a
> run-status row using `StatusPill`.

## Building agents with Visuno [#building-agents-with-visuno]

Because the components are designed for agent interfaces, they map cleanly onto the states an AI
product moves through — thinking, reading, working, waiting for review, streaming an answer, logging
actions. Browse the **Agent status** and **Conversation** groups in the sidebar for the building
blocks, and compose them into your own flows.

<Cards>
  <Card title="Browse components" href="/docs/components/status-pill" description="APIs and live examples for every component." />
  <Card title="llms.txt" href="/llms.txt" description="The machine-readable docs index." />
</Cards>

# Introduction (/docs)

**Visuno** is an open-source UI component library for building agent interfaces. Every component
ships natively for **React**, **Angular**, and **Flutter**, built from a single shared set of
design tokens — so a component looks and behaves the same wherever you use it.

Each component in these docs has a **live preview** you can toggle between light/dark and the two
styles, plus the code for all three frameworks side by side.

## Three frameworks, one design [#three-frameworks-one-design]

| Framework | Form | Package |
|-----------|------|---------|
| **React** | `.tsx` components (React 18+) | `@visuno/react` |
| **Angular** | Standalone components (`vo-*` selectors, Angular 18+) | `@visuno/angular` |
| **Flutter** | Dart widgets, themed to match the web | `visuno` on pub.dev |

The React version is the reference; Angular and Flutter are native ports that mirror the same props
and behavior.

## Theming [#theming]

Every component responds to the same two switches, so your whole UI changes at once:

- **Dark mode** — `data-theme="dark"` on a parent element (web); `Brightness.dark` in the Flutter
  theme.
- **Style** — the default **Blueprint** style, or **Soft** via `data-style="soft"` (web). Blueprint
  is crisp and squared; Soft is rounded and plush.

Design tokens (`--vo-*` on the web, `VoColors`/`VoSpace`/`VoRadius` in Flutter) drive every color,
space, radius, and motion — change a token once and it flows everywhere.

## Sections [#sections]

Components are grouped by what they do in an agent product:

- **Agent status** — show what the agent is doing: live status, thinking states, reasoning trails,
  action logs, run timelines, cost and context meters.
- **Charts and tables** — present data: stat cards and more.
- **Dates** — pick and switch: segmented controls and date tools.
- **Forms and inputs** — the basics: buttons, badges, progress, tooltips.

## Get started [#get-started]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Browse components" href="/docs/components/status-pill" description="Live previews and code for every component." />
  <Card title="Components on GitHub" href="https://github.com/Visuno/components" description="The source for all three frameworks." />
</Cards>

Pick a component from the sidebar, copy the snippet for your framework, and drop it in. Pull the
shared core once (tokens + helpers), and every component you add just works.


# Roadmap (/docs/roadmap)

Where Visuno is headed. This is a direction, not a dated commitment — priorities shift
with what people need. Have a request? Open an issue on
[GitHub](https://github.com/Visuno/issues/issues).

## Shipped [#shipped]

- **Agent status** components — status pill, thinking, thinking states, reasoning trail,
  agent phases, step loader, action log, context meter, and more.
- **Conversation** components — live answer, thread panel, composer, model picker, voice
  capture and orb, tool call, artifact card, and more.
- **Charts and tables**, **Dates**, and **Forms and inputs** — stat cards, segmented
  control, buttons, badge, progress, and tooltip.
- **Docs site** with live previews, light/dark and Blueprint/Soft toggles, and per-framework
  code for every component.

## In progress [#in-progress]

- **Full three-framework parity** — bringing every documented component to React, Angular,
  and Flutter.
- **Accessibility pass** — keyboard, focus, and reduced-motion coverage audited and
  documented per component.
- **Theming guide** — a dedicated page on the `--vo-*` token system and how to build a
  custom theme.

## Planned [#planned]

- **Installation & setup guide** — a first-class getting-started flow per framework.
- **Copy-paste recipes** — common agent-UI compositions built from several components.
- **Versioned releases** — semver-tagged packages with migration notes in the
  [changelog](/docs/changelog).
- **More components** — driven by what agent products actually need; suggestions welcome.

## Exploring [#exploring]

Ideas we're considering but haven't committed to. Feedback shapes what graduates to
_Planned_:

- A CLI to pull components and tokens into a project.
- Design-tool assets (Figma kit) matched to the shipped components.

---

Nothing here is a promise of a date. The [changelog](/docs/changelog) records what has
actually shipped; this page records intent.
